metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: No, it's just intuitively I can see that life becomes easier

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: at the lower end if it's increased.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It becomes less and less, it is an empirical scientific question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: but it becomes less and less obvious to me

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that more intelligence is better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: At the high end, not because it would make life easier,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: but it would make whatever problems you're working on more solvable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And if you are working on artificial intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: there is a tremendous potential for that to improve society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I understand. So at whatever problems you're working on, yes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: but there's also the problem of the human condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There's love, there's fear, and all those beautiful things

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that sometimes if you're good at solving problems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: you're going to create more problems for yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I'm not exactly sure. So ignorance is bliss is a thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So there might be a sweet spot of intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: given your environment, given your personality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: all of those kinds of things, and that becomes less beautifully complicated

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: the more and more intelligent you become.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But that's a question for literature, not for science perhaps.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Well, imagine this. Imagine there was an IQ pill,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: and it was developed by a private company, and they are willing to sell it to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And whatever price they put on it, you are willing to pay it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: because you would like to be smarter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But just before they give you a pill, they give you a disclaimer for them to sign.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Don't hold us... You understand that this pill has no guarantee

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that your life is going to be better, and in fact it could be worse.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Well, yes, that's how lawyers work, but I would love for science to answer the question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: to try to predict if your life is going to be better or worse

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: when you become more or less intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's a fascinating question about what is the sweet spot for the human condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Some of the things we see as bugs might be actually features,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: may be crucial to our overall happiness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: is our limitations might lead to more happiness than less.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But again, more intelligence is better at the lower end.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's something that's less arguable and fascinating if possible to increase.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But you know there's virtually no research that's based on a neuroscience approach

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: to solving that problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: All the solutions that have been proposed to solve that problem

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: or to ameliorate that problem are essentially based on the blank slate assumption

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that enriching the environment, removing barriers, all good things by the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I'm not against any of those things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But there's no empirical evidence that they're going to improve the general reasoning ability

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: or make people more employable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Have you read Flowers of Algernon?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's to the question of intelligence and happiness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There are many profound aspects of that story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It was a film that was very good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The film was called Charlie for the younger people who are listening to this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You might be able to stream it on Netflix or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But it was a story about a person with very low IQ who underwent a surgical procedure in the brain

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: and he slowly became a genius.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And the tragedy of the story is the effect was temporary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's a fascinating story really.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That goes in contrast to the basic human experience that each of us individually have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But it raises the question of the full range of people you might be able to be,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: given different levels of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You've mentioned the normal distribution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So let's talk about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There's a book called The Bell Curve written in 1994,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: written by psychologist Richard Herrnstein and political scientist Charles Murray.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Why was this book so controversial?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This is a fascinating book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I know Charles Murray.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I've had many conversations with him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: What is the book about?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The book is about the importance of intelligence in everyday life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's what the book is about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's an empirical book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It has statistical analyses of very large databases that show that essentially IQ scores

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: or their equivalent are correlated to all kinds of social problems and social benefits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And that in itself is not where the controversy about that book came.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The controversy was about one chapter in that book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And that is a chapter about the average difference in mean scores between black Americans and white Americans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And these are the terms that were used in the book at the time and are still used to some extent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And historically, or really for decades, it has been observed that disadvantaged groups score on average lower than Caucasians

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: on academic tests, tests of mental ability, and especially on IQ tests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And the difference is about a standard deviation, which is about 15 points, which is a substantial difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: In the book, Harnstein and Murray in this one chapter assert clearly and unambiguously

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that whether this average difference is due to genetics or not, they are agnostic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They don't know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Moreover, they assert they don't care because you wouldn't treat anybody differently knowing

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: if there was a genetic component or not, because that's a group average finding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Every individual has to be treated as an individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You can't make any assumption about what that person's intellectual ability might be

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: from the fact of an average group difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They're very clear about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Nonetheless, people took away, I'm going to choose my words carefully because I have a feeling

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that many critics didn't actually read the book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They took away that Harnstein and Murray were saying that blacks are genetically inferior.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That was the take-home message.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And if they weren't saying it, they were implying it because they had a chapter

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that discussed this empirical observation of a difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And isn't this horrible?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And so the reaction to that book was incendiary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: What do we know about from that book and the research beyond about race differences and intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's still the most incendiary topic in psychology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Nothing has changed that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Anybody who even discusses it is easily called a racist just for discussing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's become fashionable to find racism in any discussion like this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's unfortunate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The short answer to your question is there's been very little actual research on this topic since the Belker of even before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This really became incendiary in 1969 with an article published by an educational psychologist named Arthur Jensen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Let's just take a minute and go back to that to see the bell curve in a little bit more historical perspective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Arthur Jensen was an educational psychologist at UC Berkeley.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I knew him as well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And in 1969 or 68, the Harvard Educational Review asked him to do a review article on the early childhood education programs

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that were designed to raise the IQs of minority students.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This was before the federally funded Head Start program.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Head Start had not really gotten underway at the time Jensen undertook his review of what were a number of demonstration programs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: These demonstration programs were for young children around kindergarten age.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They were specially designed to be cognitively stimulating, to provide lunches,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: do all the things that people thought would minimize this average gap of intelligence tests.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There was a strong belief among virtually all psychologists that the cause of the gap was unequal opportunity due to racism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: all negative things in the society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And if you could compensate for this, the gap would go away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So early childhood education back then was called literally compensatory education.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Jensen looked at these programs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He was an empirical guy. He understood psychometrics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And he wrote a, it was over a hundred page article detailing these programs and the flaws in their research design.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Some of the programs reported IQ gains of on average five points,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: but a few reported 10, 20, and even 30 point gains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: One was called the miracle in Milwaukee.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That investigator went to jail ultimately for fabricating data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But the point is that Jensen wrote an article that said, look, the opening sentence of his article is classic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The opening sentence is, I may not quote it exactly right, but it's, we have tried compensatory education and it has failed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And he showed that these gains were essentially nothing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You couldn't really document empirically any gains at all from these really earnest efforts to increase IQ.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But he went a step further, a fateful step further.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He said, not only have these efforts failed, but because they have had essentially no impact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: we have to re-examine our assumption that these differences are caused by environmental things that we can address with education.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: We need to consider a genetic influence, whether there's a genetic influence on this group difference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So you said that this is one of the more controversial works ever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I think it's the most infamous paper in all of psychology, I would go on to say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Because in 1969, the genetic data was very skimpy on this question, skimpy and controversial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's always been controversial, but it was even skimpy and controversial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's kind of a long story that I go into a little bit in more detail in the book, Neuroscience of Intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But to say he was vilified is an understatement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I mean, he couldn't talk at the American Psychological Association without bomb threats clearing the lecture hall.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Campus security watched him all the time. They opened his mail.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He had to retreat to a different address.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This was one of the earliest kinds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This is before the internet and kind of internet social media mobs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But it was that intense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I have written that overnight after the publication of this article, all intelligence research became radioactive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Nobody wanted to talk about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And then it didn't, nobody was doing more research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And then the bell curve came along.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And the Jensen controversy was dying down.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I have stories that Jensen told me about his interaction with the Nixon White House on this issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I mean, this was like a really big deal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It was some unbelievable stories, but he told me this, so I kind of believe these stories.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But nonetheless, 25 years later, 25 years later, all the silence basically saying, you know, this nobody wants to do this kind of research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There's so much pressure, so much attack against this kind of research.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And here's a sort of a bold, stupid, crazy people that decided to dive right back in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I wonder how much discussion that was.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Did they want to include this chapter or not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Murray has said they discussed it and they felt they should include it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And they were very careful in the way they wrote it, which did them no good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So as a matter of fact, when the bell curve came out, it was so controversial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I got a call from a television show called Nightline, it was with a broadcaster called Ted Koppel, who had this evening show, I think it was on late at night, talked about news.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It was a straight up news thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And producer called and asked if I would be on it to talk about the bell curve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I said, you know, she asked me what I thought about the bell curve as a book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I said, look, it's a very good book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It talks about the role of intelligence in society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And she said, no, no, what do you think about the chapter on race?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's what we want you to talk about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I remember this conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I said, well, she said, what would you say if you were on TV?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I said, well, what I would say is that it's not at all clear if there's any genetic component to intelligence, any differences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But if there were a strong genetic component, that would be a good thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And, you know, complete silence on the other end of the phone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And she said, well, what do you mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I said, well, if it's the more genetic any differences, the more it's biological.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And if it's biological, we can figure out how to fix it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I see. That's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: She said, would you say that on television?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I said, no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And so that was the end of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I think that the chapter on more like biology is within the reach of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And the environment is a public policy, social and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: From your perspective, whichever one you think is more amenable to solutions in the short term is the one that excites you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But you saying that is good.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The truth of genetic differences, no matter what, between groups is a painful, harmful, potentially dangerous thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Let me ask you to this question, whether it's bell curve or any research on race differences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Can that be used to increase the amount of racism in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Can that be used to increase the amount of hate in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Do you think about this kind of stuff?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I've thought about this a lot, not as a scientist, but as a person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And my sense is there is such enormous reservoirs of hate and racism that have nothing to do with scientific knowledge of the data, that speak against that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: No, I don't want to give racist groups a veto power over what scientists study.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: If you think that the differences, and by the way, virtually no one disagrees that there are differences in scores.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's all about what causes them and how to fix it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So if you think this is a cultural problem, then you must ask the problem, do you want to change anything about the culture?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Or are you okay with the culture because you don't feel it's appropriate to change a person's culture?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Are you okay with that and the fact that that may lead to disadvantages in school achievement?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's a question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: If you think it's environmental, what are the environmental parameters that can be fixed?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I'll tell you one, lead from gasoline in the atmosphere, lead in paint, lead in water.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's an environmental toxin that society has the means to eliminate and they should.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yeah, just to sort of try and define some insights and conclusion to this very difficult topic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Is there been research on environment versus genetics, nature versus nurture on this question of race differences?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There is not, no one wants to do this research. First of all, it's hard research to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Second of all, it's a minefield. No one wants to spend their career on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Tenured people don't want to do it, let alone students.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The way I talk about it, well, before I tell you the way I talk about it, I want to say one more thing about Jensen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He was once asked by a journalist straight out, are you a racist?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: His answer was very interesting. His answer was, I've thought about that a lot and I've concluded it doesn't matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now I know what he meant by this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The guts to say that, wow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He was a very unusual person. I think he had a touch of Asperger's syndrome to tell you the truth because I saw him in many circumstances.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He would be canceled on Twitter immediately with that sentence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yeah, but what he meant was he had a hypothesis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And with respect to group differences, he called it the default hypothesis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He said whatever factors affect individual intelligence are likely the same factors that affect group differences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It was the default, but it was a hypothesis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It should be tested. And if it turned out empirical tests didn't support the hypothesis, he was happy to move on to something else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He was absolutely committed to that scientific ideal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That it's an empirical question. We should look at it and let's see what happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The scientific method cannot be racist from his perspective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It doesn't matter what the scientists, if they follow the scientific method, it doesn't matter what they believe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And if they are biased and they consciously or unconsciously bias the data, other people will come along to replicate it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They will fail and the process over time will work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So let me push back on this idea because psychology to me is full of gray areas.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And what I've observed about psychology, even replication crisis aside, is that something about the media, something about journalism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: something about the virality of ideas in the public sphere, they misinterpret.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They take up things from studies willfully or from ignorance, misinterpret findings and tell narratives around that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I personally believe for me, I'm not saying that broadly about science, but for me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: it's my responsibility to anticipate the ways in which findings will be misinterpreted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So I've had, I thought about this a lot because I published papers on semi-autonomous vehicles and those, you know, cars, people dying cars.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There's people that have written me letters saying emails, nobody writes letters, I wish they did, that have blood in my hands

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: because of things that I would say positive or negative, there's consequences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: In the same way, when you're a researcher of intelligence, I'm sure you might get emails or at least people might believe that

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: finding your study is going to be used by a large number of people to increase the amount of hate in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I think there's some responsibility on scientists, but for me, I think there's a great responsibility

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: to anticipate the ways things will be misinterpreted and there you have to, first of all, decide whether you want to say a thing at all,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: do the study at all, publish the study at all, and to the words with which you explain it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I find this on Twitter a lot actually, which is when I write a tweet, and I'm usually just doing so innocently,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I'll write it, you know, it takes me like five seconds to write it or whatever, 30 seconds to write it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: and then I'll think, all right, I like close my eyes open and try to see how will the world interpret this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: like what are the ways in which this will be misinterpreted?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I'll sometimes adjust that tweet to see like, yeah, so in my mind it's clear, but that's because it's my mind from which this tweet came,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: but you have to think in a fresh mind that sees this and it's spread across a large number of other minds,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: how will the interpretation morph? I mean, for a tweet, it's a silly thing, it doesn't matter,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: but for a scientific paper and study and finding, I think it matters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So I don't know what your thoughts are about that, because maybe for Jensen, the data is there, what do you want me to do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This is a scientific process has been carried out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: If you think the data was polluted by bias, do other studies that reveal the bias, but the data is there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I'm not a poet, I'm not a literary writer, like what do you want me to do? I'm just presenting you the data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: What do you think on that spectrum? What's the role of a scientist?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The reason I do podcasts, the reason I write books for the public is to explain what I think the data mean and what I think the data don't mean.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I don't do very much on Twitter other than to retweet references to papers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I don't think it's my role to explain these because they're complicated, they're nuanced.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But when you decide not to do a scientific study or not to publish a result because you're afraid the result could be harmful or insensitive,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that's not an unreasonable thought. And people will make different conclusions and decisions about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I wrote about this, I'm the editor of a journal called Intelligence, which publishes scientific papers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Sometimes we publish papers on group differences. Those papers sometimes are controversial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: These papers are written for a scientific audience, they're not written for the Twitter audience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I don't promote them very much on Twitter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But in a scientific paper, you have to now choose your words carefully also because those papers are picked up by non-scientists, by writers of various kinds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And you have to be available to discuss what you're saying and what you're not saying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Sometimes you are successful at having a good conversation like we are today that doesn't start out pejorative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Other times I've been asked to participate in debates where my role would be to justify race science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Well, you can see you start out, that was a BBC request that I received.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I have so much, it's a love-hate relationship, mostly hate with these shallow journalism organizations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So they would want to use you as a kind of in a debate setting to communicate as to like there is race differences between groups and make that into debate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And put you in a role of justifying racism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Justifying racism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's what they're asking me to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Courses like educating about this field of the science of intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I want to say one more thing before we get off the normal distribution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You also asked me what is the science after the bell curve?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And the short answer is there's not much new work, but whatever work there is supports the idea that there still are group differences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's arguable whether those differences have diminished at all or not.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And there is still a major problem in underperformance for school achievement for many disadvantaged and minority students.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And there so far is no way to fix it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: What do we do with this information?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: What is this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Is this now a task?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now we'll talk about the future on the neuroscience and the biology side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But in terms of this information as a society in the public policy, in the political space, in the social space, what do we do with this information?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I've thought a lot about this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The first step is to have people interested in policy understand what the data actually show to pay attention to intelligence data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You can read policy papers about education and using your word processor, you can search for the word intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You can search a 20,000 word document in a second and find out the word intelligence does not appear anywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: In most discussions about what to do about achievement gaps, I'm not talking about test gaps, I'm talking about actual achievement gaps in schools, which everyone agrees is a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The word intelligence doesn't appear among educators.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: As a matter of fact, in California, there has been tremendous controversy about recent attempts to revise the curriculum for math in high schools.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: We had a Stanford professor of education who was running this review assert there's no such thing as a mathematical talent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: She wanted to get rid of the advanced classes in math because not everyone could do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now, of course, this has been very controversial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They've retreated somewhat, but the idea that a university professor was in charge of this who believes that there's no talent, that it doesn't exist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: this is rather shocking, let alone the complete absence of intelligence data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: By the way, let me tell you something about what the intelligence data show.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Let's take race out of it, even though the origins of these studies were a long time ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I'm blocking on the name of the report.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The Coleman Report was a famous report about education.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They measured all kinds of variables about schools, about teachers, and they looked at academic achievement as an outcome.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They found the most predictive variables of education outcome were the variables the student brought with him or her into the school,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: essentially their ability, and that when you combine the school and the teacher variables together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: the quality of the school, the funding of the school, the quality of the teachers, their education,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: you put all the teacher and school variables together, it barely accounted for 10% of the variance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And this has been replicated now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You know who you can ask?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302
