metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And that seems to me that's at the core here, that facing some kind of truth that's not able to be changed makes it difficult to sort of...

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Is limiting as opposed to empowering.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's the concern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: If you sort of test for intelligence and lay the data out, it feels like you will give up on certain people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You will sort of start bidding people as like, well, this person is like, let's focus on the average people or let's focus on the very intelligent people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's the concern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And there's a kind of intuition that if we just don't measure and we don't use that data, that we would treat everybody equal and give everybody equal opportunity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: If we have the data in front of us, we're likely to misdistribute the amount of sort of attention we allocate, resources we allocate to people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's probably the concern.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's a realistic concern, but I think it's a misplaced concern if you want to fix the problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: If you want to fix the problem, you have to know what the problem is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now, let me tell you this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Let's go back to the bell curve, not the bell curve, but the normal distribution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: 16% of the population on average has an IQ under 85, which means they're very hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: If you have an IQ under 85, it's very hard to find gainful employment at a salary that sustains you at least minimally in modern life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: OK, not impossible, but it's very difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: 16% of the population of the United States is about 51 or 52 million people with IQs under 85.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This is not a small issue.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: 14 million children have IQs under 85.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Is this something we want to ignore?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: What is the Venn diagram between when you have people with IQs under 85 and you have achievement in school or achievement in life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There's a lot of overlap there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This is why, to go back to the IQ pill, if there were a way to shift that curve toward the higher end, that would have a big impact.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: If I could maybe, before we talk about the impact on life and so on, some of the criticisms of the bell curve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So Stephen Jay Gould wrote that the bell curve rests on four incorrect assumptions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It would be just interesting to get your thoughts on the four assumptions, which are intelligence must be reducible to a single number,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: intelligence must be capable of rank-ordering people in a linear order, intelligence must be primarily genetically based, and intelligence must be essentially immutable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Maybe not as criticisms, but as thoughts about intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: We could spend a lot of time on him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Oh, Stephen Jay Gould?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He wrote that in what, about 1985, 1984?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: His views were overtly political, not scientific.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He was a scientist, but his views on this were overtly political.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I would encourage people listening to this, if they really want to understand his criticisms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: they should just Google what he had to say and Google the scientific reviews of his book, The Mismeasure of Man,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: and they will take these statements apart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They were wrong. Not only were they wrong, but when he asserted in his first book that there was no biological basis, essentially, to IQ,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: by the time the second edition came around, there were studies of MRIs showing that brain size, brain volume, were correlated to IQ scores, which he declined to put in his book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So, I'm learning a lot today. I didn't know actually the extent of his work. I was just using a few little snippets of criticism. That's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So, there's a battle here. He wrote a book, Mismeasure of Man, that's missing a lot of the scientific grounding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: His book is highly popular in colleges today. You can find it in any college bookstore under assigned reading.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's highly popular.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The Mismeasure of Man?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yes, highly influential.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Can you speak to the Mismeasure of Man? I'm undereducated about this. So, is this the book basically criticizing the ideas in the book?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yeah, where those four things came from. And it is really a book that was really taken apart point by point by a number of people who actually understood the data. And he didn't care. He didn't modify anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's a politically... Listen, because this is such a sensitive topic, like I said, I believe the impact of the work, as it is misinterpreted, has to be considered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Because it's not just going to be scientific discourse, it's going to be political discourse, there's going to be debates, there's going to be politically motivated people that will use messages in each direction, make something like the bell curve the enemy, or the support for one's racist beliefs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And so, I think you have to consider that. But it's difficult because Nietzsche was used by Hitler to justify a lot of his beliefs. And it's not exactly on Nietzsche to anticipate Hitler or how his ideas will be misinterpreted and used for evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But there is a balance there. So, I understand. This is really interesting. I didn't know. Is there any criticism of the book you find compelling or interesting or challenging to you from a scientific perspective?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There were factual criticisms about the nature of the statistics that were used, the statistical analyses. These were more technical criticisms. And they were addressed by Murray in a couple of articles where he took all the criticisms and spoke to them. And people listening to this podcast can certainly find all those online.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's very interesting. But Murray went on to write some additional books, two in the last couple of years. One about human diversity, where he goes through the data refuting the idea that race is only a social construct with no biological meaning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He discusses the data. It's a very good discussion. You don't have to agree with it. But he presents data in a cogent way. And he talks about the critics of that. And he talks about their data in a cogent, not personal way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's a very informative discussion. The book is called Human Diversity. He talks about race and he talks about gender. Same thing. About sex differences. And more recently, he's written what might be his final say on this, a book called Facing Reality, where he talks about this again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So, you know, he can certainly defend himself. He doesn't need me to do that. But I would urge people who have heard about him and the bell curve and who think they know what's in it, you are likely incorrect and you need to read it for yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But it is scientifically, it's a serious subject. It's a difficult subject. Ethically, it's a difficult subject. Everything you said here calmly and thoughtfully is difficult. It's difficult for me to even consider that G-factor exists.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I don't mean from like that somehow G-factor is inherently racist or sexist or whatever. It's just, it's difficult in the way that considering the fact that we die one day is difficult. That we are limited by our biology is difficult.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And it's, at least from an American perspective, you like to believe that everything is possible in this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Well, that leads us to what I think we should do with this information.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And what I think we should do with this information is unusual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Because I think what we need to do is fund more neuroscience research on the molecular biology of learning and memory. Because one definition of intelligence is based on how much you can learn and how much you can remember.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And if you accept that definition of intelligence, then there are molecular studies going on now. And Nobel Prizes being won on molecular biology or molecular neurobiology of learning and memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now, the step those researchers, those scientists need to take when it comes to intelligence is to focus on the concept of individual differences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Intelligence research has individual differences as its heart because it assumes that people differ on this variable and those differences are meaningful and need understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Cognitive psychologists who have morphed into molecular biologists studying learning and memory hate the concept of individual differences historically.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Some now are coming around to it. I once sat next to a Nobel Prize winner for his work on memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I asked him about individual differences and he said, don't go there. It'll set us back 50 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But I said, don't you think they're the key though to understand why can some people remember more than others? He said, you don't want to go there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I think the 21st century will be remembered by the technology and the science that goes to individual differences because we have now data. We have now the tools, the much, much better to start to measure, start to estimate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Not just on the sort of through tests and IQ test type of things, sort of outside the body kind of things, but measuring all kinds of stuff about the body. So you had to truly go into the molecular biology, to the neurobiology, to the neuroscience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Let me ask you about the life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: How does intelligence correlate with or lead to or has anything to do with career success? You've mentioned these kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Is there any data? You had an excellent conversation with Jordan Peterson, for example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Is there any data on what intelligent means for success in life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Success in life. There is a tremendous amount of validity data that looked at intelligence test scores and various measures of life success.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now, of course, life success is a pretty broad topic and not everybody agrees on what success means, but there's general agreement on certain aspects of success that can be measured.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Including life expectancy, like you said.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Life expectancy. Now, there's life success. Life expectancy. I mean, that is such an interesting finding, but IQ scores are also correlated to things like income.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now, okay, so who thinks income means you're successful? That's not the point. The point is that income is one empirical measure in this culture that says something about your level of success.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You can define success in ways that have nothing to do with income. You can define success based on your evolutionary natural selection success.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But for variables, and even that, by the way, is correlated to IQ in some studies. So however you want to define success, IQ is important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's not the only determinant. People get hung up on, well, what about personality? What about so-called emotional intelligence?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yes, all those things matter. The thing that matters empirically, the single thing that matters the most is your general ability, your general mental intellectual ability, your reasoning ability.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And the more complex your vocation, the more complex your job, the more G matters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: G doesn't matter, and a lot of occupations don't require complex thinking. And there are occupations like that, and G doesn't matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Within an occupation, the G might not matter so much. So that if you look at all the professors at MIT and had a way to rank order them on, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: there's a ceiling effect is what I'm saying.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Also, when you get past a certain threshold, then there's impact on wealth, for example, or career success, however that's defined in each individual discipline.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But after a certain point, it doesn't matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Actually, it does matter in certain things. So, for example, there is a very classic study that was started at Johns Hopkins when I was a graduate student there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I actually worked on this study at the very beginning, the study of mathematically and scientifically precocious youth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And they gave junior high school students, age 11 and 12, the standard SAT math exam.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And they found a very large number of students scored very high on this exam.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Not a large number. I mean, they found many students when they cast the net, they're all of Baltimore.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They found a number of students who scored as high on the SAT math when they were 12 years old as incoming Hopkins freshmen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And they said, gee, now this is interesting. What shall we do now?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And on a case by case basis, they got some of those kids into their local community college math programs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Many of those kids went on to be very successful. And now there's a 50 year follow up of those kids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And it turns out, these kids were in the top 1%.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So everybody in this study is in the top 1%. If you take that group, that rarefied group and divide them into quartiles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: so you have the top 25% of the top 1% and the bottom 25% of the top 1%, you can find unmeasurable variables of success.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The top quartile does better than the bottom quartile in the top 1%. They have more patents, they have more publications,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: they have more tenure at universities. And this is based on their, you're dividing them based on their score at age 12.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I wonder how much interesting data is in the variability in the differences.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So, but that's really, oh boy, that's very interesting, but it's also, I don't know, somehow painful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I don't know why it's so painful that that's so, that G-factor so determinant of even in the nuanced top percent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Well, this is interesting that you find that painful. Do you find it painful that people with charisma are very successful,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: can be very successful in life, even though having no other attributes other than they're famous and people like them?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Do you find that painful? Yes, if that charisma is untrainable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So one of the things, again, this is like I learned psychology from the Johnny Depp trial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But one of the things the psychologist, the personality psychologist, he can maybe speak to this because he had interest in this for time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: is she was saying that personality, technically speaking, is the thing that doesn't change over a lifetime.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: One question about the Flynn effect. What is it? Are humans getting smarter over the years, over the decades, over the centuries?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The Flynn effect is James Flynn passed away about a year ago, published a set of analyses going back a couple of decades.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: When we first noticed this, that IQ scores when you looked over the years seemed to be drifting up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now this was not unknown to the people who make the test because they re-norm the test periodically

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: and they have to re-norm the test periodically because what 10 items correct meant relative to other people 50 years ago

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: is not the same as what 10 items mean relative today. People are getting more things correct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now the IQ scores have been drifting up about three points per decade.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This is not a personal effect. This is a cohort effect. It's not for an individual.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The world. So what's that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This has presented intelligence researchers with a great mystery. Two questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: First, is it effect on the 50% of the variance that's the G factor or on the other 50%?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There's evidence that it is a G factor effect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Second, what on earth causes this and doesn't this mean intelligence and G factor cannot be genetic

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: because the scale of natural selection is much, much longer than a couple of decades ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And so it's been used to try to undermine the idea that there can be a genetic influence on intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But certainly it can be the Flynn effect can affect the non-genetic aspects of intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: because genes account for maybe 50% of the variance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Maybe higher. It could be as high as 80% for adults, but let's just say 50% for discussion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So the Flynn effect, it's still a mystery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's still a mystery. That's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's still a mystery, although the evidence is coming out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I told you before I edited a journal on intelligence and we're doing a special issue in honor of James Flynn.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So I'm starting to see papers now on really the latest research on this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I think most people who specialize in this area of trying to understand the Flynn effect are coming to the view based on data

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that it has to do with advances in nutrition and healthcare.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And there's also evidence that the effect is slowing down and possibly reversing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Oh boy. So how would nutrition, so the nutrition would still be connected to the G factor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yes. And it's a good question because I think everyone should always be asked what evidence would change your mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's certainly not only a fair question, it is really the key question for anybody working on any aspect of science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I think that if environment was very important, we would have seen it clearly by now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It would have been obvious that school interventions, compensatory education, early childhood education, all these things that have been earnestly tried and well-funded, well-designed studies would show some effect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And they don't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They don't. What if the school, the way we've tried school, compensatory school sucks?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's what everybody said to Jensen. He said, well, maybe we need to start earlier.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Maybe we need not do pre-kindergarten but pre-pre-kindergarten.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's always an infinite, well, maybe we didn't get it right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But after decades of trying, 50 years, 50 or 60 years of trying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: surely something would have worked to the point where you could actually see a result and not need a probability level at 0.05 on some means.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So that's the kind of evidence that would change my mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Population level interventions like schooling that you would see, like this actually has an effect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yes. And when you take adopted kids and they grow up in another family and you find out when those adopted kids are adults, their IQ scores don't correlate with the IQ scores of their adoptive parents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But they do correlate with their IQ scores of their biological parents whom they've never met.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I mean, these are important. These are powerful observations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And it would be convincing to you if the reverse was true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yes, that would be more. And there is some data on adoption that indicates that the adopted children are moving a little bit more toward their adoptive parents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But to me, the overwhelming, I have this concept called the weight of evidence where I don't interpret any one study too much.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The weight of evidence tells me genes are important. But what does that mean?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: What does it mean that genes are important knowing that gene expression, genes don't express themselves in a vacuum.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They express themselves in an environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So the environment has to have something to do with it, especially if the best genetic estimates of the amount of variance are around 50 or even if it's as high as 80 percent, it still leaves 20 percent of non genetic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now, maybe that is all luck. Maybe that's all chance. I could believe that. I could easily believe that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So, but I do think after 50 years of trying various interventions and nothing works, including memory training, including listening to Mozart, including playing computer games, none of that has shown any impact on intelligence test scores.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Is there data on the intelligence, the IQ of parents as it relates to the children?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yes. And there is some evidence, genetic evidence of kind of an interaction between the parents IQ and the environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: High IQ parents provide an enriched environment, which then can impact the child in addition to the genes. It's that environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So there are all these interactions that, you know, but it's not, you know, think about the number of books in a household.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This was a variable that's correlated with IQ and it is. Yeah. Well, what? Well, why?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Especially if the kid never reads any of the books, it's because more intelligent people have more books in their house.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And if you're more intelligent and there's a genetic component to that, the child will get those genes or some of those genes as well as the environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But it's not the number of books in the house that actually directly impacts the child.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So the two scenarios on this are you find that this was used to get rid of the SAT test. Oh, the SAT scores highly correlated with the social economic status of the parents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So all you're really measuring is how rich the parents are. OK. Well, why are the parents rich? Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And so you could the opposite kind of syllogism is that people who are very bright make more money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: They can afford homes in better neighborhoods so their kids get better schools. Now the kids grow up bright.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Where in that chain of events does that come from? Well, unless you have a genetically informative research design where you look at siblings that have the same biological parents and so on, you can't really disentangle all that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Most studies of social economic status and intelligence do not have a genetically informed design. So any conclusions they make about the causality of the social economic status being the cause of the IQ is a stretch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And where you do find genetically informative designs, you find most of the variance in your outcome measures are due to the genetic component.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And sometimes the SES adds a little. But the weight of evidence is it doesn't add very much variance to predict what's going on beyond the genetic variance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So when you actually look at it in some and there aren't that many studies that have genetically informed designs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But when you do see those, the genes seem to have an advantage. Sorry for the strange questions, but there's is there a connection between.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Fertility or the number of kids that you have and G factor. So, you know, the kind of conventional wisdom is people of maybe is that higher economic status or something like that or having fewer children.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I just loosely hear these kinds of things. Is there is there data that you're aware of in one direction or another on this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Well, strange questions always get strange answers. Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So you have a strange answer for that strange. The answer is there used to there were some studies that indicated the more children in a family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The the first born children would be more intelligent than the fourth or fifth or sixth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's not clear that those studies hold up over time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And of course, what you see also is that families where there are multiple children, four, five, six, seven, you know, really big families.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The social economic status of those families usually in the modern age is not that high.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Maybe it used to be the aristocracy used to have a lot of kids. I'm not sure exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But there there there have been reports of correlations between IQ and fertility.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But I'm not sure that the data are very strong, that the first born child is always the smartest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It seems like there are some data to that, but I'm not current on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: How would that be explained? That would be a nurture.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Well, it could be nurture. It could be in uterine environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I mean, boy, the biologist is complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And this is why this, you know, like many areas of science, you said earlier that there are a lot of gray areas and no definitive answers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This is not uncommon in science that the closer you look at a problem, the more questions you get, not the fewer questions, because the universe is complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And the idea that we have people on this planet who can study the first nanoseconds of the Big Bang, that's pretty amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I've always said that if they can study the first nanoseconds of the Big Bang, we can certainly figure out something about intelligence that allows that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I'm not sure what's more complicated, the human mind or the physics of the universe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's unclear to me. I think we over-emphasize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's a very humbling statement.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Maybe it's very human centric egotistical statement that our mind is somehow super complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But biology is a tricky one to unravel. Consciousness. What is that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I've always believed that consciousness and intelligence are the two real fundamental problems of the human brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And therefore, I think they must be related.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yeah, heart problems like walk together, holding hands kind of idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You may not know this, but I did some of the early research on anesthetic drugs with brain imaging, trying to answer the question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: what part of the brain is the last to turn off when someone loses consciousness? And is that the first part of the brain to turn on when consciousness is regained?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I was working with an anesthesiologist named Mike Alkire, who was really brilliant at this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: These were really the first studies of brain imaging using positron emission tomography long before fMRI.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And you would inject a radioactive sugar that labeled the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And the harder the brain was working, the more sugar it would take up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And then you could make a picture of glucose use in the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And he was amazing. He managed to do this in normal volunteers he brought in and anesthetized as if they were going into surgery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He managed all the human subjects requirements on this research. And he was brilliant at this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And what we did is we had these normal volunteers come in on three occasions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: On one occasion, he gave them enough anesthetic drug so they were a little drowsy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And on another occasion, they came in and he fully anesthetized them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And he would say, Mike, can you hear me? And the person would say, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And then we would scan people and under no anesthetic condition. So same person.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And we were looking to see if we could see the part of the brain turn off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: He subsequently tried to do this with fMRI, which has a faster time resolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And you could do it in real time as the person went under and then regain consciousness where you couldn't do that with PET.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You had to have three different occasions. And the results were absolutely fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: We did this with different anesthetic drugs and different drugs impacted different parts of the brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So we were naturally looking for the common one. And it seemed to have something to do with the thalamus and consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: This was actual data on consciousness, real actual consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: What part of the brain turns on? What part of the brain turns off?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It's not so clear. But maybe has something to do with the thalamus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The sequence of events seem to have the thalamus in it. Boy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now, here's the question. Are some people more conscious than others?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Are there individual differences in consciousness? And I don't mean it in the psychedelic sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I don't mean it in the political consciousness sense. I just mean it in everyday life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Do some people go through everyday life more conscious than others?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And are those the people we might actually label more intelligent?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now, the other thing I was looking for is whether the parts of the brain we were seeing in the anesthesia studies

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: were the same parts of the brain we were seeing in the intelligence studies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Now, this was very complicated, expensive research. We didn't really have funding to do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: We were trying to do it on the fly. I'm not sure anybody has pursued this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I'm retired now. He's gone on to other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But I think it's an area of research that would be fascinating to see the parts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: There are a lot more imaging studies now of consciousness. I'm just not up on them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: But basically the question is which imaging, so newer imaging studies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: to see in high resolution, spatial and temporal way, which part of the brain lights up

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: when you're doing intelligence tasks and which parts of the brain lights up

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: when you're doing consciousness tasks and see the interplay between them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Try to infer. I mean, that's the challenge of neuroscience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Without understanding deeply, looking from the outside,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: try to infer something about how the whole thing works.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Well, imagine this. Here's a simple question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Does it take more anesthetic drug to have a person lose consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: if their IQ is 140 than a person with an IQ of 70?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: That's an interesting way to study it. Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I mean, if the answer to that is a stable yes, that's very interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So I tried to find out. And I went to some anesthesiology textbooks

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: about how you dose. And they dose by weight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And what I also learned, this is a little bit off subject,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: anesthesiologists are never sure how deep you are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And they usually tell by poking you with a needle, and if you don't jump,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: they tell the surgeon to go ahead. I'm not sure that's literally true,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: but it's... Well, it might be very difficult to know precisely

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: how deep you are. It has to do with the same kind of measurements

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that you were doing with the consciousness. It's difficult to know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: So I don't lose my train of thought. I couldn't find in the textbooks

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: anything about dosing by intelligence. I asked my friend, the anesthesiologist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: he said, no, he doesn't know. I said, can we do a chart review

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: and look at people using their years of education as a proxy for IQ?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Because if someone's gone to graduate school, that tells you something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You can make some inference as opposed to someone who didn't graduate high school.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Can we do a chart review? And he says, no, they never really put down

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: the exact dose. No, he said, no. So to this day, the simple question,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: does it take more anesthetic drug to put someone under if they have a high IQ?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Or less. Or less. It could go either way. Because by the way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: our early PET scan studies of intelligence found the unexpected result

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: of an inverse correlation between glucose metabolic rate and intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It wasn't how much a brain area lit up. How much it lit up was negatively correlated

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: to how well they did on the test, which led to the brain efficiency hypothesis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: which is still being studied today. And there's more and more evidence

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: that the efficiency of brain information processing is more related to intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: than just more activity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yeah, and it would be interesting, again, this total hypothesis,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And if the data take you to places that you don't have the technical expertise to follow,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: like, you know, I would like to understand more about molecular biology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: but I'm not going to become a molecular biologist now, but I know people who are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And my job is to get them interested, to take their expertise into this direction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And that is not so easy, but…

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And if the data takes you to a place that's controversial, that's counterintuitive in this world, no.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I would say it's probably a good idea to still push forward boldly,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: but to communicate the interpretation of the results with skill, with compassion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: with a greater breadth of understanding of humanity, not just the science, of the impact of the results.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: One famous psychologist wrote about this issue that somehow a balance has to be found

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: between pursuing the science and communicating it with respect to people's sensitivities,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: the legitimate sensitivities.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Somehow. He didn't say how.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Somehow. And this is…

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Every part of that sentence, somehow, and balance, is left up to the interpretation of the reader.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Let me ask you, you said big questions, the biggest, or one of the biggest.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: We already talked about consciousness and intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: one of the most fascinating, one of the biggest questions, but let's talk about the why.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Why are we here? What's the meaning of life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Oh, I'm not going to tell you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: You know, but you're not going to tell me? This is very…

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I'm going to have to wait for your next book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: The meaning of life. You know, we do the best we can to get through the day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And then there's just the finite number of the days.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Are you afraid of the finiteness of it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I think about it more and more as I get older. Yeah, I do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And it's one of these human things, that it is finite, we all know it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Most of us deny it and don't want to think about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Sometimes you think about it in terms of estate planning, you try to do the rational thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Sometimes it makes you work harder because you know your time is more and more limited

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: and you want to get things done.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: I don't know where I am on that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: It is just one of those things that's always in the back of my mind.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And I don't think that's uncommon.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Well, it's just like G-factor intelligence. It's a hard truth that's there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And sometimes you kind of walk past it and you don't want to look at it, but it's still there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Yeah, yes, you can't escape it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: And think about the G-factor in intelligence is everybody knows this is true on a personal daily basis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: Even if you think back to when you were in school, you know who the smart kids were.

metadata.title: Podcast: Richard Haier: IQ Tests, Human Intelligence, and Group Differences | Lex Fridman Podcast #302

body.input: When you are on the phone talking to a customer service representative that in response to your detailed question
