metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: 50 Feet From Syria was done that way. So you're on a boat broke.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Yeah. Yeah. But it's free food and free lodging because there's a bunk on the boat.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: But I do that not intended to stay broke, right? But based on a foundational belief that

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: if I bring to bear all of my sort of quiver of creative arrows to it, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: That I can create something of value in the world, but hopefully also financially that then I can sell to someone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And you know, every time I've done that, Lex, I've gotten into the black.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: So it's a risk and I have to have a certain risk threshold financially to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: But I believe so deeply in these stories that I'm willing to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I didn't have to do that with Hunger Ward. Luckily I had funders for that film.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Yeah. Yeah. Take risks in this life. It's going to pay off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Which reminds me of, let me ask you, I already asked you for advice about for a filmmaker, how to win an Oscar.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Well, I haven't won an Oscar. How to get nominated for an Oscar. That's true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Or just how to make great documentaries, how to make great film. But let me ask even zoom out bigger.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: You mentioned some of these things, doing the things that you think matters.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: What advice would you give to young people, high school, college, dreaming of living a life worth living?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: What advice would you give them about career or maybe just life in general?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: How to have a life they can be proud of?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Yeah. I don't know how you're going to react to this given sort of your expertise, but I would say put down the smartphone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Step away from the monitor. Because real life is not a screen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I believe that the foundational skills which are conducive and important to success aren't necessarily those technical skills,

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: which we're going to learn in trade schools or university. I think they're more foundational than that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: They're learning how to interact and listen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: With humans?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: With humans. Yeah. To really see and listen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And observe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And observe. And how to step out of your door. And if the electricity goes out and you're five miles away from your house,

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: you don't need a smartphone to get home because you've set visual markers for yourself on how to get back to where you live.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I think we're in danger right now of living in a world where if the satellites stop functioning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: then a whole lot of people become completely dysfunctional because we're so reliant upon the screens in our lives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: So I think there's a lot of foundational skills that have nothing to do with technology that we need to learn and everything rests upon those.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: So I would say learn those foundations. Learn how to write well. Read a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: There's a different kind of knowledge and wisdom that comes out of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: So reading is kind of the equivalent of listening and observing and writing is kind of integration of all of that that you've observed and listened to and tried to express something with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I think my training in the theater has served me so well in the documentary world, right? Because it's all about interaction and listening and talking and dialogue, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And that's what I do in documentaries, right? Is I listen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Yeah. We mentioned fear. Being an introvert, I'm very afraid of people, but I'm drawn to them and fascinated by them because of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Yeah. Yeah. Totally. And observing them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And you mentioned reading. You mentioned books as a catalyst, as a stimulator of your imagination.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Is there books in your life, a couple, one, two, three, that kind of left an impact or a little bit of spark of inspiration early on in life that stand out from your memory?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I was given The Prophet by Killio Debron as a graduation present from my high school English teacher.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And I still have that book in a special place on my bookshelf because I think it speaks to the nature of human experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And I return to it all the time because there's wisdom there. But there's many, many books.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Fiction or nonfiction? What connects with you usually in the past?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I read mostly nonfiction most of the time. Ten Points is a book I love a lot.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: What is Ten Points?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Ten Points is, I think his name is Bill Strickland. He was the editor of I think Bicycle Magazine.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And it's sort of his personal memoir of his experience growing up with a lot of abuse and how that transformed him as a human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: You know, one instrumental book for me that I bumped into in my early 20s, boy, these are all nonfiction, except for The Princess Bride.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I have to mention, it's an outlier. No, no, The Seven Habits of Highly Effective People.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I read that in my early 20s and I found so many of the principles in that book.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: What are the habits from that one?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Seek first to understand, then to be understood is one of them. You know, the notion of proactivity is one of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: It's really, and so I've held on to some of those principles through my life as well, for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: What have been, you've observed suffering, darker aspects of human nature in your own personal life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: What has been some of the darkest moments in your life, darkest times in your life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Is there something that you went through and then perhaps you carry it through your work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Yeah. Probably one of the darkest moments was an experience that I had again in my early 20s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I was living in Southern California and the Pacific Coast Highway that goes north and south along the beach

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: and there's that little concrete path that people jog and ride their bikes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I was riding my bike on the PCH and I was coming up to a corner on it and I heard this tremendous crash.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: It was really loud and I came around the corner and it was a car accident, a car crash.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: It was a multiple vehicle crash and what had happened is that a Volvo had hit another car

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: and then when it hit it, it went over the top of the car and hit a Volkswagen van.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: It peeled away the top of the Volkswagen van when it hit it and then landed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: So three vehicles and it just happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Lying in the middle of the road was a body decapitated and there was another person from one of the cars

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: lying in the middle of the road still alive and then on the hood of the Volvo was this woman

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: who had come through the windshield, just a mess, blood everywhere, moaning back and forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And a bystander ran into the middle of the road and started administering first aid to the person lying in the road.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And I stood there watching the scene and every fiber of my being wanted to run to the woman on the hood of the Volvo

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: and do something, anything, just to be there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And it was obvious to me that she was going to die.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: But I felt like at least if I ran there, I could offer some comfort for her last moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And right then, the sirens started to blare and I knew that there'd be paramedics there within minutes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: that people would come to help.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And I froze and I was scared and I didn't do anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And I watched while this woman died on the hood of the Volvo.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And that experience sort of seared into my consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: The fact that I watched and didn't act, I feel is one of the great failures of my life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: that I wasn't able to act in a moment of need, no matter how small.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And from that, I made a decision out of that experience that if I ever found myself in a situation

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: where I had the ability to act and I could act to help another human being in such need that I would act,

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: that I wouldn't let fear freeze me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Instead, I would allow that fear to catalyze me into action and do something and intervene

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: in whatever way I could, even if I didn't have the skill set.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And in some ways, all of that echoes in your documentaries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: You're not going to let fear stop you from trying to help.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I think that experience, that experience of failure, what I framed as just human failure on my part,

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: is foundational, probably, to my work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I don't want that to happen again, Lex. I don't want to be that person who watches.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I want to do what I can when I can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: If we zoom out, you were just one human that witnessed that, that trauma.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: You're one human that witnessed so much suffering in different parts of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And as we zoom out across space and time and look at Earth, why do you think we're here on this Earth?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: What's the meaning of human civilization? What's the meaning of your life, of individual human life?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And broadly speaking, what is the meaning of life, Sky Fitzgerald?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Oh boy, yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: For me, I can speak personally on that only.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And that's that I believe that the meaning of my life is to try to make the world a little bit better before I go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: When I was in theater in grad school, I directed a play called Shadowlands by C.S. Lewis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And there's a quote from that. It goes like this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: We are like blocks of stone out of which the sculptor carves the forms of men.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: The blows of his chisel, which hurt us so much, are what make us perfect.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Now, I would take away the perfect part, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: But I think I've remembered that quote for so many years because I believe in the underlying notion

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: that the blows of the chisel, which are the experiences that we go through, shape us, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Necessarily so, and hopefully shape us into a better human being.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And in my case, a human being that I hope can make the world a little better, you know, through those blows.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Before it's over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Yeah, before it's over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Before you go, as you said, do you think about that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: You think about the going part? Your mortality?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: You ever think about that? You said you don't have a death wish, you tried to minimize risk, but eventually it's going to be over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Yeah, for all of us. Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I'll speak for yourself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Well, you've got other plans to sell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I tend to merge. I'm going to merge with robots.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I mean, body, no, not at all. Yes, for all of us, unfortunately or fortunately, or who the heck knows.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: But do you ponder your mortality? Are you afraid of it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I live with my mortality knowing that it's fleeting, that my life is fleeting and that I'm going to go into the ground just like everyone else or maybe as ashes, you know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: So I live with that knowledge every day, but I don't allow it to stop me or hold me up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Rather, I really, it drives me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: It drives me to try to get as much done as I can before I go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Right. Yeah. So the knowledge of your death is a kind of dance partner and you try to dance beautifully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Sky, you're an incredible human, incredible artist and filmmaker.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And it's a huge honor that you would sit and spend your really valuable time with me today. I really, really enjoyed this conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: I did too. Thanks for having me, Lex, and thanks for doing what you do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Thanks for listening to this conversation with Sky Fitzgerald. To support this podcast, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And now let me leave you with some words from Elie Wiesel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: The opposite of love is not hate. It's indifference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: The opposite of art is not ugliness. It's indifference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: The opposite of faith is not heresy. It's indifference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: And the opposite of life is not death. It's indifference.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: Thank you for listening. I hope to see you next time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Skye Fitzgerald: Hunger, War, and Human Suffering | Lex Fridman Podcast #278

body.input: The lesson I would want everyone to take from the story of the First World War is that human life

body.input: material at the front, they would solve their political problems with military force. And

body.input: please check out our sponsors in the description. And now dear friends, here's Christopher Capazzola.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Let's start with a big and difficult question. How did World War I start?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: On the one hand, World War I started because of a series of events in the summer of 1914

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that brought the major powers of Europe into conflict with one another. But I actually think

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: it's more useful to say that World War I started at least a generation earlier when rising powers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: particularly Germany, started devoting more and more of their resources toward military affairs

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and naval affairs. This sets off an arms race in Europe. It sets off a rivalry over the colonial

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: world and who will control the resources in Africa and Asia. And so by the time you get to the summer

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of 1914, and in a lot of ways, I say the war has already begun and this is just the match that

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: lights the flame. So the capacity for war was brewing within the leaders and within the populace.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: They started accepting sort of slowly through the culture propagated this idea that we can go to war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: It's a good idea to go to war. It's a good idea to expand and dominate others, that kind of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Maybe not put in those clear terms, but just the sense that military action is the way that nations

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: operate at the global scale. Yes, yes and, right. So yes, there's a sense that the military can

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: be the solution to political conflict in Europe itself. And the and is that war and military

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: conflict are already happening, right? That there's war particularly in Africa, in North Africa,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in the Middle East, Balkans. Conflict is already underway and the European powers haven't faced off

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: against each other. They've usually faced off against an asymmetrical conflict against much less

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: powerful states. But in some ways that war is already underway. So do you think it was inevitable?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: It was inevitable because World War I is brought up as a case study where it seems like a few

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: accidental leaders and a few accidental events or one accidental event led to the war. And if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: change that one little thing, it could have avoided the war. Your sense is the drums of war have been

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: beating for quite a while and it would have happened almost no matter what or very likely to have happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Yes, historians never like to say things are inevitable. And certainly, you know, there were

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: people who could have chosen a different path, both in the short term and the long term.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: But fundamentally, there were irreconcilable conflicts in the system of empires in the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in 1914. I can't see, you know, it didn't have to be this war, but it had it probably had to be a war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So there was the German Empire, the Austro-Hungarian Empire, there's France and Great Britain, US,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the USP called that empire at that moment yet. When do you graduate to empire status?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Well, certainly after 1898 with the acquisition of the former territories of the Spanish Empire,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: you know, the United States has formal colonial possessions. And it has sort of mindsets of rule

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and military acquisition that would define empire in a kind of more informal sense.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So you would say you would put the blame or the responsibility of starting World War One into the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: hands of the German Empire and Kaiser Wilhelm II? You know, that's a really tough call to make.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And you know, that deciding that is going to keep historians in business for the next 200 years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And I think there are people who would lay all of the blame on the Germans, right? And you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: who would point toward a generation of arms buildup, you know, alliances that Germany made

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and promises that they made to their allies in the Balkans, to the Austro-Hungarians. And so yes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: there's an awful lot of responsibility there. There has been a trend lately to say, no,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: it's no one's fault, right? That, you know, that all of the various powers literally were sleep

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: walking into the war, right? They backed into it inadvertently. I think that lets everyone a little

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: too much off the hook, right? And so I think in between is, you know, I would put the blame on

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the system of empires itself on the system. But in that system, the actor that sort of carries the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: most responsibility is definitely Imperial Germany. So the leader of Austro-Hungarian

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Empire, Franz Joseph I, his nephew, Archduke Franz Ferdinand, he was assassinated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And so that didn't have to lead to a war. And then the leader of the German Empire,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Kaiser Wilhelm II, pressured sort of started talking trash and boiling the water that ultimately

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: resulted in the explosion plus all the other players. So what can you describe the dynamics

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of how that unrolled? What's the role of US? What's the role of France? What's the role of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Great Britain, Germany, and Austro-Hungarian Empire? Yeah, over the course of about four weeks,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: right? Following the assassination of the Archduke in Sarajevo, it sort of triggers a series of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: political conflicts and ultimately ultimatums, sort of demanding sort of that one or other power

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: sort of stand down in response to the demands of either, you know, Britain, France, or in turn,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Germany or Russia, at the same time that those alliances kind of trigger automatic responses

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: from the other side. And so it escalates. And once that escalation is combined with the call up of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: military troops, then none of those powers wants to be sort of the last one to kind of get ready

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: for conflict. So even throughout it, they think they are getting ready in a defensive maneuver.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And they think if there is conflict, well, it might be a skirmish, it might be, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: sort of a standoff. It could be solved with diplomacy later because diplomacy is failing now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And that turns out not to be the case. Diplomacy fails. It's not a skirmish. It becomes a massive

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: war. And the Americans are watching all of this from the sidelines. They have very little influence

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: over what happens that summer. How does it go from a skirmish between a few nations to a global war?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Is there a place where there's a phase transition? Yeah, I think the phase transition is in over the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: course of the fall of 1914 when the Germans make an initial sort of bold move into France. In many

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: ways, they're fighting the last war, the Franco-Prussian War of 1870. And they really do

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: sort of, you know, kind of want to have a quick sort of lightning strike in some ways against

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: France to kind of bring the war to a speedy conclusion. France turns out to be able to fight

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: back more effectively than the Germans expected. And then the battle lines sort of harden. And then

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: behind that, the French and the Germans as well as the British on the side of the French start

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: digging in literally, right? And digging trenches, trenches that at first are, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: three feet deep to avoid shelling from artillery, then become six feet, 10 feet deep, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: two miles wide that include telegraph wires that include whole hospitals in the back. And then at

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that point, you know, the front is locked in place. And the only way to break that is sort of basically

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: dialing the war up to 11, right? So massive numbers of troops, massive efforts, none of which

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: work, right? And so the war is stuck in this, but that's the phase transition right there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: What were the machines of war in that case? You mentioned trenches. What were the guns used?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: What was the size of guns? What are we talking about? What did Germany start accumulating that

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: led up to this war? One of the things that we see immediately is the industrial revolution of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: previous 30 or 40 years brought to bear on warfare, right? And so you see sort of machine guns,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: you see artillery, you know, these are the kind of the key weapons of war on both sides, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: The vast majority of battlefield casualties are from artillery shelling from one side to another,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: not, you know, sort of rifle or even sort of, you know, machine gun kind of attacks. In some ways,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the weapons of war are human beings, right? You know, tens of thousands of them poured over the top

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in these sort of waves to kind of try to break through the enemy lines. And it would work for

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: a little while, you know, but holding the territory that had been gained often proved to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: even more demanding than gaining it. And so often, you know, each side would retreat back into the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: trenches and wait for another day. And how did Russia, how did Britain,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: how did France get pulled into the war? I suppose the France one is the easy one. But what is the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: order of events here? Right. How it becomes a global war? Yeah. So Britain, France, and Russia

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: are at this time in, they're an alliance. And so the conflicts, you know, in the summer of 1914

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that lead sort of to the declarations of war happen sort of one after another, right? In August,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in late August of 1914. And all three powers essentially come in at the same time, because

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: they have promised to do so through a series of alliances conducted secretly in the years before

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: 1914 that committed them to defend one another. Germany, Austria, Hungary, and the Ottoman empire

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: have their own sort of set of secret agreements that also commit them to defend one another.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And what this does is it sort of brings them all into conflict at the exact same moment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: They're also, for many of these countries, bringing not just their national armies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: but also their empires into the conflict, right? So Britain and France, of course, have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: you know, enormous sort of global empires that begin mobilizing soldiers as well as raw materials.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Germany has, you know, less of an overseas empire. Russia and the Ottoman empire, of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: have their own sort of hinterland, you know, within the empire. And very soon, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: sort of all of the warring powers are bringing the entire world into the conflict.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Did they have a sense of how deadly the war is? I mean, this is another scale of death and destruction.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: At the beginning, no, but very quickly. The scale of the devastation of these sort of massive

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: over the top attacks on the trenches is apparent to the military officers, and it very quickly

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: becomes apparent even at home. You know, there is, of course, censorship of the battlefield,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and, you know, specific details don't reach people. But, you know, for civilians in any of the warring

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: powers, they know fairly soon how destructive the war is. And to me, that's always been a real sort

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of puzzle, right? So that by the time the United States comes to decide whether to join the war in

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: 1917, they know exactly what they're getting into, right? They're not backing into the war in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: ways that the European powers did. You know, they've seen the devastation. They've seen

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: photographs. They've seen injured soldiers, and they make that choice anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: When you say they, do you mean the leaders of the people? Did the death and destruction reach

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the minds of the American people by that time? Yes, absolutely. You know, we don't, in 1917,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: have the mass media that we have now, but, you know, there are images in newspapers. There are

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: newsreels that play at the movie theaters, and, of course, some of it is sanitized. But

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that combined with press accounts, often really quite descriptive press accounts, gory accounts,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: reached, you know, anyone who cared to read them. You know, certainly plenty of people didn't follow

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the news, felt it was far away. But most Americans who cared about the news knew how devastating this

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: war was. Yeah, there's something that happens that I recently visited Ukraine for a few weeks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: There's something that happens with the human mind as you get away from the actual front,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: wherever the bullets are flying, like literally one kilometer away. You start to not feel the war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: You'll hear an explosion, you'll see an explosion, you start to like get assimilated to it, or you

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: start to get used to it. And then when you get as far away from like currently what is Kiev,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: you start to, you know the war's going on, everybody around you is fighting in that war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: but it's still somehow distant. And I think with the United States, with the ocean between,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: even if you have the stories everywhere, it still is somehow distant, like the way a movie is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: maybe, yeah, like a movie or a video game, it's somewhere else. Even if your loved ones are going,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: or you are going to fight. Yeah, that is absolutely the case. And in some ways,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: right? And both of those things really are crystal clear in terms of their importance during the war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Right? So both of those things are on the table. Being a citizen who is a citizen who isn't

body.input: But also what it means to be an American, right? To feel like it, to be part of this project is

body.input: Perhaps that's a good example of it, of the James Montgomery Flagg's 1916 poster

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: it's memeified form. I don't know, but we know this poster and we don't know where it came from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Or most Americans, I think, me included, didn't know where it came from. And it actually comes

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: from 1916. Does this poster represent the birth of something new in America, which is a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: commodification or, I don't know, that propaganda machine that says what it means to be an American

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: is somebody that fights for their country. Yeah. So the image, it's, in fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I think one of the most recognizable images, not only in the United States, but in the entire world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And you can bring it almost anywhere on earth in 2022 and people will know what it refers to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So this is an image that circulated first as a magazine cover, later as a recruitment poster,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and saying, I want you. And the I want you is a recruitment tool to join the US Army.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And this image really kind of starts as a kind of, like I said, a magazine cover in 1916

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And at that point in 1916, we're still neutral. In 1917, it's turned into a US Army recruiting

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: It's a sort of window into American culture at a crucial moment in our history, where the federal

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: citizens. And at the same time, where sort of technologies of mass production and mass media,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and what we would probably call propaganda, are being sort of mobilized for the first time in this

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320
