body.input: What's the Espionage Act?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: The Espionage Act is a sort of omnibus bill, it contains about 10 or different provisions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: very few of which have to do with espionage. But one key provision basically makes it illegal

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to say or do anything that would interfere with military recruitment. And that provision is used

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to shut down radical publications, to shut down German language publications. And this really has

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: a chilling impact on speech during the war. Could you put into words what it means to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: an American citizen that is in part sparked by World War I? What does that mean? Somebody that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: should be willing to sacrifice certain freedoms to fight for their country?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Somebody that's willing to fight to spread freedom elsewhere in the world, spread the American ideals?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Does that begin to tell the story what it means to be an American?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I think what we see is a change, right? So citizenship during World War I now includes

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the obligation to defend the country, to serve, and if asked to die for it. And we certainly see

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that. And I think we see the close linkage of military service and US citizenship coming out

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of this time period. But when you start making lots of demands on people to fulfill obligations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in turn, they're going to start demanding, right, to defend their country.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And in turn, they're going to start demanding rights. And we start to see not necessarily

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: during the war, but after, more demands for free speech protections, more demands for equality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: for marginalized groups. And so obligations and rights are sort of developing in a dynamic

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: relationship. Oh, it's almost like an overreach of power sparked a sense like, oh, crap, we can't

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: centralize power to a beauty, like to drag us into a war we need to be able to. So there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the birth of that tension between the government and the people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: It's a rebirth of it. Of course, that tension is always there. But in its modern form,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I think it comes from this re-intensification of it. So what about the, you said that World War I

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: gave birth to the surveillance state in the US. Can you explain?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Yeah. So the Espionage Act sort of empowers federal organizations to watch other Americans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: They are particularly interested in anyone who is obstructing the draft, anyone who is trying to

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: organize labor or strikes or radical movements, and anyone who might have sympathy for Germany,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: which basically means all German-Americans come under surveillance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Initially, this is very small scale, but soon every government agency gets involved,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: from the Treasury Department Secret Service to the post office, which is sort of reading mail,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to the Justice Department, which mobilizes 200,000 volunteers. It's a really significant

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: enterprise. Much of it goes away after the war, but of all the things that go away,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: this core of the surveillance state is the thing that persists most fully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Is this also a place where the size of government starts to grow in these different organizations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: or maybe creates a momentum for growth of government?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Oh, it's exponential growth. Over the course of the war, by almost any metric you use,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: right? The size of the federal budget, the number of federal employees, the number of soldiers in

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the standing army, all of those things skyrocket during the war. They go down after the war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: but they never go down to what they were before.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And probably gave a momentum for growth over time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Yes, absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Did World War I give birth to the military industrial complex in the United States, so

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: war profiteering, expanding of the war machine in order to financially benefit a lot of parties

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: involved?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So I guess I would maybe break that into two parts, right? That on the one hand, yes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: there is war profiteering. There are investigations of it. In the years after the war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: there's a widespread concern that the profit motive had played too much of a part in the war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and that's definitely the case. But I think when you try to think of this term, military industrial

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: complex, it's best to think of it as at what point does the one side lock in the other,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: right? That military choices are shaped by industry objectives and vice versa. And I do

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: think that that was fully locked into place during World War I. I think that's really a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Cold War phenomenon when the United States is on this intense kind of footing for two

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: generations in a row.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So industrial is really important there, there's companies. So before then, weapons of war were

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: funded directly by the government. Who was manufacturing the weapons of war?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Who was manufacturing the weapons of war? They were generally manufactured by private industry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: There were of course, our arsenal sort of 19th century iterations where the government would

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: produce its own weapons, partly to make sure that they got what they wanted. But most of the weapons

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of war for all of the European powers and the United States are produced by private industry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So why do you say that the military industrial complex didn't start then? What was the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: important thing that happened in the Cold War?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I think one way to think about it is the Cold War is a point at which it switches from being a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: dial to a ratchet, right? So during World War I, the relationship between the military and industry

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: dials up fast and high and stays that way and it dials back down. Whereas during the Cold War,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the relationship between the two often looks more like a ratchet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Yeah, it becomes unstoppable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: It goes up again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: In the way that you start, I think the way the military industrial complex is often

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: discussed as a system that is unstoppable. It expands. If you take a very cynical view,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: it creates war so that it can make money. It doesn't just find places where it can help

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: through military conflict. It creates tensions that directly or indirectly lead to military

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: conflict that it can then fuel and make money from.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: That is certainly one of the concerns of both people who were critical of the First World War

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and then also of Dwight Eisenhower when he's president and in his farewell address where he

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: introduces the term military industrial complex. Some of it is about the profit motive, but some

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of it is a fear that Eisenhower had that no one had an interest in stopping this and that no one

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: had a voice in stopping it and that the ordinary American could really do nothing to dial it to

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: dial things down. Is it strange to you that we don't often hear that kind of speech today

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: with Eisenhower speaking about the military industrial complex? For example, we'll have

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: people criticizing the spending on war efforts, but they're not discussing the machinery of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: military industrial complex, like the basic way that human nature works, that we get ourselves

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: trapped in this thing. They're saying there's better things to spend money on versus describing

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: a very seemingly natural process of when you build weapons of war that's going to lead to more war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: It pulls you in somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: AC Yeah. I would say throughout the Cold War and even after the end of it, there has not been a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: sustained conversation in the United States about our defense establishment, what we really need

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and what serves our interest and to what extent other things like market forces, profit motives,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: belong in that conversation. What's interesting is that in the generation after the First World War,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that conversation was on the table through a series of investigations in the US, the NIE

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Committee in Britain, a royal commission, journalistic exposés. This would have been just

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: talked about constantly in the years between about 1930 and 1936, as people were starting to worry

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that storm clouds were gathering in Europe again. AC Yeah, but it always seems like those folks get

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: pushed to the fringes. You're made an activist versus a thinking leader.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: AC Those discussions are often marginalized, framed as conspiracy theory, etc. I think it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: important to realize that in the generation after World War I, this was a serious civic conversation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: It led to investigations of defense finance. It led to experiments in Britain and France,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in public finance of war material. I think those conversations need to be reconvened

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: now in the 21st century. AC Is there any parallels between

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: World War I and the war in Ukraine? The reason I bring it up is because

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: you mentioned there was a hunger for war, a capacity for war that was already established,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and the different parties were just boiling the tensions. There's a case made that America had a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: role to play, NATO had a role to play in the current war in Ukraine. Is there some truth to that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Is there some truth to that when you think about it in the context of World War I?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Or is it purely about the specific parties involved, which is Russia and Ukraine?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: AC I think it's very easy to draw parallels between World War I and the war in Ukraine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: but I don't think they really work. The First World War in some ways is generated by a fundamental

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: conflict in the European system of empires, in the global system of empires. In many ways,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: if there's a parallel, the war in Ukraine is the parallel to some of the conflicts in the Mediterranean

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and the Balkans in 1911 to 1913, that then later there was a much greater conflict.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I think if there's any lessons to be learned for how not to let World War III look like World War I,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: it would be to make sure that systems aren't locked into place, that escalate wars out of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: people's expectations. RL That's, I suppose, what I was implying, that this is the early stages of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: World War III. That in the same way that several wolves are licking their chops or whatever the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: expression is, they're creating tension, they're creating military conflict with a kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: unstoppable imperative for a global war. Many people that are looking at this are really

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: worried about that. Now, the stopping, the forcing function to stop this war is that there's several

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: nuclear powers involved, which has, at least for now, worked to stop full-on global war.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: But I'm not sure that's going to be the case. In fact, what is one of the surprising things to me

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in Ukraine is that still in the 21st century, we can go to something that involves nuclear powers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: not directly yet, but awfully close to directly go to a hot war. Do you worry about that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that there's a kind of descent into a World War I type of scenario?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: RL Yes. That keeps me up at night, and I think it should keep the citizens of both the United

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: States and Russia up at night. And I think, again, it gets back to what I was saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that in the summer of 1914, even then, things that looked like a march toward war could have

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: been different. And so I think it's important for leaders of both countries and of all of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: sort of related country, of Ukraine, of the various NATO powers, to really sort of imagine

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: off-ramps and to imagine alternatives and to make them possible, whether it's through diplomacy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: whether it's through other formats. I think that that's the only way to prevent sort of greater

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: escalation. CB What's the difference between World War I and the Civil War? In terms of how they

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: defined what it means to be an American, but also the American citizen's relationship with the war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: what the leaders were doing, is there interesting differences and similarities?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Besides the fact that everybody seems to have forgot about World War I in the United States,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and everyone still remembers Civil War. RL I mean, it's true. And the American Civil War

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: defines American identity in some ways, along with the Revolution and the Second World War,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: more so than any other conflict. And it's a fundamentally different war. It's one because

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: on the territory of the United States between Americans. And so the dynamics are really quite

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: different. The leaders, particularly Lincoln, have a different relationship to the home front,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to civilians than they then say Wilson or Roosevelt have in World War I and II.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: CB Also, the way you would tell the story of the Civil War, perhaps similar to the way we tell the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: story of World War II, there's like a reason to actually fight the war. The way we tell the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: story is we're fighting for this idea that all men are created equal, that the war is over slavery

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in part. Perhaps that's a drastic oversimplification of what the war was actually about

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in the moment. Like how do you get pulled into an actual war versus a hot discussion?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And the same with World War II, people kind of framed the narrative that it was against evil.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Hitler being evil, I think the key part of that is probably the Holocaust,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: is how you can formulate Hitler's being evil. If there's no Holocaust, perhaps there's a case

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to be made that we wouldn't see World War II as such, quote unquote, good war,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that there's an atrocity that had to happen to make it really, to be able to tell a clear narrative

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of why we get into this war. Perhaps such a narrative doesn't exist for World War I,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Yeah. I mean, I think the Civil War in both the North and the South,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: troops are raised overwhelmingly through volunteer recruitment. There is a draft in both the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: conscription. And so in fact, the mobilization for volunteers often organized locally around

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: individual communities or states, creates multiple identities and levels of loyalty.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Where people both in the North and the South have loyalty both to their state regiments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to their community militias, and as well to the country. They are fighting over the country,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: after the victory in the war, is a crucial force shaping America ever since.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So what was the neutrality period? Why did the US stay out of the war for so long? What was going

body.input: on in that interesting, what made Woodrow Wilson change his mind? What was the interesting dynamic

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: there? I always say that the United States entered the war in the early 1900s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: The United States entered the war in April of 1917, but Americans entered it right away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: They entered it, some of them actually went and volunteered and fought almost exclusively on the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: side of Britain and France. At least 50,000 joined the Canadian army or the British army and serve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Millions volunteer, they sent humanitarian aid. I think in many ways, modern war creates modern

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: humanitarianism and we can see that in the neutrality period. And even if they wanted the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: United States to stay out of the war, a lot of Americans get involved in it by thinking about

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: it, caring about it, arguing about it. And at the same time, they're worried that British propaganda

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: is shaping their news system. They are worried that German espionage is undermining them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: They're worried that both Britain and Germany are trying to interfere in American elections

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and American news cycles. And at the same time, a revolution is breaking out in Mexico.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So there are concerns about what's happening in the Western hemisphere as well as what's happening

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in Europe. So World War I was supposed to be the war to end all wars and it didn't. How did

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of politics of resentment and hate that comes from the Nazis. For the United States, in some ways,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320
