body.input: that divert that hate into other places. One of the biggest things I thought was not

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: part of the calculus in when the United States invaded Afghanistan and Iraq is the creation of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: hate. When you drop a bomb, even if it hits military targets, even if it kills soldiers,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: which in that case, it didn't, there's a very large amount of civilians, what does that do to the...

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Yeah, how many years, minutes, hours, months, and years of hate do you create with a single bomb

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: you drop? And I calculate that. Literally, in the Pentagon have a chart, how many people will hate

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: us, how many people does it take, do some science here, how many people does it take when you have a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: million people that hate you, how many of them will become terrorists? How many of them will do

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: something to the nation you love and care about, which is the United States, will do something that

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: will be very costly? I feel like there was not a plot in a chart. It was more about short-term

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: effects. Yes, it's again, it's the idea of using military force to solve political problems. And I

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: think there's a squandering of goodwill that people have around the world towards the United States.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: That's a respect for its economy, for its consumer products, and so forth. And I think that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: been lost a lot of that. Do you think leaders can stop war? I have perhaps a romantic notion,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: perhaps because I do these podcasts in person and so on, that leaders that get in a room together

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and can talk, they can stop war. I mean, that's the power of a leader, especially one in an

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: authoritarian regime, that they can, through camaraderie, alleviate some of the emotions

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: associated with the ego. Yes, leaders can stop war if they get into the room when they understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: from the masses in their countries that war is something that they want stopped.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So the people ultimately have a really big say. They do. It was mass movements by people in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: United States for the nuclear freeze, in Russia pushing for openness that brought, for example,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev to Reykjavik to debate and eventually put caps on nuclear

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: weapons. Those two people made choices in the room that made that possible, but they were both

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: being pushed and knew they were being pushed by their people. Boy, that's a tough one. It puts a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: lot of responsibility on the German people, for example. In both wars, we fans of history tend to

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: conceive of history as a meeting of leaders. We think of Chamberlain, we think of Churchill,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and the importance of them in the Second World War. We think about Hitler and Stalin and think that

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: if certain conversations happened, the war could have been avoided. You tell the story of how many

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: times Hitler and Nazi Germany's military might was not sufficient. They could have been easily

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: stopped. The pacifists, the people who believed Hitler or foolish enough to believe Hitler,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: didn't act properly. If the leaders just woke up to that idea, in fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Churchill is a kind of representation of that. But in your conception here, it's possible that

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Churchill was also a representation of the British people, even though seemingly unpopular,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that force was... They gave birth to somebody like Churchill, who said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: we'll never surrender, right? Yes. She'll fight in the beaches.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Yes. I think World War II Britain is a good example of that. It is clearly a dynamic leader

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: who has his pulse on what the people want and demand and are willing to do. It's a very

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: dynamic art of leading that and shaping those wants at the same time as knowing that you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: bound by them. Well, then if we conceive a history in this way, let me ask you about our presidents.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: You are taking on the impossibly difficult task of teaching a course in a couple of years here,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: or in one year, called the History of American Presidency. What is the history of American

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: presidents called? The History of American Presidential Elections.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So if the people are in part responsible for leaders,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: how can we explain what is going on in America that we have the leaders that we do today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So if we think about the elections of the past several cycles,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I guess let me ask, are we a divided nation? Are we more of a divided nation than we were in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: past? What do you understand about the American citizen at the beginning of this century

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: from the leaders we have elected? Yes. Obviously, we are a divided country

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in our rhetoric, in our day-to-day politics. But

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: we are nowhere near as divided as we have been in other periods in our history, the most obvious,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of course, being the American Civil War 150 years ago. And the distinction is not just that we

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: haven't come to blows, but that we are fundamentally one society, one economy, and deeply integrated

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: as a nation, both domestically and on the world stage in ways that look nothing like the United

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: States in 1861. Will political rhetoric continue to be extreme? Of course. But we're not as divided

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: as people think we are. Well, then if you actually look throughout human history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: does it always get outside of the people, do the elections get as contentious as they've recently

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: been? So there's a kind of perception that has been very close, and there's a lot of accusations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: a lot of tensions. It's very heated. It's almost fueling the machine of division. Has that been

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: often the case? It has. It hasn't, it hasn't. I mean, I do think right now is different. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: there it's worth distinguishing, are there deep social or economic divisions, which I don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: actually think that there are, versus partisanship in particular, sort of the rivalry between the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: two parties. And it's very clear that we are in an era of what political scientists call

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: hyperpartisanship, right? And that the two parties have taken fundamentally different positions and

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: moved further apart from one another. And that is what I think people talk about when they say

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: our country is divided. So the country may not be divided, even if our politics are highly partisan,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that is a divergence from other time periods in our history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So I wonder if this kind of political partisanship is actually an illusion of division. I sometimes

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: feel like we mostly all agree on some basic fundamentals. And the things that people

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: allegedly disagree on are really blown out of proportion. And there's like a media machine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and the politicians really want you to pick a blue side and a red side. And because of that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: somehow, I mean, families break up over Thanksgiving dinner about who they voted for.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: There's a really strong pressure to be the red or blue. And I wonder if that's a feature or a bug,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: whether this is just part of the mechanism of democracy that we want to, even if there's not

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: a real thing to be divided over, we need to construct it such that you can always have a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: tension of ideas in order to make progress, to figure out how to progress as a nation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I think we're figuring that out in real time. On the one hand, it's easy to say that it's a feature

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of a political system that has two parties. And the United States is in some ways unique

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in not being a parliamentary democracy. And so in some ways, you would think that would be the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: feature that is causing partisanship and to reach these heights. That said, we can even see in

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: parliamentary systems and all around the world that the same kinds of rhetorics of irreconcilable

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: division, a kind of politics of emotion are proliferating around the world. Some of that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: as you say, I think is not as real as it appears on television, on social media, and other formats.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So I don't know that other countries that are experiencing sort of political conflict,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I'm not sure that they're deeply divided either. So I've had the fortune of being intellectually

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: active through the George Bush versus Al Gore election, then the Obama, and just every election

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: since. And it seems like a large percentage of those elections, there's been a claim that the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: elections were rigged, that there is some conspiracy, corruption, malevolence on the other side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I distinctly remember when Donald Trump won in 2016, a lot of people I know said that election

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: was rigged and there's different explanations, including Russian influence. And then in 2020,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I was just running in Austin along the river and somebody said like, oh, huge fan of the podcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And they said like, what do you think of it? This is just not right. What's happening in this country

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that the 2020 election was obviously rigged from their perspective in electing Joe Biden versus

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Donald Trump. Do you think there's a case to be made for and against each claim in the full context

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of history of our elections being rigged? I think the American election system is

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: fundamentally sound and reliable. And I think that the evidence is clear for that regardless of which

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: election you're looking at. In some ways, whether you look at a presidential election or even a local

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: county election for dogcatcher or something, that the amount of time and resources and precision

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that go into voter registration, vote counting, certification processes are crucial to democratic

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: institutions. I think when someone says rigged, regardless of which side of the political spectrum

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: they're coming from, they're looking for an answer. They're looking for that one answer for what is in

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: fact a complex system. So on the left, when they say rigged, they may be pointing to a wide range

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of ways in which they think that the system is tilted through gerrymandering,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: misrepresentation through the electoral college. On the right, when people say rigged, they may be

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: concerned about voter security, about ways in which the mainstream media may control

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: messages. In both cases, the feeling is it's articulated as my vote didn't get counted right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: But the deeper concern is my vote doesn't count. My voice isn't being heard. So no, I don't think

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the elections are rigged. So let me push back. There's a comfort to the story that they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: not rigged. And a lot of us like to live in comfort. So people who articulate conspiracy theories

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: say, sure, it's nice to be comfortable, but here's the reality. And the thing they articulate is

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: there's incentives in close elections, which we seem to have nonstop close elections. There's so

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: many financial interests. There's so many powerful people. Surely you can construct not just with the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: media and all the ways you describe both on the left and the right, the elections could be rigged,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: but literally actually in a fully illegal way, manipulate the results of votes. Surely there's

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: incentive to do that. And I don't think that's a totally ridiculous argument because it's like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: all right, well, I mean, it actually lands to the question, which is a hard question for me to ask

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: as an optimist of how many malevolent people out there and how many malevolent people are required

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to rig an election. So what is the face transition for a system to become from like

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: corruption light to high level of corruption such that you could do things like rig elections,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: which is what happens quite a lot in many nations in the world even today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So yes, there is interference in elections and there has been in American history,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and we can go all the way back into the 18th century. You don't have to go back to Texas

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in the 1960s, LBJ to find examples of direct interference in the outcome of elections.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And there are incentives to do that. Those incentives will only feel more existential

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: as hyper-partisanship makes people think that the outcome of the elections are a matter of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: black and white or life and death. And you will see people organizing every way they can

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to shape elections. We saw this in the 1850s when settlers, pro and anti-slavery flooded into Kansas

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to try to determine the outcome of an election. We see this in the reconstruction period when

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the Ku Klux Klan shows up to block the doors for black voters in the South.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: This history is not new, it's there. I think the reason why I think that the system is sound

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: is not or the reason when I say I believe that the election system is fundamentally sound,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: is fundamentally sound. I'm not trying to be reassuring or encourage complacency.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I'm saying this is something that we need to do and to work on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: AC So the current electoral mechanisms are sufficiently robust. Even if there is corruption,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: even if there is rigging, the force that corrects itself, corrects and ensures that nobody gets out

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of line is much stronger than the other incentives, which are like the corrupting incentives.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: That's the thing I talked about, visiting Ukraine talking about corruption.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: A lot of people talk about corruption as being a symptom. If the system allows,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: creates these incentives for there to be corruption, humans will always go for corruption.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: That's just, you have to assume that. The power of the United States is that it constructs

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: systems that prevent you from being corrupt at scale. At least, I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: depends what you believe, but most of us, if you believe in this country, you have to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: you believe in the self-correcting mechanisms of corruption that even if that desire is in

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the human heart, the system resists it, prevents it. That's your current belief.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: AC Yes, as of today. But I do think that those, that will require oversight by institutions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: ideally ones that are insulated as much as possible from partisan politics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: which is very difficult right now. And it will require the demands of the American people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that they want these elections to be fair and secure. And that means being willing to lose them,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: regardless of which party you're in favor of. AC So what do you think about the power of the media

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to create partisanship? I'm really worried that there's a huge incentive, speaking of incentives,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to divide the country. The media and the politicians, I'm not sure where it originates,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: but it feels like it's the media. Maybe it's a very cynical perspective on journalism, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: it seems like if we're angry and divided as evenly as possible, you're going to maximize the number

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of clicks. So it's almost like the media wants to elect people that are going to be the most

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: divisive maximizing. And the worry I have is they are not beyond either feeding or if you want to

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: be very cynical, manufacturing narratives that lead that division, like the narrative of an

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: election being rigged. Because if you convinced half the populace that the election was completely

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: rigged, that's a really good way to get a lot of clicks. And the very cynical view is I don't know

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: if the media machine will stop the destruction of our democracy in service of getting more clicks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: It may destroy our entire democracy just to get more clicks, just because the fire, as the thing

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: burns down, will get clicks. Am I putting too much blame on the media here? The machine of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: You're diagnosing the incentive structure, you're depicting that with 100% accuracy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: But I think history teaches that you might be giving the media too much causal power,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that the American people are smarter than the media that they consume. And even today,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: we know that. Even people who consume just Fox or just MSNBC know what they're consuming.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So I don't think that media will be the solution. And I certainly don't think that returning to

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: a media structure of the mid 20th century with three news channels that all tell us one story,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that's no golden age that we're trying to get back to, for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Well, there is a novel thing in human history, which is Twitter and social media and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So we're trying to find our footing as a nation to figure out how to think about politics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: how to maintain our basic freedoms, our sense of democracy, of our interaction with government,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and so on on this new medium of social media. How do you think Twitter changed things?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Do you think Twitter is good for democracy? Do you think it has changed what it means to

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: be an American citizen? Or is it just the same old media mechanism?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: It has not changed what it means to be an American citizen. It may have changed the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: day to day sound of being and the experience of it. It got noisier, it got louder,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and it got more decentered. I think Twitter is paradoxical. On the one hand, it is a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: fundamentally democratic platform. And in some ways, it democratizes institutions that had

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: gatekeepers and authority figures for a very long time. But on the other hand, it's not a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: democratic institution at all. It's a for-profit corporation, and it operates under those principles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And so that said, it's an institution of American and global life that the people

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of the United States have the authority to do. And so it's a very important platform.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: It's an institution of American and global life that the people of the United States have the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: authority to regulate or reshape as they see fit, both that and other major media players.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So one of the most dramatic decisions that illustrate both sides of what you're saying

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: is when Twitter decided to ban, I think permanently, the president of the United

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: States, Donald Trump, off of Twitter. Can you make the case that that was a good idea and

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: a good idea? Yes. I think the simple fact of the matter is Twitter is a platform. It has rules of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: service. Twitter concluded that President Trump had violated the terms of service and blocked

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: them. And if you have rules, you have to enforce them. Did it have consequences? It had direct and

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: predictable consequences of creating a sense among millions of Americans that Twitter had taken

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: aside in politics or confirming their belief that it had done so. Will it have unintended

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: consequences? This is where the historian can come in and say, yes, there's always unintended

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: consequences. And we don't know what it would mean for political figures to be excluded from

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: various media platforms under these notions that they had violated terms of service, et cetera.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I guess we'll see. Well, to me, I'm generally against censorship,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: but to take Twitter's perspective, it's unclear to me in terms of unintended consequences,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: whether censoring a human being from being part of your platform is going to decrease or increase

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the amount of hate in the world. So it is a strong case to be made that banning somebody like Donald

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Trump increases the amount of resentment among people and that's a very large number of people

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that support him or even love him or even see him as a great president, one of the greatest this

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: country has had. And so if you completely suppress his voice, you're going to intensify the support

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that he has from just the regular support for another human being who ran for president to

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: somebody that becomes an almost heroic figure for that set of people. Now, the flip side is

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: removing a person from a platform like Donald Trump might lessen the megaphone of that particular

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: person, might actually level the democratic notion that everybody has a voice. So basically,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: removing the loud extremes is helpful for giving the center, the calm, the thoughtful voices more

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: power. And so in that sense, that teaches a lesson that don't be crazy in any one direction. Don't

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: go full, don't go Lenin, don't go Hitler. You have to stay in the middle. There's divisions in the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: middle, there's discussions in the middle, but stay in the middle. So, I think that's

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: sort of the steel man, the case for censoring. But I, boy, is censorship a slippery slope.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: And also, boys, Twitter becoming a thing that's more than just a company. It seems like it's a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: medium of communication that we use for information, for knowledge, for wisdom even. During the period

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of COVID, we used it to gain an understanding of what the hell's going on. What should we do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: What's the state of the art science? Science fundamentally transformed during the time of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: COVID because you have no time for the full review cycle that science usually goes through. And some

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of the best sources of information for me, from the conspiracy theory to the best doctors, was

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Twitter. The data, the stats, all that kind of stuff. And that feels like more than a couple,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: more than a company. And then Twitter and YouTube and different places took a really strong stance

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: on COVID, which is the lazy stance, in my opinion, which is we're going to listen to whatever CDC or

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the institutions have said. But the reality is you're an institution of your own now. You're kind

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of the press. You're like, there's a, there's a, it's a really difficult position. It's a really,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: really difficult position to take. But I wish they have stepped up and take on the full responsibility

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and the pain of fighting for the freedom of speech.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Yes, they need, they need to do that. But, you know, I'm struck by some of the things that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: said, ways in which, you know, Twitter has the power to shape the conversation. And I don't think

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in a democratic society, democratic polities should cede that power to, to for-profit companies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Do you agree that it's possible that Twitter has that power currently? Do you sense that it has

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the power? Because I might sense as Twitter has the power to start wars, like tweets have the power

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to start wars, to, to, yeah, to, to change the direction of elections.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Maybe in the sense in the ways in which, you know, a wave has the power to wash away sand, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: You know, it's, it's the meat, it's still the medium, right? It's not, it's not in itself an

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: actor. It's how actors use the platform, which requires us to scrutinize the structure of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: platform and access to it. Unfortunately, it's not maybe as similar to the wave. It's not just a

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: medium. It's a, it's a medium plus. It's a medium that enables virality that benefits from virality

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of engagement. And that means singular voices can, can have a disproportionate impact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: like not even voices, singular ideas, dramatic ideas can have a disproportionate impact. And so

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that actually threatens, it's almost like, I don't know what the equivalent is in nature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: but it's a, it's a wave that can grow exponentially because of the intensity of the, the initial

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: intensity of the wave. I don't know how to describe this as a dynamical system, but it feels like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: it feels like there, there is a responsibility there not to accelerate, not to accelerate

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: voices just because they get a lot of engagement. You have to have a proportional representation

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of that voice. But you're saying that a strong democracy should be robust to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: A strong democracy can and should, and will be. I mean, I think the other thing a historian will

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: tell you about Twitter is that this too shall pass, right? But, but I do think, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the structures of, of the, of the platform, of the algorithm, of, of this and other major players

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: are, are eligible for scrutiny by, by democratic institutions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: So in preparing to teach the course, the history of American presidential elections leading up to

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the 2024 elections. So one of the lessons of history is this too shall pass. So don't make

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in some new ways, right? Not only American projection of power into Asia, right? But also

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the ways in which American power affected people in Asia, right? Either as in places like the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Philippines where the United States had a colony for almost 50 years, or Asian Americans, people

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: who had migrated over their descendants in the United States. And those linkages between the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: United States and Asia, particularly the US-Philippine connection, I think were something

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that needed to be traced across the 20th century, because it's a way, kind of a new way of seeing

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: American power from a different angle. You see it in that way. What are some aspects that define

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: America from when you take the perspective of the Pacific? What military conflict and the asymmetry

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: of power there? Right. So I start in 1898 with the US invasion of the Philippines,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: its conquests and annexation. And I think in many ways, this is a defining conflict of the 20th

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: century that's often completely overlooked. We're described, I think, incorrectly as merely a war

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: with Spain, right? That the war in the Philippines is our first extended overseas conflict, our first

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: conflict in what would come to be called the developing world or third world. It's a form of

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: counterinsurgency. This is the US Army sort of learning lessons that are then repeated again in

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the Second World War in Korea, Vietnam, and even after 9-11. Is the Philippines our friends or

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: enemies in this history? Well, that's the interesting part, right? Is that the book focuses

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in particular on Filipinos who fight with the Americans who fought in the US Army and Navy

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: over the course of the 20th century. And they are in a fundamentally ironic position, right? They are

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: from the Philippines and they're fighting for the United States, which is the colonial power

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: occupying their country. And I think that irony persists, right? So if you look at polling data

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: where they ask people all around the world, do you think positively or negatively about the United

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: States? That the highest responses are from the Philippines, right? Filipinos view the United

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: States more favorably than people from any other country in the world, including America, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: That they think more favorably of Americans than Americans do. And so, sort of unpacking that irony

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: is part of what I'm trying to get at in the book. What was the People Power Revolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: and what lessons can we learn from it? You kind of assign an important,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: a large value to it in terms of what we can learn for the American project.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Yeah. So in 1986, the president of the Philippines, Ferdinand Marcos, is overthrown by

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: a popular revolution known as People Power in the wake of a contested and probably almost certainly

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: rigged election that sort of confirms his rule. When that is overturned through sort of mass

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: movements in the Philippines, it's also sort of confirmed in many ways by the reluctance of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: United States to intervene to prop up a Cold War ally. Ferdinand Marcos had supported American

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: policy throughout his administration. The Reagan administration, Ronald Reagan was president at the

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: time, basically chooses not to support him. That's a personally wrenching decision for Reagan himself,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: but he's being shaped in many ways by the emerging voices of neoconservative, political,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: foreign policy voices. In particular, Paul Wolfowitz and the State Department and others who see

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: movements for democracy and democratization that then kind of take fire in the late 20th century

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: in Latin America, in South Korea, in Eastern Europe, and all around the world until

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: it hits the wall in Tiananmen Square in June 1989.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: What's that wall? What do you mean by it hits the wall?

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: There are global movements for democratization, for opening up throughout the world starting in

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the 1980s. Obviously, they continue in Eastern Europe with the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: I say it hits the wall in China with the protests in Tiananmen Square that are blocked and that are

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: crushed and I think represent a real sort of turning point in the history of democratic

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: institutions on a global scale in the late 20th century. There's some places where the fight for

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: this dynamic dance between leaders, whether totalitarian leaders or leaders of democratic

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: movements and the people that they're leading. Sometimes it works and sometimes it doesn't.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: Let me ask a big ridiculous question because we talked about presidential elections. Now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: a fundamental moral character, and just the ability to fight the fight of politics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: that Lincoln would be reelected. Both times, he's not a master campaigner by any means,

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: but he was a master politician as a governor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: the great moments. Yeah, both of those things are true.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: That feels like the case.

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: how the nations, how the history of these nations unravel, unfold rather. So it's very interesting

metadata.title: Podcast: Christopher Capozzola: World War I, Ideology, Propaganda, and Politics | Lex Fridman Podcast #320

body.input: to think about. And the same is true for Donald Trump, Joe Biden, Obama, George Bush, Bill Clinton,

body.input: and so on. I think it's probably an unanswerable question of which of the presidents will be
