body.input: and converted to compounds that are needed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: A lot of it gets released as carbon dioxide and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So these are actually really important cycles

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: that are catalyzed by the virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's so wild that nature has developed a mechanism

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: for mass murder of bacteria.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: That's one way to look at it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: but it's just what happened, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I mean, I wonder what the evolutionary advantage

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: of like such fast cycling of life is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Is it just an accident of evolution

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: that viruses are so numerous?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Or is it a feature, not a bug?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So the fast is, it's not all fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Not all viruses are fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Some are 20 minutes per cycle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Some take weeks per cycle.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But that's just per second.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: There's so many viruses in the ocean

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: that that's what you get per second,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: no matter how fast the cycle is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But I look at it this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Viruses were probably the first organic entities

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: to evolve on the planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Long ago, billions, billion years ago,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: just as the earth cooled and organic molecules began to form,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I think these self, we call them self-replicators.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They're just short things that today would look like RNA,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: which is the basis of many viruses, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They evolved and they were able to replicate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Of course, they were just naked molecules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They had no protection.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And it was just RNA-based.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that's tough because RNA is pretty fragile in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And it probably didn't get very big as a consequence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But then proteins evolved, and I'm skipping like hundreds

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: of millions of years of evolution.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Proteins evolved, maybe without a cell, maybe with a cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But then to make a cell, there probably were some RNA-based

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: cells early on, but they were pretty simple.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But the cells that we know of today, even bacteria

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: and single-celled eukaryotes, they have very long DNA genomes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And you need a lot of DNA to make a complicated cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And so we think at some point, the RNA became DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And probably one of the earliest enzymes that arose

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: is the enzyme that could copy that RNA into DNA,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: which we now know today as reverse transcriptase,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: which my former boss, David Baltimore, and Howard Temin,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: co-discovered.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that enzyme arose and copied RNA to DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then you could build big cells because DNA can be

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: millions and millions of bases in length.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And RNA, the longest RNA we know of is 40,000 bases,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: not much bigger than the SARS-CoV-2.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: What would you say is the magic moment along that line?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I saw it was one or two billion, maybe three billion years

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: it took to go from bacteria to complex organism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It seems like Earth had a very long time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: like not a very long time without life,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: and then a very long time with very primitive life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Maybe I'm discriminating calling bacteria primitive life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah, people would object to you doing that for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But it seems like complex organism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: when it starts becoming something like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I don't know what's a good, not animal-like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: but more complexity than just like a single cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: What do you think is the magic there?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: What's the hardest thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: If you were trying to engineer Earth and build life

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: and build the simulations, obviously we're living in a video game,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: what this is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So if you're trying to build this video game,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: what's the hardest part along this evolution pathway?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So bacteria are mostly single cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They do make colonies, they get together in biofilms,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: which are really important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But they're all single bacteria in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And the key is making an organism where cells do different things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We have skin cells and eye cells and brain cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Bacteria never do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And the reason is probably energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Bacteria can't make enough energy to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And so there was another cell existing at the time, the archaea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And the idea is that a bacteria went into an archaea

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: and became the modern-day mitochondria,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: the energy factory of the cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that now led that cell develop into more and more

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: complicated organisms like we have today.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It was all about energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So the mitochondria, the energy, the mitochondria is the magic thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I think so.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's actually not my idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's Nick Jones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Have you heard of Nick Jones?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: He's an evolutionary biologist in the UK.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And he's done experimental work on this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And it's his idea that the defining point was the ability to make a lot of energy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: which a mitochondria can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's basically a whole bacteria inside of a bigger cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that becomes what we now call eukaryotes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that they can get more and more complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So let me bring you back to the viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I want to finish that story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah, which points of viruses come along?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So remember, we have these precellular, they're called precellular replicons.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And so we have a precellular stage where we have these self-replicating molecules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then cells arise.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then the self-replicating molecules invade the cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Why?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Because it's a hospitable environment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I mean, they didn't know that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They just went in and it turned out it was beneficial for them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So it stuck.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And they replicate inside the cell now where they have pools of everything they need.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They get more and more complicated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then they steal proteins from the cell to build a protective shell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then they can be released as virus particles.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They're now protected.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They can move from host to host.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And because they're at the earliest stages of cellular evolution,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: they can diversify to infect anything that arises.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that is why I think there's so many of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And everything on the planet is infected because the ancestor of everything was infected many years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So it's easier to steal than to build from scratch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So it's easier to sort of break into somebody else's thing and steal their proteins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: My colleague, Dixon de Pommier, calls viruses safe crackers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Safe crackers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So it's just from an evolutionary perspective, it's easier to steal because you can select.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But then you have to figure out mechanisms for stealing, for breaking into, for cracking the safe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Well, you don't have to figure out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It just happens, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Because molecules are so diverse that a molecule gets into a cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And if there's a protein that sticks to it, it's going to stick.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that gives an advantage.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: There's no planning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: There's no thinking about it, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It just happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We'll return to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But these numbers are crazy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So what, as these more complex organisms evolved, let's take us humans as an example.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Should we be afraid of these high numbers?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Should we be worried that there's so many viruses in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: To a certain extent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I mean, they have, it's twofold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They're good and bad, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Viruses are no, there's no question they can be bad.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We know that because they've infected and caused disease throughout history.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But we're also, you and I are full of viruses that don't hurt us at all and probably help us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And every organism is the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So they are clearly beneficial as a consequence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So I think, so every living thing on the planet has multiple viruses infecting everything you can see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And most of them I think we don't worry about because they can't infect us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They're unable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: In fact, now you can actually take your feces and send them to a company and they will sequence your viruses in your feces for you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Your fecal virome, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And the most common virus in human feces is a plant virus that infects peppers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's called pepper model mosaic virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that's because people eat a lot of peppers and it just passes right through you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Cabbage is full of viruses from the insects that walk on the cabbage in the fields.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We eat them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They just pass us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So I think most of the viruses we don't need to worry about except when we're talking about species that are closest to us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Mammals, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And I think the most numerous ones are the most concerning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They're viruses like bats.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Bats are 20% of mammals and rodents are 40% of mammals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And we humans live nearby, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And we know throughout history many viruses have come from bats and from rodents to people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: No question about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So there's a proximity in terms of just living together and a proximity genetically too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So it's more likely that a virus will jump from a bat and a rodent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And birds too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Birds can give us their viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: That's happened.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Influenza viruses come from birds mainly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So I think those are the three species.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Not species.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's higher than species, obviously.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But those are the three I would worry about in terms of getting their viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And we don't really know what's out there, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We have very little clue about what viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And I've for years wanted to capture wild mice in my backyard and see what viruses they have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Because no one knows.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And it's an easy...

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We can't ask them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So you mean map?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Like is there a way to...

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I can't ask them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: No, I would have to sacrifice them and take tissue and then bring it in the lab and do genome sequencing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So you can do a thorough sequencing to determine your viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Is there a sufficiently good categorization of viruses where you'd be...

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: That's a very good question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So whenever you do sequence, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You get some environmental sample and you extract nucleic acid and you sequence it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: What you do is you run it past the database.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: The gold standard is the GenBank database, which is maintained here in the US.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And you see if you get any hits.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then you can say, ah, look, this sequence is similar to this virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And you can classify all the viruses you see.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: The problem is 90% of your sequence is dark matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It doesn't hit with anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's probably a lot of it is unknown viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that's going to be hard to figure out because someone's going to have to go after it and sort it through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So yes, you can find a lot of viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And the numbers you get are astounding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You can find thousands of new viruses just by looking in various life forms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But there are many more that we don't pick up because they're not in the database.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Maybe this is a good time to take a quick tangent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: What do you think about Alpha Fold 2?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I don't know if you've been paying attention to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: With them DeepMind solving the protein folding problem and then also releasing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: first of all, open sourcing the code, which is for me as a software person that I love.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then second of all, also making like 300,000 predictions or something like that for different protein structures and releasing that data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So on the side of because you're saying there's dark matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Is there something?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: First, what are your general thoughts, level of excitement about their work?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And second, how can that be applied to viruses?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Do you think we'll be able to explore the dark matter of virology using machine learning?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Absolutely. Because in all this dark sequence, you can translate it and make a protein.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You can see what a protein looks like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It has what we call an open reading frame, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: A start and a stop.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And right now it's just a bunch of amino acids.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But if we could fold it, maybe the fold would be like something we already know.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Some protein fold, which gives you a lot of clues, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Because there are only so many protein folds in biology and that dark matter is probably one of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So I think that's very exciting because for years I followed structural biologists for years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And in the beginning, we couldn't even solve structures of viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They're too big. We could do small molecules like myoglobin.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: That was the first one done. It took years to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Then as computational power increased, then they could start to do viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But it took a long time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: X-ray crystallography depended on getting crystals of the virus, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And now we can do cryo-electron microscopy, which is much faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You could solve a spike of SARS-CoV-2 was solved in two months by Jason McClelland here in Austin, actually, at the beginning of the pandemic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But you're limited. You can't do huge proteins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You can only do moderately sized ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So, or actually, you can do viruses, but you can't do small proteins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So that's speeded it up, but it's still too fast to solve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You get a new protein, you want to solve its structure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So if we could predict it, and I know from talking to structural biologists, this has been their holy grail from day one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They want to be able to take a sequence of a protein, put it in a computer and have the structure put out without having to do all the experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So that's why this is very exciting that you can predict it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: That means it's not finished, obviously, and there's more to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But I think there will be a day where you could take any amino acid sequence and predict what it's going to look like.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: See, but aren't structural biologists going to get greedy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So once you have that, don't you want to go more complicated then?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Don't you want to go, because that's just the first step, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: To go from amino acids to the structure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And there's like multiple protein interactions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Like, how do you get to the virus?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Well, so that's what the ultimate goal of getting a structure is.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: That then you can do experiments and figure out what the structure means, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So many, in the old days, structural biology was a career in itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You worked with people who had a system and just solved proteins for them, and then you moved on to another one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You didn't really do any experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: The other people got to do all the interesting experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Now, young structural biologists are multifaceted.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They solve the structure and then they say, what happens if we change this amino acid?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Oh, look, it blocks binding to the receptor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: This must be the receptor binding interface.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So that's the exciting stuff, absolutely, is doing the experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I wonder if you can do some kinds of simulations of different proteins or multi-protein systems going to war against each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Like, to try to figure out, you know, reinforcement learning is used in AlphaZero, for example, to learn chess and Go.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that's using the self-play mechanism where the thing plays against itself and learns better and better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I wonder if you can simulate almost evolution in that way for primitive biological systems, have them in simulation, fight each other, and then see what comes out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Like, a super dangerous virus comes out or super like Chuck Norris type of thing that defends against the super dangerous virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And it's all in simulation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So an example would be we have all these variants of SARS-CoV-2 arising, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Which look to be selected by immune responses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But we know what amino acids are changing in the spike and how they block antibody binding.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You could simulate that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You could say, what is the antibody looking at?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Where antibodies bind on proteins are called epitopes, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You could map them all and change them in a simulation one by one and go back and forth between the antibody and the virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So all these evolution is what we call an arms race, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: The virus changes and then it evades the host and then the host can change.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: The host takes longer to change, though, unfortunately.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It takes geological time, but it can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then the virus can change and it can go back and forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And we can see evidence of this in genome sequences of both viruses and their hosts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And so you can take a protein in a host that is a receptor for multiple viruses and you can see all the impacts of virus pressure on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And you could simulate that for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that's just one thing that you could do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You could simulate changes in, say, an enzyme that makes it resistant to a drug and predict all the drug resistance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But the problem is people like me, the experimental virologists, don't know how to do any of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So we need to collaborate with people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I guess.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Oh, with other humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But with people from a field that we're not used to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I suppose people who would it be AI, I suppose?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah, machine learning people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Machine learning people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And you would say, look, this is the biological problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Is there a way we can use your tools to attack it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: The problem is those people are anti-social introverts that have a place like this and try to hide from other people in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Very difficult to find in the wild.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: OK, so outside of doing amazing, brilliant lectures online, you host and produce five, I would say, related podcasts,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: including my favorite This Week in Virology, also This Week in Parasitism, This Week in Microbiology, and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So you're a good person to ask, what are the categories of small things, small biological things in this world that can kill you, kill us humans?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Let's look.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You said like most viruses are friendly or at least not unfriendly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But let's look at the unfriendly ones in viruses and bacteria and those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: When you look at the full spectrum of things that can kill you, can you kind of paint a brief picture?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah, I think the big picture is that the things that can kill you are a minority of everything that's out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And we're talking about molecules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So we have in us proteins that can kill us, prions that are just a protein in us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And if it misfolds, it makes all of its other copies misfold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then you die of a neurological disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: That's pretty rare.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So there are proteins, there are viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And as I said, only certain ones can kill us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But even if we get those from animals, it's not straightforward.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: If you look at SARS-CoV-2, this is probably a once in a hundred year pandemic, I would say.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Equivalent to 1918 in its devastation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And in between there have been smaller pandemics of other viruses, but it doesn't happen all that often.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So we have a lot of viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We have a lot of bacteria of various sorts that can cause infections in us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And it's a limited number.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You're streptococci and staphylococci and clostridia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We could go on and on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But we know how to handle those as long as we have antimicrobials.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's just that we abuse them and we get resistance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So that can be a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Then we have fungi.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Not mushrooms, but much smaller fungi that multiply submicroscopic or just at the microscopic level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So those are the tiny guys.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then we have parasites, which we do this week in parasitism, where single cells, even worms of various sorts, can invade you and cause all sorts of problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Maybe a good place to start is what is a virus?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: That's great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I mean, I talk in my first lecture for 20 minutes before I get to that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And I wonder if I should put it up front, but it's kind of a boring definition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So if you do that first, people will turn off.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So first you tell them about all the millions and billions of viruses around.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So a virus, we have a very specific definition because it's different from everything else on the planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Because first of all, it's a parasite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: A parasite means you take something from someone else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We have human parasites who take money from others, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But in biological terms, a parasite takes something from the host that the host would otherwise use energy or some building block or something.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: There's never really a symbiotic relationship between a virus and a host.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Well, there can be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So that's the dichotomy, I think, is that we define them as parasites.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yet, I just told you 20 minutes ago that many viruses are probably beneficial.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So I think what it means is at some point we're going to have to change our definition, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Because after all, definitions we make are just constructs that make it easier for us to study,

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: that not necessarily represent what's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah, like Pluto was a planet at first and now it's not a planet anymore and a lot of people are very upset.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But it's only according to us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: There may be another race living somewhere else who thinks it's a planet, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Well, maybe that's why viruses are attacking humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They're very angry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They weren't calling them parasites.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So right now our definition includes parasite because a virus cannot do anything without a cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: If this mug were full of viruses, it would not do anything for years.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It would eventually probably lose its infectivity, but it's not going to reproduce here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It needs cells.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And to the first people who discovered viruses, that was astounding that they didn't just reproduce, divide on their own like bacteria.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So the virus needs to get inside of a cell, inside the cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It can't just hang around on the surface.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It needs to get in in order to make more of itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And so we call it an obligate intracellular parasite because it needs to get in a cell and then it takes things from the cell in the form of all kinds of molecules and processes and energy and so forth to make new viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Obligate means it's obligated to be inside the cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Absolutely. It will not reproduce outside of the cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So this mug of viruses can in no way be living in my opinion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: However, once it gets inside of a cell, now the cell is a virus infected cell.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's alive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So a virus, in my view, has two phases.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Right. It's this nonliving particulate phase that everyone is used to.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I'll send you. You need a virus for your table.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I'll send you a nice model.

body.input: I think it would look good here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yes, definitely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You don't have to go with all this other stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah. Well, these are all mechanical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: There's no biology here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So you wouldn't want a virus here?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: No, I'd want a virus, of course.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I'll send you one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I would love that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You can look at it because now that we have the three dimensional structures

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: solved by structural biologists, we take the coordinates and we put it in a 3D

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: printer and you can make amazing models of any virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And so there's a huge variety of viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Huge that we know of, which is only a fraction of what's out there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: What's the category?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So there's RNA, there's DNA viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: What are those?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: What's DNA and RNA?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Two broad categorizations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: RNA and these are genetic material.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Can be two different chemicals.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So RNA, everything else on the planet besides viruses is all DNA based.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You and I are DNA based.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Everything on the planet today is DNA based, except some viruses are RNA based.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And that's because, as I mentioned earlier, the first life that arose on the

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: planet was RNA based.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah, so these are like old school viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: These are old school.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: These are what we call relics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Relics, and this has got a name.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's called the RNA world, which I think is great.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Is it big still or are the relics dying out?

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Oh no, the relics in my opinion are the most successful viruses, the RNA viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And SARS-CoV-2 is an RNA virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We can talk about why they're so successful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But you have broadly speaking viruses with RNA, genetic information, which are relics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Of course, they're contemporary.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They have adapted to the modern world and the modern organisms living in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then we have DNA based viruses, which are extremely conservative and slow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They're very successful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: You know, everyone has a herpes virus infection, but they don't get the news like the RNA

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: viruses do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: The HIVs and the influenza viruses and the SARS-Coronaviruses, they get all the press

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: and they're RNA based because RNA lets you change more so than DNA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So they evolve much faster, the RNA viruses.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Much faster.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And in fact, when I have an electron evolution, I don't know if you've listened to that when

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: you should.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's really, I think it's really interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: RNA viruses exist at their error threshold, which means they can't make any more mutations

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: when they reproduce.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Otherwise, they're dead.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They would go extinct.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They're evolving at their error threshold.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: DNA viruses are hundreds of times lower than their error thresholds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And we know this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We can do an experiment to find that out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Now, why that is, is a good question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: But that's the reason why RNA viruses are far more successful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They infect many more hosts and they're very, I would say, slippery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: They can change hosts really quickly because in any animal harboring an RNA virus, like

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: The virus, the yeast cell wall is pretty hard to get through.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: It's just through so many years of evolution, you select something that works and it continues.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And what survives then goes on with perhaps a slightly different approach.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I love this idea of passive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: And then there's no free will.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: We're all just operating in the same way a cell does, but just a much higher level of complexity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: So I love the distinction between active and passive.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I mean, the point is I think anthropomorphizing to a certain extent is fine because it helps people understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: That's why I tell my students be careful about the anthropomorphizing because you're going to apply your values to a virus and you have different values.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: In both directions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

body.input: I actually one of the things that push back on is in the space of robotics, people, most people in robotics try to not anthropomorphize.

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216

metadata.title: Podcast: Vincent Racaniello: Viruses and Vaccines | Lex Fridman Podcast #216
