body.input: So if you know that a gene is related to disease,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: you don't wanna just know that it's related to the disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: You wanna know what is the disease mechanism

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: because you wanna go and intervene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So the way that I like to describe it

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: is that traditionally, epidemiology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: which is basically the study of disease,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: sort of the observational study of disease,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: has been about correlating one thing with another thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So if you have a lot of people with liver disease

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: who are also alcoholics, you might say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: well, maybe the alcoholism is driving the liver disease,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: or maybe those who have liver disease

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: self-medicate with alcohol.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So the connection could be either way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: With genetic epidemiology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: it's about correlating changes in genome

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: with phenotypic differences,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and then you know the direction of causality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So if you know that a particular gene

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: is related to the disease, you can basically say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: okay, perturbing that gene in mouse

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: causes the mice to have X-phenotype.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So perturbing that gene in human

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: causes the humans to have the disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So I can now figure out

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: what are the detailed molecular phenotypes

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: in the human that are related

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: to that organismal phenotype in the disease.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So it's all about understanding disease mechanism,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: understanding what are the pathways,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: what are the tissues, what are the processes

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that are associated with the disease

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: so that we know how to intervene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: You can then prescribe particular medications

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that also alter these processes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: You can prescribe lifestyle changes

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that also affect these processes, and so on and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: That's such a beautiful puzzle to try to solve.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Like what kind of perturbations

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: eventually have this ripple effect

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that leads to a disease across the population?

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: And then you study that for animals, a mice first,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and then see how that might possibly connect to humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: How hard is that puzzle of trying to figure out

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: how little perturbations might lead to,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: in a stable way, to a disease?

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: In animals, we make the puzzle simpler

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: because we perturb one gene at a time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: That's the beauty of it, it's the power of animal models.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: You can basically decouple the perturbations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: You only do one perturbation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and you only do strong perturbations at a time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: In human, the puzzle is incredibly complex

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: because, I mean, obviously you don't do

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: human experimentation, you wait for natural selection

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and natural genetic variation

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: to basically do its own experiments,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: which it has been doing for hundreds and thousands of years

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: in the human population, and for hundreds of thousands

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: of years across the history leading to the human population.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So you basically take this natural genetic variation

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that we all carry within us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Every one of us carries six million perturbations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So I've done six million experiments on you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: six million experiments on me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: six million experiments on everyone

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: of seven billion people on the planet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: What's the six million correspond to?

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Six million unique genetic variants

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that are segregating the human population.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Every one of us carries millions of polymorphic sites,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: polymanymorph forms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Polymorphic means many forms, variants.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: That basically means that every one of us

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: has single nucleotide alterations

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that we have inherited from mom and from dad

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that basically can be thought of

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: as tiny little perturbations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Most of them don't do anything,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: but some of them lead to all of the phenotypic differences

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that we see between us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: The reason why two twins are identical

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: is because these variants completely determine

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: the way that I'm gonna look at exactly 93 years of age.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: How happy are you with this kind of data set?

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Is it large enough of the human population of Earth?

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Is that too big, too small?

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Yeah, so is it large enough is a power analysis question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: And in every one of our grants,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: we do a power analysis based on what is the effect size

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that I would like to detect

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and what is the natural variation in the two forms.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So every time you do a perturbation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: you're asking, I'm changing form A into form B.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Form A has some natural phenotypic variation around it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and form B has some natural phenotypic variation around it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: If those variances are large

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and the differences between the mean of A

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and the mean of B are small,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: then you have very little power.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: The further the means go apart,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that's the effect size, the more power you have,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and the smaller the standard deviation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: the more power you have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So basically, when you're asking,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: is that sufficiently large?

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Certainly not for everything,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: but we already have enough power

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: for many of the stronger effects

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: in the more tight distributions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So that's a hopeful message

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that there exists parts of the genome

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that have a strong effect, that has a small variance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: That's exactly right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Unfortunately, those perturbations

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: but if we can figure out

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and help many other people better

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So I'm gonna explain it a little bit more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Why do we not have a connection between a gene

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and a disease, but we have a connection

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: between a genetic region and a disease?

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: The reason for that is that 93% of genetic variants

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that are associated with disease

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: don't impact the protein at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So if you look at the human genome, there's 20,000 genes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: There's 3.2 billion nucleotides.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Only 1.5% of the genome codes for proteins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: The other 98.5% does not code for proteins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: If you now look at where are the disease regions

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: located, 93% of them fall in that outside the gene's portion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Of course, genes are enriched,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: but they're only enriched by a factor of three.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: That means that still 93% of genetic variants

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: fall outside the proteins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Why is that difficult?

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Why is that a problem?

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: The problem is that when a variant falls outside the gene,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: you don't know what gene is impacted by that variant.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: You can't just say, oh, it's near this gene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: Let's just connect that variant to the gene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: And the reason for that is that the genome circuitry

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: is very often long range.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So you basically have that genetic variant

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that could sit in the intron of one gene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: And intron is sort of the place between the exons

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that code for proteins.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So proteins are split up into exons and introns,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and every exon codes for a particular subset of amino acids,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and together they're spliced together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: and then make the final protein.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So that genetic variant might be sitting

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: in an intron of a gene.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: It's transcribed with the gene,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: it's processed and then excised,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: but it might not impact this gene at all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: It might actually impact another gene

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: that's a million nucleotides away.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: So it's just riding along,

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: even though it has nothing to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: with this nearby neighborhood.

metadata.title: Podcast: Manolis Kellis: Biology of Disease | Lex Fridman Podcast #133

body.input: That's exactly right.

body.input: And now, let me leave you with some words

body.input: The following is a conversation with Doug Lennett, creator of Psych, a system that for close to 40

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: years and still today has sought to solve the core problem of artificial intelligence, the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: acquisition of common sense knowledge and the use of that knowledge to think, to reason, and to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: understand the world. To support this podcast, please check out our sponsors in the description.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: As a side note, let me say that in the excitement of the modern era of machine learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it is easy to forget just how little we understand exactly how to build the kind of intelligence

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that matches the power of the human mind. To me, many of the core ideas behind Psych, in some form,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: in actuality or in spirit, will likely be part of the AI system that achieves

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: general super intelligence. But perhaps more importantly, solving this problem of common

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: sense knowledge will help us humans understand our own minds, the nature of truth, and finally,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: how to be more rational and more kind to each other. This is the Lex Friedman Podcast,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and here is my conversation with Doug Lennett. Psych is a project launched by you in 1984

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and still is active today, whose goal is to assemble a knowledge base that spans the basic

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: concepts and rules about how the world works. In other words, it hopes to capture common sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: knowledge, which is a lot harder than it sounds. Can you elaborate on this mission and maybe perhaps

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: speak to the various sub-goals within this mission? When I was a faculty member in the computer

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: science department at Stanford, my colleagues and I did research in all sorts of artificial

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: intelligence programs, so natural language understanding programs, robots, expert systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and so on. And we kept hitting the very same brick wall. Our systems would have

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: impressive early successes. And so if your only goal was academic, namely to get enough material

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to write a journal article, that might actually suffice. But if you're really trying to get AI,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: then you have to somehow get past the brick wall. And the brick wall was the programs didn't have

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: what we would call common sense. They didn't have general world knowledge. They didn't really

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: understand what they were doing, what they were saying, what they were being asked.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: And so very much like a clever dog performing tricks, we could get them to do tricks, but they

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: never really understood what they were doing. Sort of like when you get a dog to fetch your

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: morning newspaper. The dog might do that successfully, but the dog has no idea what a newspaper is or what

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it says or anything like that. What does it mean to understand something? Can you maybe elaborate

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: in that a little bit? Is it is understand an action of like combining little things together,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: like through inference, or is understanding the wisdom you gain over time that forms a knowledge?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: I think of understanding more like a, think of it more like the ground you stand on, which

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: could be very shaky, could be very unsafe. But most of the time is not because underneath it is

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: more ground and eventually rock and other things. But layer after layer after layer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that solid foundation is there. And you rarely need to think about it. You rarely need to count

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: on it, but occasionally you do. And I've never used this analogy before, so bear with me. But

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: I think the same thing is true in terms of getting computers to understand things, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you ask a computer a question, for instance, Alexa or some robot or something, and maybe it gets the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: right answer. But if you were asking that of a human, you could also say things like, why,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: or how might you be wrong about this or something like that. And the person would answer you. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it might be a little annoying if you have a small child and they keep asking why questions in series,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: eventually you get to the point where you throw up your hands and say, I don't know, it's just the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: way the world is. But for many layers, you actually have that layered solid foundation of support so

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that when you need it, you can count on it. And when do you need it? Well, when things are unexpected,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: when you come up against a situation which is novel, for instance, when you're driving,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it may be fine to have a small program, a small set of rules that cover 99% of the cases, but that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: 1% of the time when something strange happens, you really need to draw on common sense. For instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: my wife and I were driving recently and there was a trash truck in front of us. And I guess they had

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: packed it too full and the back exploded and trash bags went everywhere. And we had to make a split

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: second decision, are we going to slam on our brakes? Are we going to swerve into another lane? Are we

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: going to just run it over? Because there were cars all around us. And in front of us was a large

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: trash bag and we know what we throw away in trash bags, probably not a safe thing to run over. Over

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: on the left was a bunch of fast food restaurant trash bags. And it's like, oh, well, those things

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: are just like styrofoam and leftover food. We'll run over that. And so that was a safe thing for

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: us to do. Now that's the kind of thing that's going to happen maybe once in your life. But the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: point is that there's almost no telling what little bits of knowledge about the world you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: might actually need in some situations which were unforeseen. But see, when you sit on that mountain

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: or that ground that goes deep of knowledge in order to make a split second decision about fast

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: food trash or random trash from the back of a trash truck, you need to be able to leverage that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: ground you stand on in some way. It's not enough to just have a lot of ground to stand on. It's

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: your ability to leverage it, to utilize it and integrate it all together to make that split

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: second decision. And I suppose understanding isn't just having common sense knowledge to access,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it's the act of accessing it somehow. Correctly filtering out the parts of the knowledge that are

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: not useful, selecting only the useful parts, and effectively making conclusive decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So let's tease apart two different tasks really, both of which are incredibly important and even

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: necessary if you're going to have this in a useful, usable fashion as opposed to say like library

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: books sitting on a shelf and so on where the knowledge might be there, but if a fire comes,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the books are going to burn because they don't know what's in them and they're just going to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: sit there while they burn. So there are two aspects of using the knowledge. One is a theoretical,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: how is it possible at all? And then the second aspect of what you said is how can you do it

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: quickly enough? So how can you do it at all is something that philosophers have grappled with,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and fortunately, philosophers a hundred years ago and even earlier developed a kind of formal

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: language like English. It's called predicate logic or first order logic or something like

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: predicate calculus and so on. So there's a way of representing things in this formal language which

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: enables a mechanical procedure to sort of grind through and algorithmically produce all of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: same logical entailments, all the same logical conclusions that you or I would from that same

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: set of pieces of information that are represented that way. So that sort of raises a couple questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: One is how do you get all this information from say observations and English and so on into this

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: logical form? And secondly, how can you then efficiently run these algorithms to actually

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: get the information you need in the case I mentioned in a tenth of a second rather than

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: say in ten hours or ten thousand years of computation? And those are both really important questions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: And like a corollary addition to the first one is how many such things do you need to gather for it

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to be useful in certain contexts? So like what in order, you mentioned philosophers, in order to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: capture this world and represent it in a logical way and with a formal logic, like how many

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: statements are required? Is it five? Is it ten? Is it ten trillion? Is it like that's, as far as I

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: understand, is probably still an open question. It may forever be an open question to say like

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: definitively about, to describe the universe perfectly. How many facts do you need?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: I guess I'm going to disappoint you by giving you an actual answer to your question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Okay. Well, no, this sounds exciting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Yes. Okay. So now we have like three things to talk about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: We'll keep adding more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Although it's okay. The first and the third are related. So let's leave the efficiency question

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: aside for now. So how does all this information get represented in logical form so that these

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: algorithms, resolution theorem proving and other algorithms can actually grind through

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: all the logical consequences of what you said? And that ties into your question about how many

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of these things do you need? Because if the answer is small enough, then by hand,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you could write them out one at a time. So in the early 1984, I held a meeting at Stanford where

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: I was a faculty member there where we assembled about half a dozen of the smartest people I know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: people like Alan Newell and Marvin Minsky and Alan Kay and a few others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Was Feynman there by chance? Because he commented about your system, Urisco, at the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: No, he wasn't part of this meeting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Okay. That's a heck of a meeting anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: I think Ed Feigenbaum was there. I think Josh Lederberg was there. So we have all these different

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: smart people and we came together to address the question that you raised, which is if it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: important to represent common sense knowledge and world knowledge in order for AIs to not be

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: brittle, in order for AIs not to just have the veneer of intelligence. Well, how many pieces of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: common sense, how many if-then rules, for instance, would we have to actually write in order to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: essentially cover what people expect perfect strangers to already know about the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: And I expected there would be an enormous divergence of opinion and computation,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: but amazingly everyone got an answer which was around a million. And one person got the answer

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: by saying, well, look, you can only burn into human long-term memory a certain number of things

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: per unit time, like maybe one every 30 seconds or something. And other than that, it's just short-term

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: memory and it flows away like water and so on. So by the time you're say 10 years old or so,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: how many things could you possibly have burned into your long-term memory? And it's like about

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: a million. Another person went in a completely different direction and said, well, if you look

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: at the number of words in a dictionary, not a whole dictionary, but for someone to essentially

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: be considered to be fluent in a language, how many words would they need to know? And then about how

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: many things about each word would you have to tell it? And so they got to a million that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Another person said, well, let's actually look at one single short one-volume desk encyclopedia

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: article. And so we'll look at what was like a four-paragraph article or something. I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: about grebes. Grebes are a type of waterfowl. And if we were going to sit there and represent

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: every single thing that was there, how many assertions or rules or statements would we have

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to write in this logical language and so on? And then multiply that by all of the number of articles

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that there were and so on. So all of these estimates came out with a million. And so if

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you do the math, it turns out that like, oh, well then maybe in something like a hundred person years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: in one or two person centuries, we could actually get this written down by hand. And a marvelous

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: coincidence, opportunity existed right at that point in time, the early 1980s. There was something

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: called the Japanese fifth generation computing effort. Japan had threatened to do in computing

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and AI and hardware what they had just finished doing in consumer electronics and the automotive

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: industry, namely, resting control away from the United States and more generally away from the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: West. And so America was scared and Congress did something. That's how you know it was a long time

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: ago because Congress did something. Congress passed something called the National Cooperative

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Research Act, NCRA. And what it said was, hey, all you big American companies, that's also how you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: know it was a long time ago because they were American companies rather than multinational

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: companies. Hey, all you big American companies, normally it would be an antitrust violation if

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you colluded on R&D, but we promise for the next 10 years, we won't prosecute any of you if you do

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that to help combat this threat. And so overnight, the first two consortia, research consortia in

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: America sprang up, both of them coincidentally in Austin, Texas, one called Semitech focusing

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: on hardware chips and so on. And then one called MCC, the Microelectronics and Computer Technology

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Corporation, focusing more on software, on databases and AI and natural language understanding and

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: things like that. And I got the opportunity thanks to my friend Woody Bledsoe, who was one of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: people who founded that, to come and be its principal scientist. And he sent Admiral Bob

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Inman, who was the person running MCC, came and talked to me and said, look, professor, you're

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: talking about doing this project, it's going to involve person centuries of effort. You've only

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: got a handful of graduate students, you do the math, it's going to take you longer than the rest of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: your life to finish this project. But if you move to the wilds of Austin, Texas, we'll put 10 times

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: as many people on it and you'll be done in a few years. And so that was pretty exciting. And so I

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: did that. I took my leave from Stanford, I came to Austin, I worked for MCC. And the good news and

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: bad news, the bad news is that all of us were off by an order of magnitude. That it turns out what

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you need are tens of millions of these pieces of knowledge about every day, sort of like if you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: have a coffee cup with stuff in it and you turn it upside down, the stuff in it's going to fall out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So you need tens of millions of pieces of knowledge like that, even if you take trouble to make each

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: one as general as it possibly could be. But the good news was that thanks to initially the fifth

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: generation effort and then later US government agency funding and so on, we were able to get

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: enough funding not for a couple person centuries of time, but for a couple person millennia of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: time, which is what we've spent since 1984, getting Psych to contain the tens of millions

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of rules that it needs in order to really capture and span sort of not all of human knowledge,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: but the things that you assume other people know, the things you count on other people knowing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: And so by now we've done that. And the good news is since you've waited 38 years just about to talk

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to me, we're about at the end of that process. So most of what we're doing now is not putting in

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: even what you would consider common sense, but more putting in domain specific applications,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: specific knowledge about healthcare in a certain hospital or about oil pipes getting clogged up

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: or whatever the applications happen to be. So we've almost come full circle and we're doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: things very much like the expert systems of the 1970s and the 1980s, except instead of resting on

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: nothing and being brittle, they're now resting on this massive pyramid, if you will, this massive

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: lattice of common sense knowledge so that when things go wrong, when something unexpected happens,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: they can fall back on more and more and more general principles, eventually bottoming out in

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: things like, for instance, if we have a problem with the microphone, one of the things you'll do

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: is unplug it, plug it in again and hope for the best, right? Because that's one of the general

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: pieces of knowledge you have in dealing with electronic equipment or software systems or

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: things like that. Is there a basic principle like that? Is it possible to encode something

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that generally captures this idea of turn it off and turn it back on and see if it fixes? Oh,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: absolutely. That's one of the things that Psych knows. That's actually one of the fundamental

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: laws of nature, I believe. I wouldn't call it a law. It's more like a... Seems to work every time,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: so it sure looks like a law. I don't know. So that basically covered the resources needed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: And then we had to devise a method to actually figure out, well, what are the tens of millions

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of things that we need to tell the system? And for that, we found a few techniques which worked

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: really well. One is to take any piece of text almost, it could be an advertisement, it could

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: be a transcript, it could be a novel, it could be an article. And don't pay attention to the actual

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: type that's there, the black space on the white page. Pay attention to the complement of that,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the white space, if you will. So what did the writer of this sentence assume that the reader

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: already knew about the world? For instance, if they used a pronoun, why did they think that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: would be able to understand what the intended referent of that pronoun was, if they used an

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: ambiguous word, how did they think that you would be able to figure out what they meant by that word?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: The other thing we look at is the gap between one sentence and the next one. What are all the things

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that the writer expected you to fill in and infer occurred between the end of one sentence

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and the beginning of the other? So like if the sentence says, Fred Smith robbed the third national

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: bank period, he was sentenced to 20 years in prison period. Well, between the first sentence

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and the second, you're expected to infer things like Fred got caught, Fred got arrested, Fred

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: went to jail, Fred had a trial, Fred was found guilty, and so on. If my next sentence starts

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: out with something like the judge, then you assume it's the judge at his trial. If my next sentence

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: starts out something like the arresting officer, you assume that it was the police officer who

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: arrested him after he committed the crime and so on. So those are two techniques for getting

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that knowledge. The other thing we sometimes look at is fake news or humorous onion headlines or

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: headlines in the weekly world news if you know what that is or the National Enquirer where it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: like, oh, we don't believe this, then we introspect on why don't we believe it. So there are things

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: like B-17 lands on the moon. It's like, what do we know about the world that causes us to believe

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that that's just silly or something like that? Or another thing we look for are contradictions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: things which can't both be true. And we say to like, what is it that we know that causes us to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: know that both of these can't be true at the same time? For instance, in one of the weekly

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: world news editions, in one article it talked about how Elvis was cited even though he was

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: getting on in years and so on. And another article in the same one talked about people

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: seeing Elvis's ghost. So it's like, why do we believe that at least one of these articles must

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: be wrong and so on? So we have a series of techniques like that that enable our people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: And by now we have about 50 people working full-time on this and have for decades. So

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: we've put in the thousands of person years of effort. We've built up these tens of millions

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of rules. We constantly police the system to make sure that we're saying things as generally as we

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: possibly can. So you don't want to say things like no mouse is also a moose because if you said

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: things like that, then you'd have to add another one or two or three zeros onto the number of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: assertions you'd actually have to have. So at some point we generalize things more and more and we

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: get to a point where we say, oh yeah, for any two biological taxons, if we don't know explicitly that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: one is a generalization of another, then almost certainly they're disjoint. A member of one is

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: not going to be a member of the other and so on. And the same thing with Elvis and the ghost. It

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: has nothing to do with Elvis. It's more about human nature and the mortality and that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Right. In general, things are not both alive and dead at the same time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Yeah. Unless special cats in theoretical physics examples.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Well, that raises a couple important points.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Well, that's the onion headline situation. Okay, sorry.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: But no, no. So what you bring up is this really important point of like, well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: how do you handle exceptions and inconsistencies and so on? And one of the hardest lessons for us to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: learn, it took us about five years to really grit our teeth and learn to love it, is we had to give

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: up global consistency. So the knowledge base can no longer be consistent. So this is a kind of scary

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: thought. I grew up watching Star Trek and anytime a computer was inconsistent, it would either freeze

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: up or explode or take over the world or something bad would happen. Or if you come from a mathematics

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: background, once you can prove false, you can prove anything. So that's not good and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So that's why the old knowledge-based systems were all very, very consistent. But the trouble is that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: by and large our models of the world, the way we talk about the world and so on, they're all sorts

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of inconsistencies that creep in here and there that will sort of kill some attempt to build some

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: enormous globally consistent knowledge base. And so what we had to move to was a system of local

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: consistency. So a good analogy is you know that the surface of the earth is more or less spherical

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: globally, but you live your life every day as though the surface of the earth were flat. When

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you're talking to someone in Australia, you don't think of them as being oriented upside down to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: When you're planning a trip, even if it's a thousand miles away, you may think a little

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: bit about time zones, but you rarely think about the curvature of the earth and so on. And for most

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: purposes, you can live your whole life without really worrying about that because the earth is

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: locally flat. In much the same way, the psych knowledge base is divided up into almost like

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: tectonic plates which are individual contexts. And each context is more or less consistent,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: but there can be small inconsistencies at the boundary between one context and the next one

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and so on. And so by the time you move say 20 contexts over, there could be glaring inconsistencies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So eventually you get from the normal modern real world context that we're in right now to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: something like road runner cartoon context where physics is very different. And in fact,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: life and death are very different because no matter how many times he's killed, the coyote

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: comes back in the next scene and so on. So that was a hard lesson to learn and we had to make sure

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that our representation language, the way that we actually encode the knowledge and represent it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: was expressive enough that we could talk about things being true in one context and false in

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: another. Things that are true at one time and false in another. Things that are true, let's say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: in one region like one country but false in another. Things that are true in one person's

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: belief system but false in another person's belief system. Things that are true at one level of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221
