body.input: abstraction and false at another. For instance, at one level of abstraction, you think of this

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: table as a solid object, but down at the atomic level, it's mostly empty space and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So then that's fascinating, but it puts a lot of pressure on context to do a lot of work. So you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: say tectonic plates, is it possible to formulate contexts that are general and big that do this

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: kind of capture of knowledge bases or do you then get turtles on top of turtles again where

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: there's just a huge number of contexts? So it's good you asked that question because

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you're pointed in the right direction, which is you want context to be first-class objects in your

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: system's knowledge base, in particular in psych's knowledge base. And by first-class object, I mean

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that we should be able to have psych think about and talk about and reason about one context or

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: another context the same way it reasons about coffee cups and tables and people and fishing

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and so on. And so context are just terms in its language just like the ones I mentioned. And so

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: psych can reason about context, context can arrange hierarchically and so on. And so you can say

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: things about let's say things that are true in the modern era, things that are true in a particular

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: year would then be a subcontext of the things that are true in a broad, let's say a century or a

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: millennium or something like that. Things that are true in Austin, Texas are generally going to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: a specialization of things that are true in Texas, which is going to be a specialization of things

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that are true in the United States and so on. And so you don't have to say things over and over

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: again at all these levels, you just say things at the most general level that it applies to. And you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: only have to say it once and then it essentially inherits to all these more specific contexts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: To ask a slightly technical question, is this inheritance a tree or a graph?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Oh, you definitely have to think of it as a graph. So we could talk about, for instance,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: why the Japanese fifth generation computing effort failed. There were about half a dozen

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: different reasons. One of the reasons they failed was because they tried to represent knowledge as

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: a tree rather than as a graph. And so each node in their representation could only have one parent

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: node. So if you had a table that was a wooden object, a black object, a flat object, you have

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to choose one and that's the only parent it could have. When of course, depending on what it is you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: need to reason about it, sometimes it's important to know that it's made out of wood, like if we're

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: talking about a fire, sometimes it's important to know that it's flat if we're talking about resting

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: something on it and so on. So one of the problems was that they wanted a kind of dewy decimal

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: numbering system for all of their concepts, which meant that each node could only have at most 10

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: children and each node could only have one parent. And while that does enable the dewy decimal type

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: numbering of concepts, labeling of concepts, it prevents you from representing all the things you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: need to about objects in our world. And that was one of the things which they never were able to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: overcome and I think that was one of the main reasons that that project failed. So we'll return

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to some of the doors you've opened, but if we can go back to that room in 1984 around there with

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Marvin Minsky and Stanford. By the way, I should mention that Marvin wouldn't do his estimate until

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: someone brought him an envelope so that he could literally do a back of the envelope calculation

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to come up with his number. Well, because I feel like the conversation in that room is an important

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: one. You know, this is how sometimes science is done in this way. A few people get together and

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: plant the seed of ideas and they reverberate throughout history and some kind of dissipate

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and disappear and some Drake equation and it seems like a meaningless equation, somewhat

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: meaningless, but I think it drives and motivates a lot of scientists. And when the aliens finally

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: show up, that equation will get even more valuable because then we'll be able to, in the long arc of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: history, the Drake equation will prove to be quite useful, I think. And in that same way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: a conversation of just how many facts are required to capture the basic common sense

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: knowledge of the world. That's a fascinating question. I want to distinguish between what you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: think of as facts and the kind of things that we represent. So we map to and essentially make sure

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that psych has the ability to, as it were, read and access the kind of facts you might find, say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: in Wikidata or stated in a Wikipedia article or something like that. So what we're representing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the things that we need a small number of tens of millions of are more like rules of thumb,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: rules of good guessing, things which are usually true and which help you to make sense of the facts

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that are sitting off in some database or some other more static storage. So they're almost

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: like platonic forms. So when you read stuff on Wikipedia, that's going to be projections

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of those ideas. You read an article about the fact that Elvis died, that's a projection of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the idea that humans are mortal. Very few Wikipedia articles will write humans are mortal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: CB Exactly. That's what I meant about ferreting out the unstated things in text. What are all

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the things that were assumed? And so those are things like if you have a problem with something,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: turning it off and on often fixes it for reasons we don't really understand and we're not happy

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: about. Or people can't be both alive and dead at the same time. Or water flows downhill. If you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: search online for water flowing uphill and water flowing downhill, you'll find more references for

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: water flowing uphill because it's used as a kind of a metaphorical reference for some unlikely

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: thing because of course everyone already knows that water flows downhill. So why would anyone

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: bother saying that? RL Do you have a word you prefer? Because we said facts isn't the right

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: word. Is there a word like concepts? CB I would say assertions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: RL Assertions. CB Assertions or rules. Because I'm not talking about rigid rules,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: but rules of thumb. But assertions is a nice one that covers all of these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: RL Yeah. As a programmer to me, assert has a very dogmatic authoritarian feel to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: CB Oh, I'm sorry. RL I'm so sorry. Okay, but assertions works. Okay. So if we go back to that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: room with Marvin Minsky with you, all these seminal figures, Ed, Fagim, thinking about this

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: very philosophical but also engineering question, we can also go back a couple of decades before

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: then and thinking about artificial intelligence broadly when people were thinking about how do

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you create superintelligence systems, general intelligence. And I think people's intuition

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: was off at the time. And I mean, this continues to be the case that when we're grappling with

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: these exceptionally difficult ideas, it's very difficult to truly understand ourselves. When

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: we're thinking about the human mind, to introspect how difficult it is to engineer intelligence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to solve intelligence, we're not very good at estimating that. And you are somebody who has

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: really stayed with this question for decades. What's your sense from 1984 to today? Have you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: gotten a stronger sense of just how much knowledge is required? So you've kind of said with some

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: level of certainty that it's still on the order of magnitude of tens of millions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: RL Right. For the first several years, I would have said that it was on the order of one or

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: two million. And so it took us about five or six years to realize that we were off by a factor of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: 10. RL But I guess when I'm asking, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Marvin Misk is very confident in the 60s. What's your sense? If you, you know, 200 years from now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you're still, you know, you're not going to be any longer in this particular biological body,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: but your brain will still be in the digital form. And you'd be looking back, would you think you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: were smart today? Like your intuition was right? Or do you think you may be really off?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: RL So I think I'm, I'm right enough. And let me explain what I mean by that, which is sometimes

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: like if you have an old fashioned pump, you have to prime the pump and then eventually it starts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So I think I'm, I'm right enough in the sense that what we've built, even if it isn't, so to speak,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: everything you need, it's primed the knowledge pump enough that psych can now itself help to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: learn more and more automatically on its own by reading things and understanding and occasionally

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: asking questions like a student would or something, and by doing experiments and discovering things

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: on its own and so on. So through a combination of psych powered discovery and psych powered reading,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it will be able to bootstrap itself. Maybe it's the final 2%, maybe it's the final 99%. So even

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: if I'm wrong, all I really need to build is a system which has primed the pump enough that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it can begin that cascade upward, that self-reinforcing sort of quadratically or maybe even exponentially

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: increasing path upward that we get from, for instance, talking with each other. That's why

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: humans today know so much more than humans 100,000 years ago. We're not really that much smarter than

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: people were 100,000 years ago, but there's so much more knowledge and we have language and we can

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: communicate, we can check things on Google and so on. So effectively we have this enormous power at

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: our fingertips and there's almost no limit to how much you could learn if you wanted to because

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you've already gotten to a certain level of understanding of the world that enables you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to read all these articles and understand them, that enables you to go out and if necessary,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: do experiments, all of that slower as a way of gathering data and so on. And I think this is

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: really an important point which is if we have artificial intelligence, real general artificial

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: intelligence, human level artificial intelligence, then people will become smarter. It's not so much

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that it'll be us versus the AIs, it's more like us and the AIs together will be able to do things

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that require more creativity that would take too long right now, but we'll be able to do lots of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: things in parallel. We'll be able to misunderstand each other less. There's all sorts of value that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: effectively for an individual would mean that individual will for all intents and purposes be

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: smarter. And that means that humanity as a species will be smarter. And when was the last time that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: any invention qualitatively made a huge difference in human intelligence? You have to go back a long

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: ways. It wasn't like the internet or the computer or mathematics or something. It was all the way

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: back to the development of language. We sort of look back on pre-linguistic cavemen as well. They

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: weren't really intelligent, were they? They weren't really human, were they? And I think that as you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: said, 50, 100, 200 years from now, people will look back on people today right before the advent

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of these sort of lifelong general AI uses and say, you know, those poor people, they weren't really

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: human, were they? Exactly. So you said a lot of really interesting things. By the way, I would

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: maybe try to argue that the internet is on the order of the kind of big leap in improvement that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the invention of language was. Well, it's certainly a big leap in one direction. We're not sure whether

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it's upward or downward. Well, I mean, very specific parts of the internet, which is access

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to information like a website like Wikipedia, like ability for human beings from across the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: world to access information so very quickly. So I could take either side of this argument. And

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: since you just took one side, I'll give you the other side, which is that almost nothing has done

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: more harm than something like the internet and access to that information in two ways. One is,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: for. And what it did was it took GWAS's genome-wide association studies. Those are big databases

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of patients that came into a hospital. They got their DNA sequenced because the cost of doing that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: has gone from infinity to billions of dollars to a hundred dollars or so. And so now patients

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: routinely get their DNA sequenced. So you have these big databases of the SNPs, the single

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: nucleotide polymorphisms, the point mutations in a patient's DNA, and the disease that happened to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: bring them into the hospital. So now you can do correlation studies, machine learning studies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of which mutations are associated with and led to which physiological problems and diseases and so

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: on, like getting arthritis and so on. And the problem is that those correlations turn out to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: be very spurious. They turn out to be very noisy. Very many of them have led doctors onto wild goose

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: chases and so on. And so they wanted a way of eliminating or the bad ones are focusing on the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: good ones. And so this is where psych comes in, which is psych takes those sort of A to Z

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: correlations between point mutations and the medical condition that needs treatment. And we say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: okay, let's use all this public knowledge and common sense knowledge about what reactions occur

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: where in the human body, what polymerizes what, what catalyzes what reactions and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: And let's try to put together a 10 or 20 or 30 step causal explanation of why that mutation might

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: have caused that medical condition. And so psych would put together in some sense some Rube Goldberg

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: like chain that would say, oh yeah, that mutation if it got expressed would be this altered protein,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: which because of that, if it got to this part of the body would catalyze this reaction. And by the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: way, that would cause more bioactive vitamin D in the person's blood. And anyway, 10 steps later,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that screws up bone resorption and that's why this person got osteoporosis early in life and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So that's human interpretable or at least doctor human interpretable.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Exactly. And the important thing even more than that is you shouldn't really trust that 20 step

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Rube Goldberg chain any more than you trust that initial A to Z correlation, except two things. One,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: if you can't even think of one causal chain to explain this, then that correlation probably was

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: just noise to begin with. And secondly, and even more powerfully, along the way that causal chain

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: will make predictions like the one about having more bioactive vitamin D in your blood. So you

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: can now go back to the data about these patients and say, by the way, did they have slightly

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: elevated levels of bioactive vitamin D in their blood and so on. And if the answer is no, that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: strongly disconfirms your whole causal chain. And if the answer is yes, that somewhat confirms

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that causal chain. And so using that, we were able to take these correlations from this GWAS database

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and we were able to essentially focus the researchers' attention on the very small

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: percentage of correlations that had some explanation and even better, some explanation

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that also made some independent prediction that they could confirm or disconfirm by looking at

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the data. So think of it like this kind of synergy where you want the right brain machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to quickly come up with possible answers. You want the left brain psych-like AI to think about that

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and think about why that might have been the case and what else would be the case if that were true

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and so on. And then suggest things back to the right brain to quickly check out again. So it's

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that kind of synergy back and forth, which I think is really what's going to lead to general AI, not

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: narrow, brittle machine learning systems and not just something like psych.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Okay. So that's a brilliant synergy. But I was also thinking in terms of the automated expansion

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of the knowledge base, you mentioned NLU. This is very early days in the machine learning space of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: this, but self-supervised learning methods. You have these language models, GPT-3 and so on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that just read the internet and they form representations that can then be mapped to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: something useful. The question is, what is the useful thing? They're now playing with a pretty

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: cool thing called Open AI Codex, which is generating programs from documentation. Okay. That's kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: useful. It's cool. But my question is, can it be used to generate in part maybe with some human

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: supervision, a psych-like assertions, help feed psych more assertions from this giant body of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: internet data? Yes. That is in fact, one of our goals is how can we harness machine learning? How

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: can we harness natural language processing to increasingly automate the knowledge acquisition

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: process, the growth of psych? And that's what I meant by priming the pump, that if you learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: things at the fringe of what you know already, you learn this new thing is similar to what you know

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: already and here are the differences in the new things you had to learn about it and so on. So

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the more you know, the more and more easily you can learn new things. But unfortunately, inversely,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: if you don't really know anything, then it's really hard to learn anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: And so if you're not careful, if you start out with too small sort of a core to start this process,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it never really takes off. And so that's why I view this as a pump priming exercise to get a big

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: enough manually produced, even though that's kind of ugly duckling technique, put in the elbow grease

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to produce a large enough core that you will be able to do all the kinds of things you're imagining

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: without sort of ending up with the kind of wacky brittlenesses that we see, for example, in GPT-3

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: where you'll tell it a story about someone plotting to poison someone and so on. And then

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: GPT-3 says, oh, you say, what's the very next sentence? The next sentence is, oh yeah,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that person then drank the poison they just put together. It's like that's probably not what

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: happened for someone. Or if you go to Siri and I think I have, where can I go for help with my

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: alcohol problem or something? It'll come back and say, I found seven liquor stores near you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So it's one of these things where, yes, it may be helpful most of the time. It may even be correct

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: most of the time. But if it doesn't really understand what it's saying and if it doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: really understand why things are true and doesn't really understand how the world works,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: then some fraction of the time it's going to be wrong. Now, if your only goal is to sort of find

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: relevant information like search engines do, then being right 90% of the time is fantastic.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: That's unbelievably great. However, if your goal is to save the life of your child who

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: has some medical problem or your goal is to be able to drive for the next 10,000 hours of driving

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: without getting into a fatal accident and so on, then error rates down at the 10% level or even

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the 1% level are not really acceptable. I like the model of when that learning happens at the edge

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and then you kind of think of knowledge as this sphere. So if you want a large sphere because the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: learning is happening on the surface. Exactly. So what you can learn next increases

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: quadratically as the diameter of that sphere goes up. It's nice because you think when you know

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: nothing, it's like you can learn anything, but the reality, not really. Right. If you know nothing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you can really learn nothing. You can appear to learn. So also, one of the anecdotes I could go

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: back and give you about why I feel so strongly about this personally was in 1980, 81, my daughter

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Nicole was born and she's actually doing fine now, but when she was a baby, she was diagnosed as

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: having meningitis and doctors wanted to do all these scary things. And my wife and I were very

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: worried and we could not get a meaningful answer from her doctors about exactly why they believed

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: this, what the alternatives were and so on. And fortunately, a friend of mine, Ted Shortliffe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: was another assistant professor in computer science at Stanford at the time. And he'd been

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: building a program called MISON, which was a medical diagnosis program that happened to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: specialize in blood infections like meningitis. And so he had privileges at Stanford Hospital

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: because he was also an MD. And so we got hold of her chart and we put in her case and it came up

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: with exactly the same diagnoses and exactly the same therapy recommendations. But the difference

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: was because it was a knowledge-based system, a rule-based system, it was able to tell us step

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: by step by step why this was the diagnosis and step by step why this was the best therapy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the best procedure to do for her and so on. And there was a real epiphany because that made all

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: the difference in the world. Instead of blindly having to trust in authority, we were able to

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: understand what was actually going on. And so at that time, I realized that that really is what was

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: missing in computer programs was that even if they got things right, because they didn't really

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: understand the way the world works and why things are the way they are, they weren't able to give

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: explanations of their answer. And it's one thing to use a machine learning system that says,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: I think you should get this operation and you say why and it says 0.83 and you say no,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: in more detail why and it says 0.831. That's not really very compelling and that's not really

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: very helpful. There's this idea of the semantic web that when I first heard about, I just fell in

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: love with the idea. It was the obvious next step for the internet. And maybe you can speak about

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: what is the semantic web, what are your thoughts about it, how your vision and mission and goals

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: with psych are connected, integrated. Are they dance partners? Are they aligned? What are your

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: thoughts there? So think of the semantic web as a kind of knowledge graph and Google already has

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: something they call knowledge graph, for example, which is sort of like a node and link diagram.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So you have these nodes that represent concepts or words or terms and then there are some arcs

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that connect them that might be labeled. And so you might have a node with one person that represents

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: one person and let's say a husband link that then points to that person's husband. And so there'd be

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: then another link that went from that person labeled wife that went back to the first node

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: and so on. So having this kind of representation is really good if you want to represent binary

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: relations, essentially relations between two things. And so if you have the equivalent of

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: like three-word sentences, like Fred's wife is Wilma or something like that, you can represent

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that very nicely using these kinds of graph structures or using something like the semantic

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: web and so on. But the problem is that very often what you want to be able to express

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: takes a lot more than three words and a lot more than simple graph structures like that to represent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So for instance, if you've read or seen Romeo and Juliet, I could say to you something like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: remember when Juliet drank the potion that put her into a kind of suspended animation?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: When Juliet drank that potion, what did she think that Romeo would think that Romeo would think

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: when he heard from someone that she was dead? And you could basically understand what I'm saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: you could understand the question, you could probably remember the answer was, well,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: she thought that this friar would have gotten a message to Romeo saying that she was going to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: this, but the friar didn't. So you're able to represent and reason with these much, much,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: much more complicated expressions that go way, way beyond what simple three, as it were, three word

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: or four word English sentences are, which is really what the semantic web can represent and

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: really what knowledge graphs can represent. If you could step back for a second,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: because it's funny you went into specifics and maybe you can elaborate, but I was also referring

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to semantic web as the vision of converting data on the internet into something that's interpretable,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: understandable by machines. Oh, of course, at that level.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: So I would say that what is the semantic web? I mean, you could say a lot of things, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it might not be obvious to a lot of people when they do a Google search that just like you said,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: while there might be something that's called a knowledge graph, but it's not always the same.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: It's not always the same. It's just a much more complex knowledge graph.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: It's really boils down to keyword search ranked by the quality estimate of the website, integrating

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: previous human based Google searches and what they thought was useful. It's like some weird combination

body.input: beautiful idea, surprising idea about Psych to you? When I look up at the stars, I kind of want like

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: that amazement you feel that wow, and you are a part of creating one of the greatest, one of the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: most fascinating efforts in artificial intelligence history. So which element brings you personally joy?

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: history that anyone ever has to teach a computer this particular thing that we're now teaching.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: It's like painting starry night. You only have to do that once or creating the Pieta. You only

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: have to do that once. It's not like a singer who has to keep, it's not like Bruce Springsteen having

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: to sing his greatest hits over and over again at different concerts. It's more like a painter

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: creating a work of art once and then that's enough. It doesn't have to be created again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: And so I really get the sense of we're telling the system things that it's useful for it to know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: it's useful for a computer to know, for an AI to know. And if we do our jobs right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: when we do our jobs right, no one will ever have to do this again for this particular piece

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: of knowledge. It's very, very exciting. Yeah, I guess there's a sadness to it too.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: a number of children and a lot of parents get to experience that joy of teaching. With AI systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: at least the current constructions they remember. You don't get to experience the joy of teaching

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: a machine millions of times. Better come work for us before it's too late then.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: That's a good hiring pitch. Yeah, it's true. But then there's also, it's a project that continues

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: forever in some sense, just like Wikipedia. Yes, you get to a stable base of knowledge,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: but knowledge grows, knowledge evolves. We learn as a human species, as science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: as an organism constantly grows and evolves and changes and then empower that with the

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: tools of artificial intelligence and that's going to keep growing and growing and growing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: Many of the assertions that you held previously may need to be significantly expanded, modified,

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: all those kinds of things. It could be like a living organism versus the analogy I think

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: we started this conversation with, which is like the solid ground.

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: The other beautiful experience that we have with our system is when it asks clarifying

metadata.title: Podcast: Douglas Lenat: Cyc and the Quest to Solve Common Sense Reasoning in AI | Lex Fridman Podcast #221

body.input: questions, which inadvertently turn out to be emotional to us. So at one point it knew
