metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's like nobody is good enough to avoid ever shooting themselves in the foot with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You write enough C code, you're going to shoot yourself in the foot.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And garbage collection is a very great thing for the vast majority of programs.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's only when you get into the tightest of real time things that you start saying it's like, no, the garbage collection has more costs than it has benefits for me there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But that's not 99 plus percent of all the software in the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So JavaScript is not terrible in those ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And I am and so much of programming is not the language itself.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's the infrastructure around every that surrounds it, all the libraries that you can get and the different stuff that you can ways you can deploy it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I am the portability that it gives you.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And JavaScript is really strong on a lot of those things where for a long time and it still does if I look at it, the web stack about everything that has to go when you do something really trivial in JavaScript and it shows up on a web browser to kind of X ray through that and see everything that has to happen for your one little JavaScript.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Statement to turn into something visible in your web browser.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's very, very disquieting.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Just the depth of that stack and the fact that so few people can even comprehend all of the levels that are going on there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But it's again, I have to caution myself to not be the in the good old days old man about it because clearly there's enormous value here.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: The world does run on JavaScript to a pretty good approximation there and it's not falling apart.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There's a bunch of scary stuff where you look at console logs and you just see all of these bad things that are happening, but it's still kind of limping along and nobody really notices.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But so much of my systems design and systems analysis goes around.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You should understand what the speed of light is like what would be the best you could possibly do here.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it sounds horrible, but in a lot of cases you can be a thousand times off your speed of light velocity for something and it's still be OK.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And in fact, it can even sometimes still be the optimal thing in a larger system standpoint where there's a lot of things that you don't want to have to parachute in someone like me to go in and say,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: make this this web page run a thousand times faster, make this web app into a hardcore native application that starts up in 37 milliseconds and everything responds in less than one frame latency.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That's just not necessary.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And if somebody wants to go pay me millions of dollars to do software like that when they can take somebody right out of a boot camp and say, spin up an application for this.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Often being efficient is not really the best metric.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's like there's that applies in a lot of areas where it's kind of interesting how a lot of our appliances and everything are all built around energy efficiency,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: sometimes at the expense of robustness in some other ways or higher costs in other ways where there's interesting things where energy or electricity could become much cheaper in a future world.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And that could change our engineering tradeoffs for the way we build certain things where you could throw away efficiency and actually get more benefits that actually matter.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That's one of my you know, I one of the directions I was considering swerving into was nuclear energy when I was kind of like, what do I want to do next?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It was either going to be cost effective nuclear fission or artificial general intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And one of the one of my pet ideas there is like, you know, people don't understand how cheap nuclear fuel is.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And there would be ways that I you could be a quarter the efficiency or less.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But if it wound up making your plant ten times cheaper, that could be a radical innovation in something like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So there's like some of these thoughts around like direct fission for energy conversion, fission fragment conversion that, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: maybe you build something that doesn't require all the steam turbines and everything, even if it winds up being less efficient.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So that applies a lot in programming where there's always it's always good to know what you could do if you really sat down and took it took it far.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Because sometimes there's discontinuities like around user reaction times.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There are some points where the difference between operating in one second and 750 milliseconds, not that huge.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You'll see it in Web page statistics, but most of the usability stuff, not that great.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But if you get down to 50 milliseconds, then all of a sudden this just feels amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You know, it's just like doing your bidding instantly rather than you're giving it a command, twiddling your thumbs, waiting for it to respond.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So sometimes it's important to really crunch hard to get over some threshold.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But there are there are broad basins in the value metric for lots of work where it just doesn't pay to even go that extra mile.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And there are craftsmen that, you know, they just don't want to buy that and more power to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You know, if somebody just wants to say, no, I'm going to be my pride is in my work.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I'm never going to do something that's not as good as I could possibly make it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I respect that. And sometimes I am that person.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But I try to focus more on the larger value picture.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you do pick your battles and you deploy your resources in the play that's going to give you sort of the best user value in the end.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Well, if you look at the evolution of life on Earth as a kind of programming effort, it's it seems like efficiency isn't the thing that's being optimized for.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Like natural selection is very inefficient, but it kind of adapts and through the process of adaptations, building more and more complex systems that are more and more intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: The final result is kind of pretty interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And so I think of JavaScript the same way.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's like this giant mess that, you know, things naturally die off if they don't work and they if they if they're become useful to people, they kind of naturally live.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And then you build this community, large community of people that are generating code and some code is sticky.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Some is not. And nobody knows the the inefficiencies of the efficiencies or the breaking points like how reliable this code is.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you kind of just run it, assume it works and then get unpleasantly surprised.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And then that's very kind of the evolutionary process.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So that's a really good analogy.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And we can go a lot of places with that, where in the earliest days of programming, when you had finite, you could count the bytes that you had to work on this.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You had all the kind of hackers playing code golf to be one less instruction than the other person's multiply routine to kind of get through.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it was so perfectly crafted.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It was a crystal piece of artwork when you had a program because there just were not that many.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You couldn't afford to be lazy in different ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And in many ways, I see that as akin to the symbolic A.I. work, where, again, if you did not have the resources to just say, well, we're going to do billions and billions of programmable weights here,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you have to turn it down into something that is symbolic and crafted like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But that's definitely not the way DNA and life and biological evolution and things work.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: On the one hand, it's almost humbling how little programming code is in our bodies.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: We've got a couple billion base pairs and it's like this all fits on a thumb drive for years now.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And then our brains are even a smaller section of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You've got maybe 50 megabytes. And this is not like Shannon limit perfectly information dense conveyances here.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's like these are messy codes.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You know, they're broken up into amino acids.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: A lot of them don't do important things or they do things in very awkward ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But it is this process of just accumulation on top of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you need you need scale, both you need scale for sort of the population for that to work out.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And in the early days in the 50s and 60s, the kind of ancient era of computers where you could count when they said,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: like when the Internet started, even in the 70s, they were like 18 hosts or something on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It was this small, finite number.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you were still optimizing everything to be as good as you possibly could be.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But now it's billions and billions of devices and everything going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you can have this very much natural evolution going on where lots of things are tried,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: lots of things are blowing up, venture capitalists lose their money.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I when a startup invested in the wrong tech stack and things completely failed or failed to scale.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But you know, but good things do come out of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's interesting to see the the mimetic evolution of the way different things happen,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: like mentioning Hello World at the beginning.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's funny how some little thing like that where everybody, every programmer knows Hello World now.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And that was a completely arbitrary sort of decision that just came out of the dominance of Unix and C and early examples of things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So millions of experiments are going on all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But some things do kind of rise to the top and win the fitness war for whether it's mind space or programming techniques or anything like there's a site on stack exchange called CodeGolf

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where people compete to write the shortest possible program for a particular task in all the different kinds of languages.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's really interesting to see folks kind of their masters of their craft really play with the limits of programming languages.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's really beautiful to see.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And across all the different programming languages, you get to see some of these weird programming languages and mainstream ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You get to see the difference between Python two and three.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You get to see the difference between C and C++ and Java.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You get to see JavaScript, all of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's kind of inspiring to see how much depth of possibility there is within programming languages that CodeGolf kind of tasks reveal.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Most of us, if you do any kind of programming, you kind of do boring kind of very vanilla type of code. That's the way to build large systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But it's nice to see that the possibility of creative genius is still within those languages.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's laden within those languages.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So given that given that you are once again one of the greatest programmers ever, what do you think makes a good programmer, maybe a good modern programmer?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Well, I just gave a long rant slash lecture at Meta to the TPM organization.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And my biggest point was everything that we're doing really should flow from user value, all the good things that we're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's like we're not technical people.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's like you shouldn't be taking pride just in the specific thing like CodeGolf is the sort of thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's a fun puzzle game, but that really should not be a major motivator for you.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's like we're solving problems for people or we're providing entertainment to people.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: We're doing something of value to people that's displacing something else in their life.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So we want to be providing a net value over what they could be doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But instead, they're choosing to use our products.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And that's where I mean, it sounds trite or corny, but I fundamentally do think that's how you make the world a better place.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: If you have given more value to people than it took you and your team to create, then the world's a better place.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: People have gone from something of lesser value, chosen to use your product, and their life feels better for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And if you've produced that economically, that's a really good thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: On the other hand, if you spent ridiculous amounts of money, you've just kind of shoveled a lot of cash into a woodchipper there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you should maybe not feel so good about what you're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So being proud about a specific architecture or specific technology or a specific code sequence that you've done,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: it's great to get a little smile, like a tiny little dopamine hit for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But the top level metric should be that you're building things of value.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Now, you can get into the argument about what is user value?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: How do you actually quantify that?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And there can be big arguments about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But it's easy to be able to say, OK, this pissed off user there is not getting value from what you're doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: This user over there with the big smile on their face, the moment of delight when something happened, there's a value that's happened there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean, you have to at least accept that there is a concept of user value.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Even if you have trouble exactly quantifying it, you can usually make relative arguments about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Well, this was better than this. We've improved things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So being a servant to the user is your job when you're a developer.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You want to be producing something that other people are going to find valuable.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And if you are technically inclined, then finding the right levers to be able to pull,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to be able to make a design that's going to produce the most value for the least amount of effort.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it always has to be kind of divided.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There's a ratio there where it's a problem at the big tech companies,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: whether it's MetaGoogle, Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, companies that have almost infinite money.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean, I know their CFO will complain that it's not infinite money, but from most developers' standpoints, it really does feel like it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's almost counterintuitive that if you're working hard as a developer on something, there's always this thought,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: if only I had more resources, more people, more RAM, more megahertz, then my product will be better.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And that sense that at certain points, it's certainly true that if you are really hamstrung by this,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: removing an obstacle will make a better product, make more value.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But if you're not making your core design decisions in this fiercely competitive way where you're saying feature A or feature B,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you can't just say, let's do both, because then you're not making a value judgment about them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You're just saying, well, they both seem good.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You don't want to necessarily have to pick out which one is better or how much better and tell team B that,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: sorry, we're not going to do this because A is more important.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But that notion of always having to really critically value what you're doing, your time, the resources you expend,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: even the opportunity cost of doing something else, that's super important.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Well, let me ask you about the big debates that you're mentioning of how to measure value.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Is it possible to measure it kind of numerically?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Or can you do the sort of Johnny Ive, the designer route of imagining sort of somebody using a thing and imagining a smile on their face,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: imagining the experience of love and joy that you have when you use the thing?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: From a design perspective or if you're building more like a lower level thing for like Linux, you imagine a developer

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that might come across this and use it and become happy and better off because of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So where do you land on those things? Is it measurable?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I imagine like Meta and Google will probably try to measure the thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: They'll try to. It's like you try to optimize engagement or something. Let's measure engagement.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And then I think there is a kind of I mean, I admire the designer ethic of like think of a future that's immeasurable.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you try to make somebody in that future that's different from today happy.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I do usually favor if you can get any kind of a metric that's good, by all means, listen to the data.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But you can go too far there where we've had problems where it's like, hey, we had a performance regression

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: because our fancy new telemetry system is doing a bazillion file rights to kind of archive this stuff

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: because we needed to collect information to determine if we were doing, you know, if our plans were good.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So when information is available, you should never ignore it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean, from actual users using the thing, human beings using the thing, large number of human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you get to see sort of. So there's the zero to one problem of when you're doing something really new,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you do kind of have to make a guess. But one of the points that I've been making at Metta is we have more than enough users

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: now that anything somebody wants to try in VR, we have users that will be interested in that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You do not get to make a completely greenfield blue sky pitch and say, I'm going to do this because I think it might be interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I challenge everyone. There are going to be people, whether it's working in VR on your like on your desktop replacement

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: or communicating with people in different ways or playing the games, there are going to be probably millions of people,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: or at least if you pick some tiny niche that we're not in right now, there's still going to be thousands of people out there

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that have the headsets that would be your target market. And I tell people, pay attention to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Don't invent fictional users. Don't, you know, make an Alice Bob Charlie that fits whatever matrix of tendencies

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that you want to break the market down to because it's a mistake to think about imaginary users when you've got real users

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that you could be working with. But, you know, on the other hand, there is there is value to having a kind of wholeness of vision

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: for a product. And companies like Metta have, you know, they understand the tradeoffs where you can have a company like SpaceX

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: or, you know, Apple in the Steve Jobs era, where you have a very powerful leading personality that I know that can micromanage

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: at a very low level and can say it's like, no, that handle needs to be different or that that icon needs to change the tint there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And they clearly get a lot of value out of it. They also burn through a lot of employees that have horror stories to tell about

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: working there afterwards. My position is that you're at your best when you've got a leader that is at their limit of what they can kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: comprehend of everything below them. And they can have an informed opinion about everything that's going on. And you take somebody

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: it's you've got to believe that somebody that has 30, 40 years of experience, you would hope that they've got wisdom that the just out of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: boot camp person contributing doesn't have. And that if they're like, well, that's wrong there, you probably shouldn't do it that way or

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: or even just don't do it that way, do it another way. So there's value there, but it can't go beyond a certain level. I am I mean, I have

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Steve Jobs stories of him saying things that are just wrong right in front of me about technical things because he was not operating at that level.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But when it does work and you do get that kind of passionate leader that's thinking about the entire product and just really deeply cares about

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: not letting anything slip through the cracks. I think that's got a lot of value. But the other side of that is the people saying that, well, we want to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: have these independent teams that are bubbling up the ideas because like it's it's almost it's anti capitalist or anti free market to say it's like

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I want my grand, you know, my great leader to go ahead and dictate all these points there where clearly free markets bring up things that you

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: know, you don't expect like in VR, we we saw a bunch of things like it didn't turn out at all the way the early people thought were going to be

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the key applications and things that you know, would not have been approved by you know, the the dark cabal making the decisions about what

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's just really not possible to argue with that if you've been around the people that that work with that level of intensity and just say, it's like, no, they should just stop.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And we had I kind of came back around to that a couple of years ago where I was using the fictional example of all right.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Some people say they'll say with a straight face, they think, no, you you are less productive if you work more than 40 hours a week.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But you're not literally getting less done.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And, you know, it seems absurd.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So there's something about a deep dedication to a thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And, you know, obsession can often get things done that just practical, prudent pedestrian work won't or at least won't for a very long time.

body.input: But it was interesting where one of the things that I can remember being an unhappy teenager not having enough money

body.input: It would be spread out.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309
