metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I'm still doing quite well at my age.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Did you have a kind of, I don't know, spiritual experience with food or coffee or any of that kind of stuff?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean, you know, the programming experience, you know, with music or or like I listen to Brown Noise on a program or like creating an environment and the things you take into your body, just everything you construct can become a kind of ritual that empowers the whole process.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: The program. Did you have that relationship with pizza or?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It would really be with Diet Coke. There still is that sense of, you know, drop the can down, crack open the can of Diet Coke.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: All right. Now I mean business. We're getting to work here.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Still to this day, Diet Coke is still part of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah, probably eight or nine a day.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Nice. OK. What about your setup? How many screens? What kind of keyboard? Is there something interesting?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: What kind of IDE, Emax Vim or something modern? Linux? What operating system? Laptop or any interesting thing that brings you joy?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I kind of migrated cultures where early on through all of game dev, there was sort of one culture there, which was really quite distinct from the more the Silicon Valley venture, you know, culture for things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: They're different groups and they have pretty different mores and the way they think about things where and I still do think a lot of the big companies can learn can learn things from the hardcore game development side of things where it still boggles my mind how I am, how hostile to debuggers and ideas that so much of them, the kind of big money, get billions of dollars, Silicon Valley venture backed funds are.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Oh, that's interesting. Sorry. So you're saying like like big companies at Google and Meta are hostile to.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: They are not big on debuggers and ideas like so much of it is like Emax Vim for things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And we just assume that debuggers don't work most of the time for the systems.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And a lot of this comes from a sort of Linux bias on a lot of things where I did come up through the personal computers and then the DOS and then I am Windows.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it was Borland Tools and then Visual Studio and do you appreciate the buggers very much so.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean, a debugger is how you get a view into a system that's too complicated to understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean, anybody that thinks just read the code and think about it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That's an insane statement in the you can't even read all the code on a big system.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You have to do experiments on the system and doing that by adding log statements, recompiling and rerunning it is an incredibly inefficient way of doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean, yes, you can always get things done even if you're working with stone knives and you know, and bearskins.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That's that is the mark of a good programmer is that given any tools you will figure out a way to get it done.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But it's amazing what you can do with sometimes much, much better tools where instead of just going through this iterative compile run debug cycle,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you have the you have the old lisp direction of like you've got a rebel and you're working interactively and doing amazing things there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But in many cases, a debugger as a very powerful user interface that can stop examine all the different things in your program, set all these different breakpoints.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And of course, you can do that with GDB or whatever there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But this is one of the user interface fundamental principles where when something is complicated to do, you won't use it very often.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There's people that will break out GDB when they're at their wits end and they just have beat their head against a problem for so long.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But for somebody that kind of grew up in game dev, it's like they were running into the debugger anyways before they even knew there was a problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you would just stop and see what was happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And sometimes you could fix things even before you even before you did one compile cycle.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You could be in the debugger and you would say, well, I'm just going to change this right here.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And, yep, that did the job and fix it and go on.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And for people who don't know, GDB is a sort of popular Linux debugger primarily for C++.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: They handle most of the languages, but it's based on C as the original kind of Unix heritage.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's kind of like command line. It's not user friendly. It doesn't allow for clean visualizations.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you're exactly right. So you're using this kind of debugger usually when you're at wits end.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And there's a problem that you can't figure out why by just looking at the codes if to find it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That's how I guess normal programmers use it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But you're saying there should be tools that kind of visualize and help you as part of the programming process,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: just a normal programming process to understand the code deeper.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah, when I'm working on like my C, C++ code, I'm always running it from the debugger.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You know, just I type in the code, I run it many times.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: The first thing I do after writing code is set a breakpoint and step through the function.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Now other people will say it's like, oh, I do that in my head.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Well, your head is a faulty interpreter of all those things there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And I've written brand new code. I want to step in there and I'm going to single step through that,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: examine lots of things and see if it's actually doing what I expected it to.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It is a kind of companion, the debugger.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Like you're now coding in an interactive way with another being.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: The debugger is a kind of dumb being, but it's a reliable being.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That is an interesting question of what role does AI play in that kind of with codecs

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and these kind of ability to generate code that might be,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you might start having tools that understand the code in interesting, deep ways that can work with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There's a whole spectrum there from static code analyzers and various kind of dynamic tools there

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: up to AI that can conceivably grok these programs that literally no human can understand.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: They're too big, too intertwined, too interconnected, but it's not beyond the possibility of understanding.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's just beyond what we can hold in our heads as kind of mutable state while we're working on things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And I'm a big proponent again of things like static analyzers and some of that stuff

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where you'll find some people that don't like being scolded by a program for how they've written something

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where it's like, oh, I know better.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And sometimes you do, but that was something that it was very, very valuable for me when,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and not too many people get an opportunity like this to have.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: This is almost one of those spiritual experiences as a programmer, an awakening to the id software code bases

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: were a couple million lines of code.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And at one point I had used a few of the different analysis tools,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: but I made a point to really go through and scrub the code base using every tool that I could find.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it was eye-opening where we had a reputation for having some of the most robust, strongest code,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where there were some great things that I remember hearing from Microsoft telling us about crashes on Xbox.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And we had this tiny number that they said were probably literally hardware errors.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And then you have other significant titles that just have millions of faults that are getting recorded all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I was proud of our code on a lot of levels.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But when I took this code analysis squeegee through everything, it was shocking how many errors there were in there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Things that you can say, okay, this was a copy paste, not changing something right here.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Lots of things that were, the most common problem was something in a printf format string

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that was the wrong data type that could cause crashes there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And you really want the warnings for things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Then the next most common was missing a check for null that could actually happen, that could blow things up.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And those are obviously like top C, C++ things. Everybody has those problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But the long tail of all of the different little things that could go wrong there,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and we had good programmers and my own code stuff that I'd be looking at, it's like, oh, I wrote that code.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That's definitely wrong. We've been using this for a year.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's this summary, you know, this mind sitting there waiting for us to step on.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it was humbling. It was, and I reached the conclusion that anything that can be syntactically allowed in your language,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: if it's going to show up eventually in a large enough code base, you're not going to, good intentions aren't going to keep it from happening.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You need automated tools and guardrails for things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And those start with things like static types and or even type hints in the more dynamic languages.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But the people that rebel against that, that basically say that slows me down doing that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There's something to that. I get that. I've written, you know, I've cobbled things together in a notebook.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I am like, wow, this is great that it just happened. But yeah, that's kind of sketchy, but it's working fine.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I don't care. It does come back to that, that value analysis where sometimes it's right to not care.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But when you do care, if it's going to be something that's going to live for years and it's going to have other people working on it,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and it's going to be deployed to millions of people, then you want to use all of these tools.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You want to be told it's like, no, you screwed up here, here and here.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And that does require kind of an ego check about things where you have to be open to the fact that everything that you're doing is just littered with flaws.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's not that, oh, you occasionally have a bad day.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's just whatever stream of code you output, there is going to be a statistical regularity of things that you just make mistakes on.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And I do think there's the whole argument about test driven design and unit testing versus kind of analysis and different things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I am more in favor of the analysis and the stuff that just like you can't run your program until you fix this rather than you can run it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And hopefully a unit test will catch it in some way.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah. In my private code, I have asserts everywhere.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It just there's something pleasant to me, pleasurable to me about sort of the dictatorial rule of like, this should be true at this point.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And too many times I've made mistakes that shouldn't have been made.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And I would assume I wouldn't be the kind of person that would make that mistake, but I keep making that mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Therefore, an assert really catches me, really helps all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I would say like 10 to 20% of my private code just for personal use is probably asserts.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And they're active comments.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's one of those things that in theory they don't make any difference to the program.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And if it was all operating the way you expected it would be, then they will never fire.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But even if you have it right and you wrote the code right initially, then circumstances change.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: The world outside your program changes.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And in fact, that's one of the things where I'm kind of fond in a lot of cases of static or race size declarations where I went through this period where it's like, OK, now we have general collection classes.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: We should just make everything variable.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Because I had this history of in the early days you get doom, which had some fixed limits on it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Then everybody started making crazier and crazier things and they kept bumping up the different limits.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: This many lines, this many sectors.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it seemed like a good idea.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Well, we should just make this completely generic.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It can go kind of go up to whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And there's cases where that's the right thing to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But it also the other aspect of the world changing around you is it's good to be informed when the world has changed more than you thought it would.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And if you've got a continuously growing collection, you're never going to find out.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You might have this quadratic slowdown on something where you thought, oh, I'm only ever going to have a handful of these.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But something changes and there's a new design style and all of a sudden you've got 10,000 of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I kind of like in many cases picking a number, some nice round power of two number and setting it up in there and having an assert saying,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: hey, you hit this limit.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You should probably think are the choices that you've made around all of this still relevant if somebody is using 10 times more than you thought they would.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah, this code was originally written with this kind of worldview.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: With this kind of set of constraints, you were thinking of the world in this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: If something breaks, that means you got to rethink the initial stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's nice for it to for it for it to do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And that that puts a kind of I need to take the same kind of retreat as you're talking about.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But now I'm still fighting the Civil War. I need to kind of move into the 21st century.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it does seem like the world is or a large chunk of the world is moving towards visual studio code,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: which is kind of interesting to me against the JavaScript ecosystem on the one hand.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And IDs are one of those things that you want to be infinitely fast. You want them to just kind of immediately respond.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And like, I mean, heck, I've got there's someone I know.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And on a modern computer, everything is just absolutely instant on something like that because it was made to work on a computer that's ten thousand or a hundred thousand times slower.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So can you explain what a.plan file is and what role that played in your life? Does it still continue to play a role?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Back in the early, early days of id Software, one of our big things that was unique with what we did is I had adopted next stations or kind of next step systems from Steve Jobs's out in the out in the woods away from Apple company.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And I they were basically it was kind of interesting because I did not really have a background with the Unix system.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So many of the people they get immersed in that in college and I know that's that sets a lot of cultural expectations for them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And I didn't have any of that. But I knew that my background was I was a huge Apple fanboy.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I am I was always a little suspicious of the Mac. I was not really what I what kind of I wanted to to go with.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But when Steve Jobs left Apple and started next this computer did just seem like one of those amazing things from the future where it had all of this cool stuff in it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And we were still back in those days working on DOS. Everything blew up.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You had reset buttons because your computer would just freeze if you're doing development work literally dozens of times a day.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Your computer was just rebooting constantly.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And so this idea of yes any of the Unix workstations would have given a stable development platform where you don't crash and reboot all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But next also had this really amazing graphical interface and it was great for building tools and it used Objective-C as the kind of an interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Oh wow. So next was Unix based. It's that Objective-C. So it has a lot of the elements that became Mac.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean the kind of reverse acquisition of Apple by next where that took over and became what what the modern Mac system and define some of the developer like the tools and the whole community.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah. You've still got if you're programming on Apple stuff now there's still all these NS somethings which was originally next step objects of different kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But one of the aspects of those old those Unix systems was they had this notion of a dot plan file where you know a dot file is a you know an invisible file.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You analyze usually in your home directory or something and there was a trivial server running on most Unix systems at the time that I am that when somebody ran a trivial little command called finger.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You could do finger and then somebody's address. It could be anywhere on the Internet if you were connected correctly.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Then all that server would do was read the dot plan file in that user's home directory and then just spit it out to you.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And originally the idea was that could be whether you're on vacation what your current project was it's supposed to be like the plan of what you're doing and people would use it for you know various purposes.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But all it did was dump that file over the to the terminal of whoever issued the finger command.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And at you know at one point I started just keeping a list of what I was doing in there which would be what I was working on in the day and I would have this little syntax I kind of got to myself about.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Here's something that I'm working on I put a star when I finish it I could have a few other little bits of punctuation and at the time it was it started off as being just like my to do list and it would be these.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Trivial obscure little things like I you know fixed something with collision detection code made him fireball do something different and just little one liners that people that were following the games could kind of decipher.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But I did wind up starting to write much more in depth things I would have I little notes of thoughts and insights and then I would eventually start having little essays I would sometimes dump into the dot plan files interspersed with the work logs of things that I was doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So in some ways it was like a super early proto blog where I was just kind of dumping out what I was working on but it was interesting enough that there were a lot of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That I that were interested in this so most of the people didn't have unix workstation so there were the websites back in the day that would follow the doom and quake development.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That would I would basically make a little service that would go grab all the changes and then people could just get it with a web browser.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And the sort of action based things 3d at the time was really largely about the simulation thoughts and this is something that really might have trended differently if not for the id software approach in the games where there were flight simulators there were driving simulators yet like hard drive in and Microsoft flight simulator and these were doing 3d and general purpose 3d and ways that were more flexible than what we were doing with our games but.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So one of the interesting things that come back to the theme of deadlines and resource constraints the the game catacombs 3D.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: We shipped we were supposed to be shipping this for gamers edge on a monthly cadence and I had slipped I was actually late it slipped like 6 weeks because this was texture mapped walls doing stuff that I hadn't done before.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And at the 6 week point it was still kind of glitchy and buggy there were things that I knew that if you had a wall that was like almost edge on you could slide over to it you could see some things freak out or vanish or not work and I hated that I but.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I was up against the wall we had to ship the game I it was still a lot of fun to play was novel nobody had seen it gave you that startle reflex I reaction so it was worth shipping but it had these things that I knew were kind of flaky and janky and not not what I was really proud of.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So one of the things that I did very differently in Wolfenstein I was I went.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Catacombs used almost a conventional thing where you had segments that were one dimensional polygons basically that were clipped and I'm back faced and done kind of like a very crude 3D engine from the professionals but I wasn't getting it done right I was not doing a good enough job I didn't really have line of sight to.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I am to fix it right there stuff that of course I look back it's like oh it's obvious how to do this do the math right do your clipping right I check all of this how you handle the precision but I did not know how to do that at that time and I was the first 3D engine you wrote catacombs 3D.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: In hover tank had been a little bit before that but that had the flat shaded walls so the texture mapping on the walls was what was bringing in some of these challenges that was that was hard for me and I couldn't solve it right at the time can you describe what flat shading isn't texture mapping so in the the walls were solid color one of 16 colors I'm in hover tank so that's easy it's fast you just draw the solid color for everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Texture mapping is what we all see today where you have an image that is stretched and distorted onto the walls of the surfaces that you're working with.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it was you know it was a long time for me to just figure out how to do that without it distorting in the wrong ways and and I did not get it all exactly right in catacombs and I had these flaws.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So that was important enough to me that rather than continuing to bang my head on that when I wasn't positive I was going to get it I went with a completely different approach for drawing for figuring out where the walls were which was a ray casting approach.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Which I had done in catacombs 3D I had a bunch of C code trying to make this work right and it wasn't working right.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: In Wolfenstein I wound up going to a very small amount of assembly code so in some ways they should be a slower way of doing it but by making it a smaller amount of work that I could more tightly optimize it worked out and Wolfenstein 3D was just absolutely rock solid.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You know it was you know nothing glitched in there the game just was pretty much flawless through all of that and I was super proud of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I'm but eventually like in the later games I went back to the more span based things where I could get more total efficiency once I really did figure out how to do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So there were two sort of key technical things to Wolfenstein one was this ray casting approach.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Which you still to this day you see people go and say let's write a ray casting engine because it's an understandable way of doing things that lets you make games.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Very much like that so you see ray casters in JavaScript ray casters in Python people that are are basically going and re implementing that that approach to to taking a tiled world and casting out into it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It works pretty well but it's not the fastest way of doing it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Can you describe what ray casting is?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So you start off and you got your screen which is 320 pixels across at the time if you haven't sized down the window for for greater speed.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And every pixel there's gonna be an angle from you got your position in the world and you're going to just run along that angle and keep going until you hit a block.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So up to 320 times across there it's gonna throw a cast array out into the world from wherever your origin is until it runs into a wall and then it can figure out exactly where on the wall it hits.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: The performance challenge of that is as it's going out every block it's crossing it checks is this a solid wall.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So that means that in like the early Wolfenstein levels you're in a small jail cell going out into a small hallway.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's super efficient for that because you're only stepping across three or four blocks.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But then if somebody makes a room that covers our maps were limited to 64 by 64 blocks.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: If you made one room that was nothing but walls at the far space it would go pretty slow because it would be stepping across 80 tile tests or something along the way.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: By the way the physics of our universe seems to be competing this very thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So this maps nicely to the actual physics of our world.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah you get I follow a little bit of something like Stephen Wolfram's work on I've you know interconnected network information states of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And that's it's beyond what I can have an informed opinion on.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But it's interesting that people are considering things like that and have and have things that can back it up.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah there's whole different sets of interesting stuff there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So Wolfenstein 3D had ray casting.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Ray casting and then the other kind of key aspect was what I called compiled scalers where the idea of.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You saw this in the earlier classic arcade games like Space Harrier and stuff where you would take a picture which is normally drawn directly on the screen.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And then if you have the ability to make it bigger or smaller big chunky pixels or physically small drop sampled pixels.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That's the fundamental aspect of what our characters were doing in these 3D games.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You would have it's just like you might have drawn a tiny little character but now we can make them really big and make them really small move it around.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That was the limited kind of 3D that we had for characters to make them turn.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There were literally eight different views of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You didn't actually have a 3D model that would rotate.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You just had these cardboard cutouts.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But that was good enough for that startle fight reaction.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it was kind of what we had to do deal with there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So a straightforward approach to do that you could just write out your doubly nested loop of you've got your stretch factor and it's like you've got a point you stretch by a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It might be on the same pixel it might be on the next pixel might have skipped a pixel.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You can write that out but it's not going to be fast enough where especially you get a character for that right in your face monster covering almost the entire screen.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Doing that with a general purpose scaling routine would have just been much too slow.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It would have worked when they're small characters but then it would get slower and slower as they got closer to you until right at the time when you most care about having a fast reaction time the game would be chunking down.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So the fastest possible way to draw pixels at that time was to.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Instead of saying I've got a general purpose version that can handle any scale I made.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I used a program to make essentially a hundred or more separate little programs that was optimized for I will take an image and I will draw it 12 pixels tall I'll take an image I'll draw it 14 pixels tall up by every two pixels even for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So you would have the most optimized code so that in the normal case where most of the world is fairly large.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I like the pixels are big you know we did not have a lot of memory so in most cases that meant that you would load a pixel color and then you would store it multiple times.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So that was faster than even copying an image in a normal conventional case because most of the time the image is expanded.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So instead of doing one read one write for a simple copy you might be doing one read and three or four writes as it got really big.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And that had the beneficial aspect of just when you needed the performance most when things are covering the screen it was giving you the most acceleration for that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: By the way we able to understand this through thinking about it or were you testing like the right speed and.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: This again comes back to I can find the antecedents for things like this so in I'm back in the Apple two days and I'm the graphics were.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Essentially single bits at a time and if you wanted to make your little spaceship if you wanted to make it smoothly go across the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: If you just took the image and you drew it out at the next location you would move by seven pixels at a time so it go chunk chunk chunk.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: If you wanted to make it move smoothly you actually had to make seven versions of the ship that were pre shifted you could write a program that would shift it dynamically but on a one megahertz processor that's not going anywhere fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So if you wanted to do a smooth moving fast action game you made separate versions of each of these sprites.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Now there are a few more tricks you could pull that if it still wasn't fast enough you could make a compiled shape where instead of.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: This program that normally copies an image and says like get this bite from here stored here get this bite store this bite if you've got the memory space.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You could say I'm going to write the program that does nothing but draw this shape.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's going to be like I'm going to load the immediate value twenty five you know which is some bit pattern and then I'm going to store that at this location.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Rather than loading something from memory that will involve indexing registers and this other slow stuff you could go ahead and say no I'm going to hard code the exact values of all of the image right into the program.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: This was always a horrible trade off there but you didn't have much memory and you didn't have much speed but if you had something that you wanted to go really fast you could turn it into a program.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And that was you know knowing about that technique is what made me think about some of these unwinding it for the PC where people that didn't come from that background were less likely to think about that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean there's some deep parallels probably to human cognition as well there's something about.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Optimizing and compressing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: The processing of a new information that requires you to predict the possible ways in which the game or the world might unroll and you have something like compiled scalers always there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You have like optimize like you have a prediction of how the world will unroll and you have some kind of optimized.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Data structure for that prediction and then you can modify if the world turns out to be different you can modify in a slight way.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And as far as building out techniques so much of the brain is about the associative context you know they're just when you learn something it's in the context of something else and you can have.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Faint tiny little hints of things and I do think there are some deep things you know around like sparse distributed memories and boosting that's like if you can just be slightly above the noise floor of having some hint of something.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You can have things refined into pulling the memory back up so having a being a programmer and having a toolbox of like all of these things that things that I did in all of these previous lives of programming tasks.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That still matters to me about how I'm able to pull up some of these things like in that case it was something I did on the apple to then being relevant for the PC.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And I have still cases when I would when I would work on mobile development then be like OK I did something like this back in the doom days but now it's a different environment but I still had that tie I can bring it in and I can transform it into what the world needs right now.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And I do think that's actually one of the very core things with human cognition and brain like I you know brain like functioning is finding these ways about you've got your brain is kind of everything everywhere all at once you know it's it is just a set of all of this stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It is just fetched back by these queries that go into it and they can just be slightly above the noise floor with random noise in your neurons and synapses that are affecting exactly what gets pulled up.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So you're saying some of these very specific solutions for different games you find that there's a kernel of an deep idea that's generalizable to other to other things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah you can't predict what it's going to be but that idea of like I called out that compiled shaders in the forward that I wrote for that the game engine black book as you know this is it's kind of an end point of unrolling code.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But that's one of those things that thinking about that and having that in your mind and I'm sure there are some programmers that you know hear about that think about it a little bit it's kind of the mind blown moment it's like oh you can just turn all of that data into code.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And nowadays you know you have instruction cache issues and that's not necessarily the best idea but there are different it's an idea that has power and has probably relevance in some other areas maybe it's in a hardware point of view that there's a way you approach building hardware that has that same.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: What is the story of how you came to program doom what is some memorable technical challenges or innovations within that game.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So the path that we went after after wolf and stein got out and we were on this crazy arc where keen one through three more success than we thought keen four through six even more success wolf and stein even more success so we were on this this crazy trajectory for things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So actually our first box commercial project was a commander keen I am game but then wolf and stein was going to have a game called spear of destiny which was a commercial version sixty new levels.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So the rest of the team took the game engine pretty much as it was and started working on that we got new monsters but it's basically reskins of the things there there's a really interesting aspect about that that i didn't appreciate until much much later.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: About how wolf and stein clearly did tap out its limit about what you want to play i am all the levels and a couple of our license things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There was a hard creative wall that you did not really benefit much by continuing to beat on it but i game like doom and other more modern games like minecraft or something there's kind of a turing completeness level of design freedom that you get in games that wolf and stein really sat on one side of.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You know all the creative people in the world could not go and do a masterpiece just with the technology that wolf and stein had wolf and stein could do wolf and stein but you really couldn't do something crazy and different.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But it didn't take that much more capability to get to wolf and stein with the free form lines and i had a little bit more artistic freedom to get to the point where people still announced new doom levels today all these years after without having completely tapped out the creative how did you put it to complete design space design space like you know we have the kind of computational universality on a lot of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But yeah there's things where a box can be too small but above a certain point you're kind of are at the point where you you really have almost unbounded creative ability there and doom is the first time you cross that line yeah where there were.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Thousands of doom levels created and some of them still have something new and interesting to say to the world about it is that line.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: out of the company. And this is one of the things that I look back, if I could go back telling my

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And that did lead to a bunch of the problems where I was sitting here going,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: it's like, all right, I'm working harder than anyone. I'm doing these technologies,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you know, nobody's done before, but we're all equal partners. And then I see, you know, somebody

body.input: that's not working as hard. And I mean, I can't say I was the most mature about that. I was,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you know, 20 something years old and it did bother me when I'm like, everybody, okay, we need to all

body.input: pull together and we've done it before everybody. We know we can do this if we get together and we

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: grind it all out, but not everybody wanted to do that for all time, you know. And I was the youngest

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: one of the crowd there. I had different sets of kind of backgrounds and motivations and left at

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that point where it was, all right, either everybody has to be contributing like up to this level or

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: they need to get pushed out was not, that was not a great situation. And I look back on it and no,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: we pushed people out of the company that could have contributed if there was a different framework

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: maybe it's non-voting stock and all those different things. We knew nothing about any of that. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So if you think the framework was different, some of the human tension could have been a little bit.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It almost certainly would have. I mean, I look back at that and it's like even trying to sum it

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: up in my mind, it's like, I know I was really, really angry about Romero not working as hard as

body.input: I wanted him to work or not carrying his load on the design for Quake and coming up with things

body.input: there. But he was definitely doing things. He made some of the best levels there. He was working with

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Because that was always one of the challenging things in it, Id, where we were doing these

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Eventually, we had sort of a challenge over the weekend that we were going to race to implement

body.input: this game to port one of our PC games back down to the Apple II. That was where we finally kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: became clear. It's like, okay, Carmack stands a little bit apart on the programming side.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Romero then very gracefully moved into, well, he'll work on the tools. He'll work on the systems,

body.input: aspects of a lot of things. He was enormously valuable in the early stuff and so much of Doom

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah. I mean, it's the Beatles problem.

body.input: that was great in the games did come from him and I would certainly not take that away from him.

body.input: Even after we parted ways and he took his swing with Eidos, in some ways, he was ahead of the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You still got love in your heart.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I just talked with him last year, I guess it was even this year, about mentioning that I'm going
