body.input: for how AI is going to play into gaming and asked if I was interested in collaborating.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's not in line with what I'm doing, but I wish almost everyone the best. I know I may not have

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: partnered on the best of terms with some people, but I was thrilled to see Tom Hall writing VR

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You were the CTO of Oculus VR since 2013 and maybe less than a year involved in it a bit

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: in 2019. Oculus was acquired by Facebook, now Meta, in 2014. You've spoken brilliantly about

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: both the low level details, the experimental design, and the big picture vision of virtual reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Let me ask you about the metaverse, the big question here, both philosophically and technically.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: How hard is it to build the metaverse? What is the metaverse in your view? You started with

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: discussing and thinking about Quake as a metaverse. As you think about it today,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: what is the metaverse, the thing that could create this compelling user value, this experience that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: will change the world, and how hard is it to build it? The term comes from Neil Stevenson's book,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Snow Crash, which many of us had read back in the 90s. It was one of those formative books.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There was this sense that the possibilities and the freedom and unlimited capabilities to build

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: a virtual world that does whatever you want, whatever you ask of it, has been a powerful draw

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: for generations of developers, game developers specifically and people that are thinking about

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: more general purpose applications. We were talking about that back in the Doom and Quake days, about

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: how do you wind up with an interconnected set of worlds that you visit from one to another,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and as web pages were becoming a thing, you start thinking about what is the interactive

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: 3D-based equivalent of this. There were a lot of really bad takes. You had like

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Vermaul then, virtual reality markup languages, and there's aspects like that that came from

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: people saying, well, what kind of capabilities should we develop to enable this?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That kind of capability first work has usually not panned out very well. On the other hand,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: we have successful games that started with things like Doom and Quake and communities

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that formed around those, whether it was server lists in the early days or literal

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: portaling between different games, and then modern things that are on completely different

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: order of magnitude like Minecraft and Fortnite that have 100 million plus users. I still think

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that that's the right way to go to build the metaverse is you build something that's amazing

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that people love and people wind up spending all their time in because it's awesome, and you

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: expand the capabilities of that. Even if it's a very basic experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: As long as people... Minecraft is an amazing case study in so many things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That's basic as it gets. Where what's been able to be done with that is really enlightening.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There are other cases where like right now, Roblox is basically a game construction kit aimed at

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: kids, and that was a capability first play, and it's achieving scale that's on the same order

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of those things. It's not impossible, but my preferred bet would be you make something

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: amazing that people love and you make it better and better. That's where I could say we could

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: have gone back and followed a path like that in the early days. If you just take the same game,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: whether it's when Activision demonstrated that you could make Call of Duty every year,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and not only is it not bad, people love it and it's very profitable. The idea that you could have

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: taken something like that, take a great game, release a new version every year that lets the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: capabilities grow and expand to start saying it's like, okay, it's a game about running around and

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: shooting things, but now you can have... Bring your media into it. You can add persistence of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: social signs of life or whatever you want to add to it. I still think that's quite a good

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: position to take, and I think that while Meta is doing a bottoms-up capability approach with

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Horizon Worlds where it's a fairly general purpose, creators can build whatever they want

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: in their sort of thing, it's hard to compare and compete with something like Fortnite,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: which also has enormous amounts of creativity, even though it was not designed originally

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: as a general purpose sort of thing. So we have examples on both sides. Me personally,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I would have bet on trying to do entertainment, valuable destination first and expanding from

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: there. So can you imagine the thing that will be kind of... If we look back a couple of centuries

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: from now and you think about the experiences that marked the singularity, the transition

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where most of our world moved into virtual reality, what do you think those experiences

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: will look like? So I do think it's going to be kind of like the way the web slowly took over,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where you're the frog in the pot of water that's slowly heating up, where having lived through all

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of that. I remember when it was shocking to start seeing the first website address on a billboard,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: when you're like, hey, my computer world is infecting the real world. This is spreading out

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: in some way. But there's still, when you look back and say, well, what made the web take off?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it wasn't a big bang sort of moment there. It was a bunch of little things that turned out

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: not to even be the things that are relevant now that brought them into it. So...

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Well, I wonder if from, I mean, like you said, you're not a historian. So maybe there's a

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: historian out there that could really identify that moment, data-driven way. It could be like

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: MySpace or something like that. Maybe the first major social network that really reached into

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: non-geek world or something like that. I think that's kind of the fallacy of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: historians though, looking for some of those kind of primary dominant causes where so many of these

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: things are like, we see an exponential curve, but it's not because like one thing is going

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: exponential. It's because we have hundreds of little sigmoid curves overlapped on top of each

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: other. And they just happen to keep adding up so that you've got something kind of going exponential

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: at any given point. But no single one of them was the critical thing. There were

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: dozens and dozens of things. I mean, seeing the transitions of stuff like as obviously MySpace

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: giving way to other things, but even like blogging giving way to social media and getting

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: resurrected in other guises and things that happened there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And the memes with the dancing baby GIF or whatever the, all your base now belong to us,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: whatever those early memes that led to the modern memes and the humor on the different evolution of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: humor on the internet that I'm sure the historians will also write books about from the different

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: website that support that create the infrastructure for that humor, like Reddit and all that kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: stuff. So people will go back and they will name firsts and critical moments, but it's probably

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: going to be a poor approximation of what actually happens. And we've already seen like in the VR

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: space where it didn't play out the way we thought it would in terms of what was going to be like

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: when the modern era of VR basically started with my E3 demo of Doom 3 on the Rift prototype. So

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: we're like first person shooters in VR match made in heaven, right? And that didn't work out that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: way at all. They have, you know, they have the most comfort problems with it. And then the most

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: popular virtual reality app is Beat Saber, which nobody predicted back then.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: What's that make you like from first principles, if you were to like reverse engineer that, why

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: are these like silly fun games the most?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It actually makes very clear sense when you analyze it from hindsight and look at the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: engineering reasons where it's not just that it was a magical quirky idea. It was something that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: played almost perfectly to what turned out to be the real strengths of VR, where the one thing that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I really underestimated importance in VR was the importance of the controllers. You know, I was

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: still thinking we could do a lot more with the game pad and just the amazingness of taking any

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: existing game, being able to move your head around and look around that that was, you know, that was

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: really amazing. But the controllers were super important. But the problem is so many things that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you do with the controllers just suck. It feels like it breaks the illusion, like trying to pick

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: up glasses with the controllers where you're like, oh, use the grip button when you're kind of close

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and it'll snap into your hand. All of those things are unnatural actions that you do them and it's

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: still part of the VR experience. But Beat Saber winds up playing only to the strengths. It

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: completely hides all the weaknesses of it because you are holding something in your hand, you keep

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: a solid grip on it the whole time. It slices through things without ever bumping into things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: You never get into the point where, you know, I'm knocking on this table, but in VR, my hand just

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: goes right through it. So you've got something that slices through. So it's never your brain

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: telling you, oh, I should have hit something. You've got a lightsaber here. It's just, you expect

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: it to slice through everything. Audio and music turned out to be a really powerful aspect of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: virtual reality where you're blocking the world off and constructing the world around you.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And being something that can run efficiently on even this relatively low powered hardware

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and can have a valuable loop in a small amount of time where a lot of modern games, you're supposed

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to sit down and play it for an hour just to get anywhere. Sometimes a new game takes an hour to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: get through the tutorial level. And that's not good for VR for a couple reasons. You do still have the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: comfort issues if you're moving around at all, but you've also got just, you know, discomfort from

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the headset, battery lifespan on the mobile versions. So having things that do break down into three and

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: four minute windows of play, that turns out to be very valuable from a gameplay standpoint.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So it winds up being kind of a perfect storm of all of these things that are really good.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It doesn't have any of the comfort problems. You're not navigating around. You're standing still.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: All the stuff flies at you. It has placed audio strengths. It adds the whole fitness in VR.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Nobody was thinking about that back in the, at the beginning. And it turns out that that is an

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: excellent daily fitness thing to be doing. If you go play an hour of BeatSaver or Supernatural or

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: something, that is legit solid exercise. And it's more fun than doing it just about any other way

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: there. So that's kind of the arcade stage of things. If I were to say with my experience with VR,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the thing that I think is powerful is the, maybe it's not here yet, but the degree to which it is

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: immersive in the way that Quake is immersive. It takes you to another world. For me, because I'm a

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: fan of role playing games, the Elder Scrolls series, like Skyrim or even Daggerfall, it just

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: takes you to another world. And when you're not in that world, you miss not being there. And then

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you just, you kind of want to stay there forever because life is shitty. And you just want to go

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to this place. There was a time when we were kind of asked to come up with like, what's your view

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: about VR? And my pitch was that it should be better inside the headset than outside. It's the world

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: as you want it. And everybody thought that was dystopian and like, that's like, oh, you're just

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: going to forget about the world outside. And I don't get that mindset where the idea that if you

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: can make the world better inside the headset than outside, you've just improved the person's life

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that has a headset that can wear it. And there are plenty of things that we just can't do for

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: everyone in the real world. Everybody can't have Richard Branson's private island, but everyone

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: can have a private VR island and it can have the things that they want on it. And there's a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: these kind of rivalrous goods in the real world that VR can just be better at. We can do a lot

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of things like that that can be very, very rich. So yeah, I want the, I think it's going to be a

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: positive thing, this world where people want to go back into their headset, where it can be better

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: than somebody that's living in a tiny apartment, can have a palatial estate in virtual reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: They can have all their friends from all over the world come over and visit them without everybody

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: getting on a plane and meeting in someplace and dealing with all the other logistics hassles.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There is real value in the presence that you can get for remote meetings. It's all the little

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: things that we need to sort out, but those are things that we have line of sight on. People

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that have been in a good VR meeting using workrooms where you can say, oh, that was better

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: than a Zoom meeting. But of course, it's more of a hassle to get into it. Not everyone has the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: headset. Interoperability is worse. You can't have, you cap out at a certain number. There's all these

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: things that need to be fixed, but that's one of those things you can look at and say, we know

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: there's value there. We just need to really grind hard, file off all the rough edges and make that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: possible. So you do think we have line of sight because there's a reason like I do this podcast

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: in person, for example, doing it remotely, it's not the same. And if somebody were to ask me why

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: it's not the same, I wouldn't be able to write down exactly why. But you're saying that it's

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: possible, whatever the magic is for in-person interaction, that immersiveness of the experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: we are almost there. Yes. So it's the idea of like, I'm doing a VR interview with someone.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I'm not saying it's here right now, but you can see glimmers of what it should be. And we largely

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: know what would need to be fixed and improved to, like you say, there's a difference between a remote

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: interview, doing a podcast over zoom or something and face to face. There's that sense of presence,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that immediacy, the super low latency responsiveness, being able to see all the subtle

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: things there, just occupying the same field of view. And all of those are things that we absolutely

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: can do in VR. And that simple case of a small meeting with a couple of people, that's the much

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: easier case than everybody thinks the ready player one multiverse with a thousand people going across

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that, you know, a huge bridge to amazing places. That's harder in a lot of other technical ways,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: not to say we can't also do that, but that's further away and has more challenges. But this

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: small thing about being able to have a meeting with one or a few people and have it feel real,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: feel like you're there. I think you have the same interactions and talking with them. You get subtle

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: cues as we start getting eye and face tracking and some of the other things on high end headsets.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: A lot of that is going to come over. And it doesn't have to be as good. This is an important thing

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that people miss where there was a lot of people that, especially rich people that would look at

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: VR and say, it's like, oh, this just isn't that good. And I'd say it's like, well, you've already

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: been courtside backstage and you know, on pit row and you've done all of these experiences because

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you get to do them in real life. But most people don't get to. And even if the experience is only

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: half as good, if it's something that they never would have gotten to do before, it's still a very

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: good thing. And as we can just, we can push that number up over time. It has a minimum

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: viable value level when it does something that is valuable enough to people. As long as it's

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: better inside the headset on any metric than it is outside and people choose to go there,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: we're on the right path. And we have a value gradient that I'm just always hammering on. We

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: can just follow this value gradient, just keep making things better rather than going for that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: one, close your eyes, swing for the fences, kind of silver bullet approach. Well, I wonder if there's

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: a value gradient for in-person meetings, because if you get that right, I mean, that would change

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the world. Yeah. It doesn't need to, I mean, you don't need a ready player one. But I wonder if

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: there's that value gradient you can follow along. Because if there is and you follow it, then there

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: will be a certain like phase shift at a certain point where people will shift from Zoom to this.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I wonder what are the bottlenecks? Is it software? Is it hardware? Is it all about latency?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I have big arguments internally about strategic things like that, where the next headset that's

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: coming out that we've made various announcements about is going to be a higher end headset,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: more expensive, more features. Lots of people want to make those trade-offs. We'll see what the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: market has to say about the exact trade-offs we've made here. But if you want to replace Zoom,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you need to have something that everybody has. So you like cheaper.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I like cheaper because also lighter and cheaper wind up being a virtuous cycle there where

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: expensive and more features tends to also lead towards heavier. And it just kind of goes,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: it's like, let's add more features. The features are not, they have physical presence and weight

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and draw from batteries and all of those things. So I've always favored a lower end, cheaper,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: faster approach. That's why I was always behind the mobile side of VR rather than the higher end PC

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: headsets. And I think that's proven out well. But ideally we have a whole range of things,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: but if you've only got one or two things, it's important that those two things cover the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: scope that you think is most important. When we're in a world when it's like cell phones

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and there's 50 of them on the market covering every conceivable ecological niche you want,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that's going to be great, but we're not going to be there for a while.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Where are the bottlenecks? Is it the hardware or the software?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah. So right now you can play, you can get work rooms on Quest and you can set up these things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's a pretty good experience. It's surprisingly good.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I haven't tried it. It's surprisingly good.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah. The voice latency is better on that than a lot better than a Zoom meeting. So you've got a

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: better sense of immediacy there. The expressions that you get from the current hardware with just

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: kind of your controllers and your head is pretty realistic feeling. You've got a pretty good sense

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of being there with someone. Are these like avatars of people? Do you get to see their body?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And they're sitting around a table? Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it feels better than Zoom? Yeah. Better than you'd expect for that. It is

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: definitely, yeah, I'd say it's quite a bit better than Zoom when everything's working right, but

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: all the rough edges of the reason Zoom became so successful is because they just nailed the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: usability of everything. It's high quality with a absolutely first rate experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And we are not there yet with any of the VR stuff. I'm trying to push hard to get,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I keep talking about it's like, it needs to just be one click to make everything happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And we're getting there in our home environment, not the whole work rooms application, but the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: main home where you can now kind of go over and click an invite and it still winds up taking

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: five times longer than it should. But we're getting close to that where you click there,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: they click on their button, and then they're sitting there in this good presence with you.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But latencies need to get a lot better. User interface needs to get a lot better.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Ubiquity of the headsets needs to get better. We need to have a hundred million of them

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: out there just so that everybody knows somebody that uses this all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Well, I think it's a virtuous cycle because I do think the interface is the thing that makes or

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: breaks this kind of revolution. It's so interesting how like you said one click,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: but it's also like how you achieve that one click. I don't know what is, can ask a dark question,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: maybe let's keep it outside of meta. But this is about meta, but also Google and big company.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Are they able to do this kind of thing? It seems like, let me put on my cranky old man hat,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: is that they seem to not do a good job of creating these user friendly interfaces as they get bigger

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and bigger as a company. Like Google has created some of the greatest interfaces ever early on.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And it's, I mean, creating Gmail, just so many brilliant interfaces and it just seems to be

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: getting crappier and crappier at that. Same with meta, same with Microsoft. It's just, it seems to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: get worse and worse at that. I don't know what it is because you've become more conservative,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: careful, risk averse. Is that why? Can you speak to that?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So it's been really eye-opening to me working inside a tech titan where I had my small companies

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and then we're acquired by a mid-size game publisher and then Oculus getting acquired by meta.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And meta has grown by a factor of many just in the eight years since the acquisition.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I did not have experience with this and it was interesting because I remember like previously my

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: benchmark for kind of use of resources was some of the government programs I interacted with on

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the aerospace side. And I remember thinking there was, okay, there's an Air Force program and they

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: spent $50 million and they didn't launch anything. They didn't even build anything. It was just kind

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of like they made a bunch of papers and had some parts in a warehouse and nothing came of it. It's

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: like $50 million. And I've had to radically recalibrate my sense of how much money can be

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: spent with mediocre resources where on the plus side, VR has turned out. We've built

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: pretty much exactly what, we just passed the 10-year mark then from my first demo of the Rift.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And if I could have said what I wanted to have, it would have been a standalone inside out tracked

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: 4K resolution headset that I, that could still plug into a PC for high-end rendering. And that's

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: exactly what we've got on Quest 2 right now. Yes. First of all, let's pause on that with me

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: being cranky and everything. What meta achieved with Oculus and so on is incredible.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean, this is, when I thought about the future of VR, this is what I imagined in terms of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: hardware, I would say. And maybe in terms of the experience as well, but it's still not there

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: somehow. On the one hand, we did kind of achieve it and win and we've got, we've sold, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: we're a success right now, but the amount of resources that have gone into it, it winds up

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: getting cluttered up in accounting where Mark did announce that they spent $10 billion a year

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: like on Reality Labs. Now Reality Labs covers a lot. It was, VR was not the large part of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It also had Portal and Spark and the big AR research efforts. And it's been expanding out

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to include AI and other things there where there's a lot going on there. But $10 billion was just a

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: number that I had trouble processing. It's just, I feel sick to my stomach thinking about that much

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: money being spent. But that's how they demonstrate commitment to this where it's not more so than,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: like, yeah, Google goes and cancels all of these projects, different things like that, while Meta

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: is really sticking with the funding of VR and AR is still further out with it. So there's something

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to be said for that. It's not just going to vanish, the work's going in. I just wish it could be,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: all those resources could be applied more effectively because I see all these cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I point out these examples of how a third party that we're kind of competing with in various ways,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: there's a number of these examples, and they do work with a tenth of the people that we do internally.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And a lot of it comes from, yes, the small company can just go do it, while in a big company,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you do have to worry about, is there some SDK internally that you should be using because

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: another team's making it? You have to have your cross-functional group meetups for different

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: things. You do have more concerns about privacy or diversity and equity and safety of different

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: things, parental issues, and things that a small startup company can just kind of cowboy off and

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: do something interesting. And there's a lot more that is a problem that you have to pay attention

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to in the big companies, but I'm not willing to believe that we are within even a factor of two or

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: four of what the efficiency could be. I am constantly kind of crying out for it. It's like,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: we can do better than this. And you wonder what the mechanisms to unlock that efficiency are.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There is some sense in a large company that an individual engineer might not believe that they

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: can change the world. Maybe you delegate a little bit of the responsibility to be the one who changes

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the world in a big company. But the reality is the world will get changed by a single engineer

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: anyway. So whether inside Google or inside a startup, it doesn't matter. It's just like Google

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and Metta needs to help those engineers believe they're the ones that are going to decrease that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: latency. It'll take one John Carmack, the 20-year-old Carmack that's inside Metta right

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: now to change everything. And I try to point that out and push people. It's like, try to go ahead

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and when you see some... Because you get the silo mentality where you're like, okay, I know

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: something's not right over there, but I'm staying in my lane here. And there's a couple people that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I can think about that are willing to just hop all over the place. And man, I treasure them,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the people that are just willing to... They're fearless. They will go over and they will go

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: rebuild the kernel and change this distribution and go in and hack the firmware over here to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: get something done right. And that is relatively rare. There's thousands of developers and you've

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: got a small handful that are willing to operate at that level. And it's potentially risky for them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: The politics are real in a lot of that. And I'm in very much the privileged position of...

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I'm more or less untouchable there where I've been dinged twice for it's like,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you said something insensitive in that post and you should probably not say that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But for the most part, yes, I get away with every week I'm posting something pretty loud

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and opinionated internally. And I think that's useful for the company, but yeah, it's rare to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: have a position like that. And I can't necessarily offer advice for how someone can do that.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Well, you could offer advice to a company in general to give a little bit of freedom for the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: young, wild... The wildest ideas come from the young minds. And so you need to give the young minds

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: freedom to think big and wild and crazy. And for that, they have to be opinionated. They have to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: think crazy ideas and thoughts and pursue them with a full passion without being slowed down by

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I do want to say a quick thing about nuclear energy where I, you know, this is something that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: about all of these, the physics of this stuff hasn't changed. And the reasons why things are

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: but even if it comes out, then you have to do all of that immensely complex, expensive stuff

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: just to make something hot where nuclear fission is basically you put these two rocks together and

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And the actual rocks, the refined uranium is not very expensive. It's a couple percent of the cost

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of electricity. That's why I made that point where you could have something which was five times less

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: efficient than current systems. And if the rest of the plant was a whole bunch cheaper, you could

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: still be super, super valuable. So how much of the pie do you think could be solved by nuclear

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: energy by fission? So how much could it become the primary source of energy on Earth?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It could be most of it. The reserves of uranium as it stands now could not power the whole Earth,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: but you get into breeder reactors and thorium and things like that that you do for conventional

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: fission. There is enough for everything. Now, solar photovoltaic has been amazing. One of my

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: current projects is working on an off-grid system, and it's been fun just putting my hands on all the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: wires, stripping the wires and wiring things together and doing all of that. And just having

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: followed that a little bit from the outside over the last couple decades, there's been semiconductor

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: like magical progress in what's going on there. So I'm all for all of that, but it doesn't solve

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: everything. And nuclear really still does seem like the smart money bet for what you should be

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: getting for baseband on a lot of things. And solar may be cheaper for peeking over air conditioning

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: loads during the summer and things that you can push around in different ways. But it's one of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: those things that's just strange how we've had the technology sitting there, but these non-technical

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: reasons on the social optics of it has been this major forcing function for something that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: really should be at the cornerstone of all of the world's concerns with energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's interesting how the non-technical factors have really dominated something that is so

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: fundamental to the existence of the human race as we know it today.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And much of the troubles of the world, including wars in different parts of the world, like Ukraine

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: is energy-based and it's just sitting right there to be solved. That said, to me personally,

body.input: I think it's clear that if AGI were to be achieved, that would change the course of human history.

body.input: So AGI-wise, I was making this decision about what do I want to focus on after VR? And I'm still

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: sized, you build it, power your building off of it. And then the government, I think, will come

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: around to what you need to. Everybody loves an existence proof. I think it's possible somebody

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: less than six key insights that need to be made. Each one of them can probably be written on the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: GPUs at scale and the data that we all have access to, that we can make something that behaves like

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: a human being or like a living creature, and that can then be educated in whatever ways that we need

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: we can formalize and make a loss function for. But there's things we don't know how to do now.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: 55, 60% now, because I do think there's a little sense of acceleration there.

body.input: we will find that clear antecedents of all the critical remaining steps for AGI are already

body.input: I think that's likely the case. One of the things that appeals to so many people, including me,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: about the promise of AGI is we know that we're only drinking from a straw from the fire hose of all

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the information out there. I mean, you look at just in a very narrowly bounded field,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: like machine learning, like you can't read all the papers that come out all the time. You can't go
