metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that happen right now. It's almost funny to see like, oh, Google does something and OpenAI does

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: something, Meta does something, and they're the same people that all talk to each other and they

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: all one-upping each other and they're all capable of implementing each other's work given a month or

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: two after somebody has an announcement of that. But there's a whole world of possible approaches

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to machine learning. And I think that we probably will in hindsight go back and see it's like, yeah,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that was kind of clearly predicted by this early paper here. And this turns out that if you do

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: this and this and take this result from animal training and this thing and this thing and this

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: training and this thing from neuroscience over here and put it together and set up this curriculum

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: for them to learn in, that that's kind of what it took. You don't have too many people now that are

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: still saying it's not possible or it's going to take hundreds of years. And 10 years ago, you would

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: get a collection of experts and you would have a decent chunk on the margin that either say,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: not possible or a couple hundred years, might be centuries. And the median estimate would be like

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: 50, 70 years. And it's been coming down. And I know with me saying eight years for something,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that still puts me on the optimistic side, but it's not crazy out in the fringes. And just being

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: able to look at that at a meta level about the trend of the predictions going down there,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the idea that something could be happening relatively soon. Now, I do not believe in fast

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: takeoffs. That's one of the safety issues that people say it's like, oh, it's going to go,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: boom, and the AI is going to take over the world. There's a lot of reasons. I don't think that's a

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: credible position. And I think that we will go from a point where we start seeing things that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: credibly look like animals behaviors and have a human voice box wired into them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's like, I tried to get Elon to say, it's like, you're a pig at Neuralink. Give it a human voice

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: box and let it start learning human words. I think that animal intelligence is closer to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: human intelligence than a lot of people like to think. And I think that culture and modalities of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: IO make the Gulf seem a lot bigger than it actually is. There's just that smooth spectrum

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of how the brain developed and cortexes and scaling of different things going on there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Culture and modalities of IO. Yes. Language is the sort of loss in translation conceals a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: intelligence. And so when you think about signs of life or AGI, you're thinking about

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: human interpretable signs. So the example I give it, if we get to the point where you've got a

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: learning disabled toddler, some kind of real special needs child that can still interact with

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: their favorite TV show and video game and can be trained and learn in some appreciably human-like

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: way. At that point, you can deploy an army of engineers, cognitive scientists, education,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: developmental education people. And you've got so many advantages there, unlike real education,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where you can do rollbacks and A-B testing and you can find a golden path through a curriculum

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of different things. If you get to that point, learning disabled toddler, I think that it's

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: going to be a done deal. But do you think we'll know when we see it? So there's been a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: really interesting general learning progress from DeepMind, OpenAI a little bit too. I tend to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: believe that Tesla Autopilot deserves a lot more credit than it's getting for making progress on

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: doing the multitask learning thing and increasing the number of tasks and automating that process of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: sort of learning from the edge, discovering the edge cases and learning from the edge cases.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: That is, it's really approaching from a different angle, the general learning problem of AGI. But

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the more clear approach comes from DeepMind, where you have these kind of game situations and

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: build systems there. But I don't know, people seem to be quite...

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There will always be people that just won't believe it and I fundamentally don't care. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I don't care if they don't believe it. When it starts doing people's jobs and I don't care

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: about the philosophical zombie argument at all. Absolutely. But do you think you will notice that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: something special has happened here? Because to me, I've been noticing a lot of special things,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I think a lot of credit should go to DeepMind for AlphaZero. That was truly special.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Self-play mechanisms achieve, solve problems that used to be thought unsolvable, like the game of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Go. Also, I mean, protein folding, starting to get into that space where learning is doing...

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: At first, it wasn't end-to-end learning, now it's end-to-end learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Of a very difficult previously thought unsolvable problem of protein folding.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And so, yeah, where do you think would be a really magical moment for you?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: There have been incredible things happening in recent years. Like you say, all of the things

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: from DeepMind and OpenAI that have been huge showpiece things. But when you really get down

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to it and you read the papers and you look at the way the models are going, it's still like a

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: feed forward. You push something in, something comes out on the end. I mean, maybe there's

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: diffusion models or Monte Carlo tree rollouts and different things going on, but it's not a being.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's not close to a being that's going through a lifelong learning process.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Do you want something that kind of gives you a sense of what's going on?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Do you want something that kind of gives signs of a being? What's the difference between a neural

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: network, a feed forward neural network and a being? Where's the lead?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Fundamentally, the brain is a recurrent neural network generating an action policy. I mean,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: it's implemented on a biological substrate. And it's interesting thinking about things like that,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where we know fundamentally the brain is not a convolutional neural network or a transformer.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Those are specialized things that are very valuable for what we're doing, but it's not

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the way the brain's doing. Now, I do think consciousness and AI in general is a substrate

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: independent mechanism where it doesn't have to be implemented the way the brain is. But if you've

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: only got one existence proof, there's certainly some value in caring about what it says and does.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And so the idea that anything that can be done with a narrow AI that you can quantify up a loss

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: function for a reward mechanism, you're almost certainly going to be able to produce something

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that's more resource effective to train and deploy and use in an inference mode, train a whole lot,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: using an inference. But a living being is going to be something that's a continuous lifelong learned

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: task agnostic thing. So the lifelong learning is really important too. And the long-term memory.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So memory is a big, weird part of that puzzle. And we've got, again, I have all the respect in

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the world for the amazing things that are being done now, but sometimes they can be taken a little

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: bit out of context with things like there's some smoke and mirrors going on, like the GATO,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the recent work, the multitask learning stuff. It's amazing that it's one model that plays all

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the Atari games as well as doing all of these other things. But of course, it didn't learn to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: do all of those. It was instructed in doing that by other reinforcement learners going through and

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: doing that. And even in the case of all the games, it's still going with a specific hand-coded reward

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: function in each of those Atari games, where it's not that, you know, how does it, it just wants to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: spend its summer afternoon playing Atari because that's the most interesting thing for it. So it's

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: again, not a general, it's not learning the way humans learn. And there's, I believe a lot of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: things that are challenging to make a loss function for that you can train through these existing

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: conventional things. We're going to chip away at all the things that people do that we can turn into

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: narrow AI problems and billions of, probably trillions of dollars of value are going to be

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: created by that. But there's still going to be a set of things. And we've got questionable cases

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: like the self-driving car where it's possible, it's not my bet, but it's plausible that the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: long tail could be problematic enough that that really does require a full-on artificial general

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: intelligence. The counter argument is that data solves almost everything. Everything is an

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: interpolation problem if you have enough data and Tesla may be able to get enough data from all of

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: their deployed stuff to be able to work like that, but maybe not. And there are all the other problems

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: about like, say you want to have a strategy meeting and you want to go ahead and bring in all of your

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: remote workers and your consultants and you want a world where some of those could be AIs that are

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: talking and interacting with you in an area that is too murky to have a crisp loss function,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: but they still have things that on some level they're rewarded on some internal level for

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: building a valuable to humans kind of life and ability to interact with things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Listen, see, I still think that self-driving cars solving that problem will take us very

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: far towards AGI. You might not need AGI, but I am really inspired by what Autopilot is doing.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Waymo, so some of the other companies, I think Waymo leads the way there is also really

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: interesting, but they don't have quite as ambitious of an effort in terms of learning based

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: sort of data hungry approach to driving, which I think is very close to the kind of thing that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: would take us far towards AGI. Yeah. And it's a funny thing because as far as I can tell, Elon

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: is completely serious about all of his concerns about AGI, being an existential threat. And

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I tried to draw him out to talk about AI and he just didn't want to. And I think that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I get that little fatalistic sense from him. It's weird because his company could very well

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: be the leading company leading towards a lot of that, where Tesla being a super pragmatic company

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that's doing things because they really want to solve this actual problem. It's a different vibe

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: than the research oriented companies where it's a great time to be an AI researcher. You've got your

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: pick of trillion dollar companies that will pay you to kind of work on the problems you're interested

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: in, but that's not necessarily driving hard towards the core problem of AGI as something

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that's going to produce a lot of value by doing things that people currently do or would like to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean, I have a million questions to you about your ideas about AGI, but do you think

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: it needs to be embodied? Do you think it needs to have a body to start to notice the signs of life

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and to develop the kind of system that's able to reason, perceive the world in the way that an

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: AGI should and act in the world? Should we be thinking about robots or can this be achieved in

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: a purely digital system? I have a clear opinion on that and that's that no, it does not need to be

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: embodied in the physical world where you could say most of my career is about making simulated

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: virtual worlds in games or virtual reality. On a fundamental level, I believe that you can make a

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: simulated environment that provides much of the value of what the real environment does and

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: restricting yourself to operating at real time in the physical world with physical objects,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I think is an enormous handicap. I mean, that's one of the real lessons driven home by all my

body.input: an evolutionary space there, when you do have free markets and you have entrepreneurs, you are going

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And the little bits of stochasticity that are sitting on in this as it cycles between different

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I don't think there's anything deeply magical about it, certainly not symbolic. I think it is

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And I think so much of that is like, it depends on what you happen to have in your field of view as

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So that's kind of the quality of the subjective experience of it is not,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: is not essential for intelligence. I don't think so. I don't think there's anything really important there.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: What about some other human qualities like fear of mortality and stuff like that? Like the fact

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that this ride ends, is that, is that important? Like you, you know, we've talked so much about

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: this conversation about the value of deadlines and constraints. Do you think that's important

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: for intelligence? That's actually a super interesting angle that I don't usually take on that about has

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: death being a deadline that forces you to make better decisions. Because I have heard people

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: talk about how if you have immortality, people are going to stop, stop trying and working on things

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: because they've got all the time in the world. But I would say that I don't expect it to be

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: a super critical thing that, that a sense of mortality and death impending death is necessary

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: there because those are things that they do wind up providing reward signals to us. And we will be

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: in control of the reward signals and there, there will have to be something fundamental that causes,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that engenders curiosity and goal setting and all of that. Something is going to play in there at the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: reward level. I am, you know, whether it's positive or negative or both,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I don't have any strong opinions on exactly what it's going to be. But that's that type of thing

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where I doubt that might be one of those half dozen key things that has to be sorted out on exactly

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: what the master reward, that's the meta reward overall of the, the local task specific rewards

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: have to be. That could be that big negative reward of death, maybe not death, but ability to walk away

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: from an interaction. So it bothers me when people treat AI systems like servants. So it doesn't

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: bother me, but I mean, it, it's, it really is drawing the line between what an AI system could

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: be. It's limiting the possibility of what an AI system could be. It's treating them as justice tools.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Now that's of course, from a narrow AI perspective, there's so many problems that narrow AI could solve,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: just like you said, as in, in its form of a tool, but it could also be a being, which is much more

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: than a tool. And to be, to become a being, you have to respect that thing for being a being.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: And for that, it has to be able to have, to make its own decisions, to walk away, to say, I had enough

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of you, I would like to break up with you now. You've not treated me well, and I would like to move on.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I think that actually, that choice to end things.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: So I, I have a couple of things on that. So on the one hand, it is kind of disturbing when you see

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: people being like people that are mean to robots and, you know, mean to Alexa, whatever. And that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: seems to speak badly about humanity. But there's also the exact opposite side of that, where you

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: have so many people that imbue humanity in inanimate objects or things that are toys or that are,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: are relatively limited. So I think there may even be more, more danger about people putting more

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: emotional investment into a lot of these proto AIs in different ways.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah. And then the AI would manipulate that. But, you know, as far as like the AI

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: ethnic sides of things, I really stay away from any of those discussions or even really thinking

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: about it. It's similar with the safety things where I think it's just premature. And there's a certain

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: class of people that enjoy thinking about impractical things, things that are not in the world and,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: you know, of pragmatic effect around you. And I think that begin, again, because I don't think

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: there's going to be a fast takeoff. I think we actually will have time to have these debates

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: when we know the shape of what we're debating. And some people do take a principled approach

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that they think it's going to go too fast, that you really do need to get ahead of it, that you

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: need to be thinking about this because we have slow processes of coming to any kind of consensus

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: or even coming up with ideas about this. And maybe that's true. I wouldn't put any of my money or

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: funding into something like that because I don't think it's a problem yet. And I think that we will

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: have these signs of life when we've got our learning disabled toddler, we should really start

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: talking about some of the safety and ethics issues, but probably not before then.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Can you elaborate briefly about why you don't think there'll be a fast takeoff? Is there some

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: deep intuition you have about it? Is it because it's grounded in the physical world or why?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yeah. So it is my belief that we're going to start off with something that requires thousands

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of GPUs. And I don't know if you've tried to go get a thousand GPU instance on a cloud anytime

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: recently, but these are not things that you can just go spin up hundreds of. There are real

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: challenges to, I mean, these things are going to take data centers and data centers take years to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: build. And the last few years we've seen a few of them kind of coming up, going in different places.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: They're big engineering efforts. You can hear people bemoan about the fact that I know, oh,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the network was wired all wrong and it took them a month to go unwire it and rewire it the right

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: way. These aren't things that you can just magic into existence. And the ideas of, like the old

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: tropes about it's going to escape onto the internet and take over other systems, the fast takeoff

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: ones are clearly nonsense because you just can't open TCP connections above a certain rate, no

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: matter how smart you are, even if you have perfect hacking ability, that take over the world in an

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: instant sort of thing just isn't plausible at all. And even if you had access to all of the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: resources, these are going to be specialized systems where you're going to wind up with

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: something that is architected around exactly this chip with this interconnect. And it's not just

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: going to be able to be plopped somewhere else. Now, interestingly, it is going to be something

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that the entire code for all of it will easily fit on a thumb drive. That's total spy movie,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: thriller sorts of things where you could have, hey, we cracked the secret AGI and it fits on this

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: thumb drive and anyone could steal it. Now they're still going to have to build the right data center

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to deploy it and have the right kind of life experience curriculum to take it up to the point

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where it's valuable. But the real core of it, the magic that's going to happen there is going to be

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: very small. It's again, tens of thousands of lines of code, not millions of lines of code.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It is possible to imagine a world, as you mentioned this spy thriller view, if it's just a few lines

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: of code, we can imagine a world where the surface of computation is growing, maybe growing

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: exponentially, meaning the refrigerators start getting a GPU. First of all, the smartphones,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the billions of smartphones, but maybe if there become highways through which code can spread

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: across the entirety of the computation surface, then you don't any longer have to book AWS GPUs.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But there are real fundamental issues there. When you start getting down to taking an actual

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: problem and putting it on an abstract machine like that, that has not worked out well in practice.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: It's always been easy to come up with ways to compute faster, say more flops or more giga ops

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: or whatever there. That's usually the easy part, but you then have interconnect and then memory

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: for what goes into it. When you talk about saying, well, cell phones, well, you're limited to like a

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: 5G connection or something on that. If you take your calculation and you factor it across

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: a million cell phones instead of a thousand GPUs in a warehouse, you might be able to have some

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: kind of a substrate like that, but it could be operating then at one one thousandth the speed.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: Yes, you could have an AGI working there, but it wouldn't be a real time AGI. It would be

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: something that is operating at really a snail's pace, much, much slower than kind of human level

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: thought for things. I'm not worried about that problem. You're transferring the problem into the

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: interconnect, the communication, the shared memory, the collective intelligence aspect of it, which is

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: extremely difficult as well. I mean, it's back to the very earliest days of supercomputers. You still

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: have the balance between bandwidth storage and computation. And sometimes they're easier to get

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: one or the other, but it's been remarkably constant across all those years that you still need all

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: three. What do your efforts now, you mentioned to me that you're really committing to AI at this

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: stage. What do you see your life in the next few months, years look like? What do you hope to achieve

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: here? So I literally just this week signed a term sheet to take some investment money for my company,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where the last two years I had backed off from Meta and I was still doing my consulting CTO role

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: there, but I had styled it as I was going to take the Victorian gentleman scientist route,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: where I was going to be the wealthy person that was going to go pursue science and learn about

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: this and do experiments. And honestly, I'm surprised there aren't more people like that,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that are like me, technical people that made a bunch of money and are interested in some of these

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: possibly the biggest leverage point in human history. I mean, I know of, I've heard of a couple

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: organizations that are basically led by one rich techie guy that gets a few people around him to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: try to work on this, but I'm surprised that there's not more, that there aren't like a dozen of them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I mean, maybe people are still think that it's an unapproachable problem, that it's kind of beyond

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: their ability to get a wrench on and have some effect on like whatever startups they've run before.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But that was my kind of like with all the stuff I've learned, whether it's gaming, aerospace,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: whatever, I go through a larval phase where I'm like, okay, I'm sucking up all of this information,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: trying to see, is this something that I can actually do? Is this something that's practical

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to devote a large chunk of my life to? And I've gone through that with the AI, machine learning

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: space of things. And I think I've got my arms around it. I've got the measure of it where

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: some of the most brilliant people in the world are working on this problem, but nobody knows

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: exactly the path that it's going on. We're throwing a lot of things at the wall and seeing what sticks.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But I have another interesting thing, just learning about all of this, the contingency of your path to

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: knowledge and talking about the associations and the context that you have with them, where people

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: that learn in the same path will have similar thought processes. And I think it's useful that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: I come at this from a different background, a different history than the people that have had

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: the largely academic backgrounds for this, where I have huge blind spots that they could easily

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: point out, but I have a different set of experiences in history and approaches to problems in systems

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: engineering that might turn out to be useful. And I can afford to take that bet where I'm not going

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: to be destitute. I have enough money to fund myself working on this for the rest of my life.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: But what I was finding is that I was still not committing, where I had a foot firmly in the VR

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: and meta side of things, where in theory I've got a very nice position there. I only have to work

metadata.title: Podcast: John Carmack: Doom, Quake, VR, AGI, Programming, Video Games, and Rockets | Lex Fridman Podcast #309

body.input: one day a week for my consulting role, but I was engaging every day. I'd still be like, my computer's

body.input: even if sometimes we make up a story.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: And that knowledge is also necessary for machines

body.input: to take good decisions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: And that knowledge is hard to codify in expert systems,

body.input: rule-based systems, and classical AI formalism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: And there are other issues, of course, with the old AI,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: like not really good ways of handling uncertainty,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: I would say something more subtle,

body.input: which we understand better now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: but I think still isn't enough in the minds of people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: There's something really powerful

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: that comes from distributed representations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: the thing that really makes neural nets work so well.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: And it's hard to replicate that kind of power

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: in a symbolic world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: The knowledge in expert systems and so on

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: is nicely decomposed into a bunch of rules.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: Whereas if you think about a neural net, it's the opposite.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: You have this big blob of parameters

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: which work intensely together

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: to represent everything the network knows.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: And it's not sufficiently factorized.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: And so I think this is one of the weaknesses

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: of current neural nets,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: that we have to take lessons from classical AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: in order to bring in another kind of compositionality,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: which is common in language, for example, and in these rules,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: but that isn't so native to neural nets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: And on that line of thinking, disentangled representations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: Yes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: So let me connect with disentangled representations,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: if you don't mind. Yes, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: So for many years, I've thought, and I still believe,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: that it's really important that we come up

body.input: but, or reinforcement, whatever,

body.input: that build representations in which the important factors,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: hopefully causal factors, are nicely separated

body.input: and easy to pick up from the representation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: So that's the idea of disentangled representations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: We can maybe just learn with linear models

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: about the things we care about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: And I still think this is important,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: but I think this is missing out

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: on a very important ingredient,

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: which classical AI systems can remind us of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

body.input: So let's say we have these disentangled representations.

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4

metadata.title: Podcast: Yoshua Bengio: Deep Learning | Lex Fridman Podcast #4
