metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So actually, I released a couple of new data sets recently.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: One is called ImageNet, the French ImageNet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: which is a small subset of ImageNet, which is designed

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: to be easy to classify.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: What's how do you spell ImageNet?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: It's got an extra T and E at the end, because it's very French.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Image, OK.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And then another one called ImageWolf,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: which is a subset of ImageNet that only contains dog breeds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And that's a hard one, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: That's a hard one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And I've discovered that if you just look at these two subsets,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: you can train things on a single GPU in 10 minutes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And the results you get are directly transferable to ImageNet

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: nearly all the time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And so now I'm starting to see some researchers

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: start to use these much smaller data sets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I so deeply love the way you think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: because I think you might have written a blog post saying

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: that sort of going to these big data sets

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: is encouraging people to not think creatively.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So it sort of constrains you to train on large resources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And because you have these resources,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: you think more research will be better.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And then you start.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So somehow you kill the creativity.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Yeah, and even worse than that, Lex,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I keep hearing from people who say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I decided not to get into deep learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: because I don't believe it's accessible to people outside

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: of Google to do useful work.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So I see a lot of people make an explicit decision

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: to not learn this incredibly valuable tool,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: because they've drunk the Google Kool-Aid, which

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: is that only Google's big enough and smart enough to do it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And I just find that so disappointing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: and it's so wrong.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And I think all the major breakthroughs in AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: in the next 20 years will be doable on a single GPU.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I would say my sense is all the big sort of even.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Well, let's put it this way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: None of the big breakthroughs of the last 20 years

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: required multiple GPUs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So like BatchNorm, Rally-U, Dropout, Cognizant in general.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Every one of them, none of them has required multiple GPUs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: The original GANs didn't require multiple GPUs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Well, and we've actually recently shown

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: that you don't even need GANs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So we've developed GAN-level outcomes without needing GANs.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And we can now do it with, again,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: by using transfer learning, we can do it

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: in a couple of hours on a single GPU.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Just using a generator model without the adversarial part?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So we've found loss functions that work super well

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: without the adversarial part.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And then one of our students, a guy called Jason Antich,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: has created a system called De-Altify,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: which uses this technique to colorize

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: all black and white movies.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: You can do it on a single GPU, colorize a whole movie

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: in a couple of hours.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And one of the things that Jason and I did together

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: was we figured out how to add a little bit of GAN

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: at the very end, which it turns out for colorization

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: makes it just a bit brighter and nicer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And then Jason did masses of experiments

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: to figure out exactly how much to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: But it's still all done on his home machine,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: on a single GPU in his lounge room.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And if you think about colorizing Hollywood movies,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: that sounds like something a huge studio would have to do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: But he has the world's best results on this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: There's this problem of microphones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: We're just talking to microphones now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: It's such a pain in the ass to have these microphones

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: to get good quality audio.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And I tried to see if it's possible to plop down

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: a bunch of cheap sensors and reconstruct higher quality

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: audio from multiple sources.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Because right now I haven't seen work from,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: okay, we can save inexpensive mics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: automatically combining audio from multiple sources

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: to improve the combined audio.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: People haven't done that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And that feels like a learning problem.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So hopefully somebody can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Well, I mean, it's eminently doable

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: and it should have been done by now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I felt the same way about computational photography

body.input: four years ago.

body.input: That's right.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: of intentional movement, so like take a few frames,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: gives you enough information to get excellent subpixel

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: resolution, which particularly with deep learning,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: you would know exactly what you meant to be looking at.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: We can totally do the same thing with audio.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I think it's a madness that hasn't been done yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Is there been progress on photography companies?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Yeah, photography is basically a standard now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So the Google Pixel Night Light,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I don't know if you've ever tried it,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: but it's astonishing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: and you get back a very high quality image.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Yeah, basically everybody now is doing most

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And also increasingly people are putting more than one lens

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So the same will happen for audio for sure.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And there's applications in the audio side.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: If you look at an Alexa type device,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: most people I've seen,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: especially I worked at Google before,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: when you look at noise background removal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: But I mean, you can still do it even with one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Like again, it's not much work's been done in this area.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: but it would be a couple of months work.

body.input: Okay, also learning rate in terms of Dawnbench.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: There's some magic on learning rate

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: that you played around with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: That's kind of interesting.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Yeah, so this is all work that came

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: from a guy called Leslie Smith.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Leslie's a researcher who like us cares a lot about

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: just the practicalities of training

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: neural networks quickly and accurately,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: which you would think is what everybody should care about,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: but almost nobody does.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And he discovered something very interesting,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: which he calls super convergence,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: which is there are certain networks

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: that with certain settings of high parameters

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: could suddenly be trained 10 times faster

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: by using a 10 times higher learning rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Now, no one published that paper

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: because it's not an area of kind of active research

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: in the academic world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: No academics recognize this is important.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And also deep learning in academia

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: is not considered a experimental science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So unlike in physics where you could say like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I just saw a subatomic particle do something

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: which the theory doesn't explain.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: You could publish that without an explanation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And then the next 60 years,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: people can try to work out how to explain it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: We don't allow this in the deep learning world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So it's literally impossible for Leslie to publish a paper

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: that says, I've just seen something amazing happen.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: This thing trained 10 times faster than it should have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I don't know why.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And so the reviewers were like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: we can't publish that because you don't know why.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So anyway.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: That's important to pause on

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: because there's so many discoveries

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: that would need to start like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Every other scientific field I know of works that way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I don't know why ours is uniquely disinterested

body.input: So space repetition is an idea created by a psychologist named Ebbinghaus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: I don't know, must be a couple of hundred years ago or something, 150 years ago.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: He did something which sounds pretty damn tedious.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: He wrote down random sequences of letters on cards and tested how well he would remember those random sequences a day later, a week later, whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: He discovered that there was this kind of curve where his probability of remembering one of them would be dramatically smaller the next day and then a little bit smaller the next day, a little bit smaller the next day.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: What he discovered is that if he revised those cards after a day, the probabilities would decrease at a smaller rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And then if you revise them again a week later, they would decrease at a smaller rate again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And so he basically figured out a roughly optimal equation for when you should revise something you want to remember.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So space repetition learning is using this simple algorithm, which is something like revise something after a day and then three days and then a week and then three weeks and so forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And so if you use a program like Anki, as you know, it will just do that for you.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And if you, and it will say, did you remember this?

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: And if you say no, it will reschedule it back to be appear again like 10 times faster than it otherwise would have.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: It's a kind of a way of being guaranteed to learn something because by definition, if you're not learning it, it will be rescheduled to be revised more quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: Unfortunately, though, it's also like it doesn't let you fool yourself if you're not learning something you know, like your revisions will just get more and more.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So you have to find ways to learn things productively and effectively like treat your brain well. So using like mnemonics and stories and context and stuff like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jeremy Howard: fast.ai Deep Learning Courses and Research | Lex Fridman Podcast #35

body.input: So, yeah, it's a super great technique. It's like learning how to learn is something which everybody should learn before they actually learn anything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: The question is, Lex, I'm a young man that has battled with depression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Do you think when trying to develop a human like AI,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: we will reach a stumbling point where the AI themselves

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: suffer from depression and other complex mental issues?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Do you think it will be a simple fix, like rewriting a piece of code

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: or a new patch or update?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Or maybe when trying to create something human like with high fidelity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: you need to leave in the possibility of the AI suffering

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: from such complex mental issues that a human can.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: What are your thoughts generally and philosophically about AI

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: suffering from depression?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think that suffering is a deep, fundamental property of consciousness.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I would like to probably say quite a bit about depression.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I have friends who suffer from depression, but that's for another time.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: That's for when we talk about depression in humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think depression is just one flavor of suffering

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that is part of the human condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I see it as a kind of dark side street

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: on the path to intelligence.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So in terms of robot suffering,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: if we are to create systems that are truly intelligent

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: in the way that they're able to interact in intelligent

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: and deeply meaningful ways with other humans,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: it's going to have many of the properties, many of the characteristics

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: of the human condition of the full human experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think depression is part of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: There's, of course, a part in us humans that longs to remove

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: all that is cruel in this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: You know, that's why people that believe in God, often the biggest question is

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: of why does God allow there to be suffering in the world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: There's this longing to understand why is there so much unfairness in this world?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And so building on that, there's an inclination to then in our systems,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: engineer something that is void of those things

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that we can understand why that's part of the human condition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: But I think it is intricately part of the experience that is to be human.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And I think if we were to build intelligence systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that are interacting with humans, there has to be in some ways

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: properties of consciousness baked in.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And if we were to have properties of consciousness baked in,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: we have to have the full mystery and uncertainty of the human experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: which, yes, includes all the different flavors of suffering

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: of which depression is part.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think the yang and the yang in all of its versions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: the ups and downs of moods, but also the more sort of rational,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: intellectual interpretations of different concepts

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that are less sort of dramatic all have to oscillate back and forth.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think that's where the interesting aspect of interactions happens.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Just like when I have conversations in the podcast,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: the interesting stuff happens when there's disagreements,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: when there's a bit of turmoil, when there's a push and pull,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: when there's a changing of minds or even just a morphing of your own opinions

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: about something, your own thoughts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think that's part of it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So I really do think all of that mess

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: of humanity has to be engineered in into AI systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that are interacting with humans and are trying to create

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: meaningful interactions with those humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: There's, of course, a huge amount of AI systems

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that are going to be more intelligent than humans at particular tasks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Those do not need to have those properties of the human experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: like suffering and all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: But for the ones that move among us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think, unfortunately, depression has to be part of that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: It has to be part of the experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So the possibility of depression has to be part of the experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Of course, I tend to focus on the positive aspects of the human experience,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: like love, beauty, joy, all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: But it's the yin and the yang.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: They go together.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: They're lifelong partners, unfortunately, I think.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Now, of course, all of this is just hypothesis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And most of my answers to all of these questions

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: are just my own thoughts.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: But I am thinking about all of this from an engineering perspective.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And maybe I'll have more to say in the future

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: about how we actually build these kinds of things

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: into our AI systems that interact with humans.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Thanks for the great question.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: It's a tough one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Question is, Lex, I was wondering if you would be willing

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: to talk about your immigrant experience.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I myself started off as an international student

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: studying and working in America, not from Russia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I'm from India.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: But there was a constant push and pull that I experienced

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: given my life circumstance.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I would be curious to hear how you were simulated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Do you feel like you belong, etc.?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Thank you for the AMA.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Your statements about do you feel like you belong hit hard for some reason?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Maybe it's because late at night, maybe because I'm a bit over caffeinated.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think what pops to mind to focus on is the aspect of loneliness,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: the aspect of belonging.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think a lot of us in the early teenage years

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: go through that process of feeling like an outsider,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: an outcast of different kinds.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think it hit me the hardest personally

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: because I was a popular kid in Russia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And when we moved here, I went to the opposite of being popular.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Or feeling like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I felt like an outcast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: The place I moved to in America had more of an emphasis.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Maybe it's a cultural thing of emphasizing material possessions

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: over two things that were deeply meaningful to me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: which is human connection, like friendship,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: and also knowledge, like mathematics and scientific discovery,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: all those kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: It's just the emphasis of what was valued was different.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And that for me was a catalyst to feel like a total outcast

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: as opposed to being this person who looks out into the world

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: and enjoys the beauty of the world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I kind of went into this brooding phase of,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: first of all, learning the English language,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: but starting to read books, more philosophical books.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: The first one I remember reading in English was The Giver

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that sort of helped me start thinking about this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I was so fortunate to be so in love with people for so long

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: and have close friends in Russia

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that I didn't notice in my childhood

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: how deeply alone we all are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So for me, the immigrant experience involved in a small way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: at least the first, realizing that hard human truth

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: is that we all are born alone, live alone, die alone.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Even when we're in the arms of somebody we love,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: we're still somehow fundamentally alone

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: with our thoughts, with our hopes, with our fears,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: trapped in this conscious meat vessel between our ears.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think the immigrant experience for me was the catalyst

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: to realizing and being terrified and also liberated

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: by the idea that I'm alone in this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And at the same time was the realization

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that this beautiful feeling I felt from the connection

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: to other humans was this gift

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that took me away from this dark realization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So it's almost that love is a kind of escape

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: from the reality of life, from the muck of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And so the journey began in that way

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: to think about this world in this way,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: both the burden of being alone coupled with a frequent escape

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: from that feeling by being lost in the company of friends,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: loved ones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Early on, coupled with this love of the human mind

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: and curiosity about the human mind

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: was the love of programming and actually building

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: little programs and engineering systems, of course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: building robots and college and so on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think the gift of the immigrant experience

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: of feeling like the outcast was the love of experiencing

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: the deep connection with others, like a deep appreciation

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: of it when it's there.

body.input: Question is, what was your decision behind going on the keto diet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So the decision or rather process of discovering the diets that work for me has to do

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: with the fact that I wrestled the combat sports my whole life that has weight classes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So you're constantly figuring out how to perform optimally physically and mentally

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: while going to school and so on while also cutting weight.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So grounded in that, I've developed a fascination with different diets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I've never thought about diet as a prescriptive thing for others.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I've always thought of myself as a kind of a nutritional scientist running a study of N of one.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So just studying myself and not trying to extrapolate to others,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: just understanding what makes me happy, what makes me perform the best.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And that's where that journey took.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I've tried everything.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think about 15 or more years ago,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I discovered the power of intermittent fasting or fasting in general,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: and I can talk about that forever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I used to do a lot of weightlifting, sort of power lifting, all that kind of stuff.

body.input: And in the world of like men's health or rather men's muscle and fitness kind of

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: where you eat six, seven times a day, small meals, chicken and broccoli, all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: In that kind of world, to realize that you can eat once a day

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: and still train two, three times that day and actually have more energy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: more focus and perform better than you ever have was mind blowing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So I think fasting was the biggest like paradigm shift for me

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: because it made me realize that I really need to study myself better,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: try new things all the time to allow myself the opportunity to discover

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: something that's totally transformative on my life, makes my life easier,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: makes my body, my mind work better, all that kind of stuff.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: that are extremely low carb that could allow you to perform well physically and mentally,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: What was the darkest time in your life and what did your road to recovery look like?

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: In general, I love life, so it's difficult for me to talk about these kinds of things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: But let me briefly say that I think the darkest times have been when I've put my faith in people,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: when I opened my heart to them, and they turned out not to be the best versions of themselves

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: or maybe the kind of amazing people that I'd hoped I thought they might be.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So my heart has been broken in small ways in my life, as I'm sure it has been for many people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: But the fire of hope still burns bright, perhaps even brighter.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: You mentioned road to recovery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think the people I mentioned, I focus on the positive moments, and there always are.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And just have gratitude for those and just don't linger on the negative.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I just remember the good times.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: That's how I recover.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: That's how I keep my optimism.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And that's how I keep my heart open for future amazing people to take the risk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: And I'm sure my heart will be broken again.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Perhaps many times in the future, but I think it's always worth the risk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I wrote this down, the Marcus Aurelius quote,

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Love the people with whom fate brings you together and do so with all of your heart.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I think that's all we can do.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: I hope some of these answers were at least somewhat interesting or useful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: If so, I'll try to do it again in the future.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: It is currently 421.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: When I started saying that sentence, it was 420 a.m.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: A good time to end as any, perhaps the best.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Good night. I love you all.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Thanks for listening to this AMA episode.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: So the choice is sleep, employment, privacy or muscle recovery.

metadata.title: Podcast: Lex Fridman: Ask Me Anything - AMA January 2021 | Lex Fridman Podcast

body.input: Choose wisely, my friends.

body.input: let me leave you with some words from Winston Churchill.

body.input: What difference between biological neural networks

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: and artificial neural networks

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: is most captivating and profound to you?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: At the higher philosophical level,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: let's not get technical just yet.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: One of the things that very much intrigues me

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: is the fact that neurons have all kinds of components,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: properties to them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: And evolutionary biology, if you have some little quirk

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: in how a molecule works or how a cell works,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: and it can be made use of,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: evolution will sharpen it up

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: and make it into a useful feature rather than a glitch.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: And so you expect in neurobiology

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: for evolution to have captured all kinds of possibilities

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: of getting neurons, of how you get neurons

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: to do things for you.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: And that aspect has been completely suppressed

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: in artificial neural networks.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: Do the glitches become features

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: in the biological neural network?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: They can.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: Look, let me take one of the things

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: that I used to do research on.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: If you take things which oscillate,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: they have rhythms which are sort of close to each other.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: Under some circumstances,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: these things will have a phase transition

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: and suddenly the rhythm will,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: everybody will fall into step.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: There was a marvelous physical example of that

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: in the Millennium Bridge across the Thames River

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: about, built about 2001.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: And pedestrians walking across,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: pedestrians don't walk, synchronize,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: they don't walk in lockstep.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: But they're all walking about the same frequency.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: And the bridge could sway at that frequency

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: and the slight sway made pedestrians tend a little bit

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: to lock into step and after a while,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: the bridge was oscillating back and forth

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: and the pedestrians were walking in step to it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: You could see it in the movies made out of the bridge.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: And the engineers made a simple-minded mistake.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: They had assumed when you walk,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: it's step, step, step, and it's back and forth motion.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: But when you walk, it's also right foot, left foot,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: side to side motion.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: And the side to side motion

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: for which the bridge was strong enough,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: but it wasn't stiff enough.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: And as a result, you would feel the motion

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: and you'd fall into step with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: And people were very uncomfortable with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: They closed the bridge for two years

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: while they built stiffening for it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: Now, nerves, look, nerve cells produce action potentials.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: You have a bunch of cells

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: which are loosely coupled together,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: producing action potentials at the same rate.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: There'll be some circumstances

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: under which these things can lock together.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: Other circumstances in which they won't.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: Well, they fire together,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: you can be sure that other cells are gonna notice it.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: So you can make a computational feature out of this

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: in an evolving brain.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: Most artificial neural networks

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: don't even have action potentials,

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: let alone have the possibility for synchronizing them.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: And you mentioned the evolutionary process.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: So the evolutionary process

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: that builds on top of biological systems

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: leverages the weird mess of it somehow.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: So how do you make sense of that ability

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: to leverage all the different kinds of complexities

body.input: in the biological brain?

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: You could duplicate that piece of DNA

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: and now one part of it can encode for that protein,

body.input: but the other one could itself change a little bit

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: and thus start coding for a molecule

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: which is slightly different.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: Now, that molecule was just slightly different.

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76

body.input: Had a function which helped any old chemical reaction

metadata.title: Podcast: John Hopfield: Physics View of the Mind and Neurobiology | Lex Fridman Podcast #76
